title: pan-2286: Implement issue
description:
## Symptom

Every watchdog-triggered dashboard restart on 2026-07-03 (~12 attempts, 06:57Z–09:26Z) failed with `pan restart --dashboard exited 1` after a consistent ~16–18s, ending twice in `WATCHDOG GIVING UP — manual intervention required`. The self-healing path has likely **never succeeded** on a loaded machine:

```
[2026-07-03T06:57:31.080Z] watchdog spawned pan restart --dashboard (pid 3613204)
[2026-07-03T06:57:49.725Z] watchdog restart failed: pan restart --dashboard exited 1
[2026-07-03T07:04:50.101Z] watchdog spawned pan restart --dashboard (pid 3740027)
[2026-07-03T07:05:06.746Z] watchdog restart failed: pan restart --dashboard exited 1
[2026-07-03T07:07:00.827Z] WATCHDOG GIVING UP — manual intervention required: The operation was aborted due to timeout
...
[2026-07-03T09:26:53.456Z] WATCHDOG GIVING UP — manual intervention required: fetch failed
```

## Root cause (verified in source)

1. **The health wait defaults to 15 seconds, and the watchdog never overrides it.**
   - `src/supervisor/server.ts:99` spawns `pan restart --dashboard` with no `--health-timeout` flag.
   - `src/cli/commands/restart.ts:178-180` leaves `healthTimeoutMs` `undefined` when the flag is absent.
   - `src/lib/platform-lifecycle.ts:210`: `const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? 15_000;`
2. **Dashboard boot-to-listen alone takes 15–92s**, so the 15s health window expires before even a healthy boot can start listening. Boot-timing lines from dashboard.log this morning: `+17312ms`, `+15174ms`, `+91780ms`, `+15444ms` (all "HTTP server listening" — health passes only after that). The restart is therefore **structurally guaranteed to exit 1** under exactly the starved conditions that trigger the watchdog in the first place. The operator SOP already says restarts need `--health-timeout` ≥ 120s; the watchdog violates it.
3. **The failure reason is invisible**: `src/supervisor/server.ts:101` spawns the child with `stdio: 'ignore'`, so the child's stderr (`✗ [health] health check at ... did not pass within 15000ms`) is discarded. The supervisor log only ever shows the bare exit code.

A secondary confusion multiplier: the exit-1 happens AFTER the child has already SIGTERM'd and respawned the dashboard, so the dashboard often does come back seconds later — while the watchdog has already recorded a failed attempt toward its give-up budget (`maxRestarts`), and (pre-PAN-2219-fix conditions) keeps burning attempts until `gaveUp`.

## Fix

1. In `src/supervisor/server.ts` `spawnRestart()`, pass an explicit generous health timeout (e.g. `--health-timeout 120000`), or thread `watchdogConfig` through so it is configurable.
2. Capture the child's stdout/stderr (pipe to the supervisor `log()` on failure) instead of `stdio: 'ignore'` so the next failure is diagnosable from supervisor.log alone.
3. Test: unit test that the spawned argv includes the health-timeout flag, plus a watchdog test where restart succeeds when boot takes 60s (fake timers per repo rule).

## Relations

- Concrete mechanism behind part of #2253 (no recovery guardian / silent outage — the guardian exists but its remedy cannot succeed).
- Amplifies #1711 (event-loop stalls trigger the watchdog; the doomed restarts then add churn on an already-starved box).
- Evidence from the 2026-07-03 morning incident; starvation driver that morning was the PAN-2148 workspace container crash-loop/rebuild churn (see #1740).
- AC: - src/supervisor/server.ts:99 spawns pan restart --dashboard with no --health-timeout flag.
- AC: - src/cli/commands/restart.ts:178-180 leaves healthTimeoutMs undefined when the flag is absent.
- AC: - src/lib/platform-lifecycle.ts:210: const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? 15_000;
- AC: Concrete mechanism behind part of #2253 (no recovery guardian / silent outage — the guardian exists but its remedy cannot succeed).
- AC: Amplifies #1711 (event-loop stalls trigger the watchdog; the doomed restarts then add churn on an already-starved box).
- AC: Evidence from the 2026-07-03 morning incident; starvation driver that morning was the PAN-2148 workspace container crash-loop/rebuild churn (see #1740).
close_reason: Implemented watchdog restart health timeout and failure output logging with focused supervisor tests

title: pan-399: Run the ordered release with health/version/smoke checks, stop-on-failure, and rollback
description:
Create src/lib/release/release-engine.ts exporting runRelease(issueId, projectPath). It: reads the merged MergeSet via getMergeSetSync(issueId) as the trigger input; loads the project release config; calls resolveReleasePlan; builds+persists a ReleaseSet; sets issue releaseStatus='releasing'. For each component in order: trigger:'manual' -> mark component 'blocked' (awaiting manual deploy), continue without failing the release; trigger:'auto' -> poll health_url until a healthy response or a bounded timeout, then run version_check then smoke_test when configured. On any stage failure: mark the component 'failed', HALT all remaining components, run rollback (async) if configured (component -> 'rolled_back'), and set issue releaseStatus to 'rolled_back' if any rollback ran else 'failed'; if some required components passed and a later one failed, use 'partial' per spec. All shell runs via async exec/spawn with explicit timeouts (NEVER execSync). Persist per-component state transitions through the release-set model. On all-pass, set releaseStatus='passed'. Injectable clock/exec seam so tests use fake timers.
- AC: Given all components healthy and smoke_test exit 0, runRelease sets each component 'passed' and issue releaseStatus 'passed'
- AC: When an earlier component passes and a later component's smoke_test fails, runRelease halts remaining components and sets issue releaseStatus to 'failed' or 'partial' (never 'passed')
- AC: When a component fails and has a rollback command, runRelease executes it, marks that component 'rolled_back', and sets issue releaseStatus 'rolled_back'
- AC: All health/version/smoke/rollback execution goes through async exec/spawn with a timeout; the module contains no execSync call
close_reason: Implemented coordinated release engine with release-set persistence, ordered health/version/smoke execution, stop-on-failure, rollback handling, focused tests passing, and deep inspection passed.

title: pan-1739: SessionNode: honor presence==='ended' so a dead session never renders as working/running with a growing timer
description:
Make presence the authoritative liveness signal in src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/CommandDeck/ProjectTree/SessionNode.tsx. Leave the existing `if (runtime.activity === 'stopped' && presence !== 'ended') return 'idle';` branch intact for live sessions (H2). (2) In the render body, gate isLiveActivity (:664) on isLive (:610, already `presence in {active,idle,suspended}`): change to `const isLiveActivity = isLive && !isPaused && (statusCssKey === 'running' || statusCssKey === 'working' || statusCssKey === 'thinking' || statusCssKey === 'starting');` so a stale backend status==='running' on a dead node cannot paint the icon with styles.sessionIconRunning. (3) Suppress the growing duration for non-live sessions: change durationLabel (:674) to `const durationLabel = isLive ? formatDuration(session.duration) : null;` (D4 — the '· 22m' timer). Add a regression test to SessionNode.test.tsx modeled on the existing live-working test at :256: set runtimeById['planning-dead'] = { activity: 'working', lastActivity: '2026-05-06T11:55:00.000Z' } and render a session { sessionId: 'planning-dead', type: 'planning', presence: 'ended', status: 'stopped' }; assert the row does NOT contain styles.sessionIconRunning, the status dot data-status is not 'active' (it is 'ended'), and no duration label renders. - AC: Given a SessionNode with presence 'ended' and runtime activity 'working', when rendered it does NOT apply the styles.sessionIconRunning (live) icon class

title: pan-2284: Add shared synchronous bootReconciliationSkipReason(agent) classifier
description:
Create src/lib/cloister/boot-reconciliation-predicates.ts exporting a type BootReconciliationSkipReason = 'workspace_missing' | 'merged' | 'completed' and a synchronous function bootReconciliationSkipReason(agent): BootReconciliationSkipReason | null. Return 'workspace_missing' when !agent.workspace || !existsSync(agent.workspace). Return 'merged' when getReviewStatusSync(agent.issueId)?.mergeStatus==='merged', OR (agent as {merged?:boolean}).merged===true, OR (review.readyForMerge && review.reviewStatus==='passed' && review.testStatus==='passed'). Return 'completed' when the agent-dir completion marker exists (existsSync(join(getAgentDir(agent.id),'completed')) || '...completed.processed') AND review.reviewStatus==='passed' && review.testStatus==='passed'. Otherwise return null. These mirror the terminal sync skips in handleAgentStoppedEvent (deacon-auto-resume.ts:641, 693, 706, 710, 715). Do NOT include issue-closed, tmux-alive, backoff, idle, or the completed+blocked→resume override. Confirm no import cycle via npm run build; if a cycle appears, keep the classifier in this dedicated module (it must not statically import deacon-auto-resume). Add a unit test covering each category and the null (genuinely-stopped) case.
- AC: bootReconciliationSkipReason returns 'workspace_missing' for an agent whose workspace path is null or does not exist on disk, and null for one whose workspace exists (all other fields clean)
- AC: Returns 'merged' when review.mergeStatus==='merged', when agent.merged===true, and when review is readyForMerge with reviewStatus and testStatus both 'passed'
- AC: Returns 'completed' only when an agent-dir completed (or completed.processed) marker exists AND review and test both 'passed'; returns null when the marker exists but review is 'blocked' (the resume-flipping case stays out of the classifier)
- AC: npm run build produces a bundle and logs no ESM import-cycle error, proving the classifier module introduces no cycle
close_reason: Closed

title: pan-2158: Implement issue
description:
## Symptom

Observed RUN-33 (2026-06-29) on PAN-2157 (the merge-unblocker fix). `pan plan PAN-2157 --auto` ran the analysis, produced a strong recommendation, then **stopped and asked the operator** — the agent pane ends with literal text *"Which way do you want me to go?"* and sits idle ("Baked for 4m 11s", blank prompt). The critical-path producer is stalled indefinitely.

## Why this is wrong

1. **The decision was already defaulted in the PRD.** PAN-2157's body enumerated 3 options (gh/installation token; provision GitHub App; warn-only) and the agent itself strongly recommended option 2 (gh token) as the smallest change that satisfies AC-1. `pan plan --auto` is documented to *"run end-to-end without prompting; if it encounters a contradiction it can't resolve, escalate to interactive; record inferred choices in plan.autoDecisions[]"*. A documented set of options with a clear best choice is **not** an unresolvable contradiction — auto-mode should have picked option 2, recorded it in autoDecisions, and proceeded.
2. **The flywheel cannot unblock it.** `pan tell` is forbidden from the flywheel role, so a single unanswered planning question stalls a producer with no autonomous recovery path. Combined with the --no-resume boot (no overflow-respawn), the agent just sits there.

## Fix direction (do not patch from flywheel role)

- **Primary:** `--auto` must NOT escalate to interactive when the PRD/issue documents the options and a defensible default exists. Pick the recommended option, record it in `plan.autoDecisions[]` with rationale, and continue. Reserve interactive escalation for genuine contradictions (conflicting requirements with no documented resolution).
- **Secondary (defense-in-depth):** when an --auto agent does ask a question, the deacon stuck-detector / a sanctioned advance path should be able to deliver the recorded default (or a 'proceed with your recommendation' nudge) so an unanswered question can't indefinitely strand a critical-path agent.

## Acceptance

- AC-1: `pan plan <id> --auto` on an issue whose body lists options + a recommended default produces a vBRIEF without prompting, with the chosen option recorded in `plan.autoDecisions[]`.
- AC-2: A simulated agent question under --auto is auto-advanced (or never asked), not left idle.

Discovered while orchestrating PAN-2157. Filed by the Flywheel orchestrator (RUN-33).

Flywheel-Discovered-In: RUN-33

Pick the recommended option, record it in plan.autoDecisions[] with rationale, and continue. Reserve interactive escalation for genuine contradictions (conflicting requirements with no documented resolution).
- AC: **Secondary (defense-in-depth):** when an --auto agent does ask a question, the deacon stuck-detector / a sanctioned advance path should be able to deliver the recorded default (or a 'proceed with your recommendation' nudge) so an unanswered question can't indefinitely strand a critical-path agent.
- AC: AC-1: pan plan <id> --auto on an issue whose body lists options + a recommended default produces a vBRIEF without prompting, with the chosen option recorded in plan.autoDecisions[].
- AC: AC-2: A simulated agent question under --auto is auto-advanced (or never asked), not left idle.

title: pan-2297: Real-git integration test reproducing PAN-2296: batch shrink lands a consistent baseline on main
description:
Add tests/unit/lib/cloister/uat-promote-baseline.test.ts. Build a real bare origin repo plus a projectRoot clone containing scripts/lint-file-size.sh + scripts/file-size-baseline.txt (copy the real script like lint-file-size.test.ts does). Seed main with a baselined file at 1925 lines and a matching baseline entry. Create a uat/<name> branch whose tree shrinks that file to 1924 lines WITHOUT lowering the baseline (reproducing the PAN-2296 state). Call buildUatPromoteGitDeps(projectRoot).mergeIntoMain('uat/<name>', 'msg'). After it returns, fetch origin/main and assert: (a) the baselined file is 1924 lines; (b) scripts/file-size-baseline.txt records 1924 for that file; (c) running `bash scripts/lint-file-size.sh` (check) against the origin/main tree exits 0. Keep git work in temp dirs; never touch the real repo. This test must fail against the pre-fix mergeIntoMain and pass after wire-into-promote.
- AC: Given a uat branch whose tree shrinks a baselined file from 1925 to 1924 lines with an un-lowered baseline, when mergeIntoMain promotes it, then origin/main's scripts/file-size-baseline.txt records 1924 for that file.
- AC: Given the promoted main tree, when `bash scripts/lint-file-size.sh` (check mode) runs against it, then it exits 0 (no stale-high baseline).
- AC: Given the pre-fix mergeIntoMain (no reconcile), when the same scenario runs, then the test asserting a consistent baseline fails — proving the test reproduces PAN-2296.
close_reason: Added real-git UAT promote baseline regression test in 6ede05e729. Verified uat-promote-baseline.test.ts, uat-promote.test.ts, and lint:file-size.

expected_outputs: a test that reproduces the PAN-2296 shrink-then-merge scenario fails before the wire-into-promote fix and passes after it

title: pan-2297: Reconcile the file-size baseline in mergeIntoMain before pushing the UAT batch to main
description:
In src/lib/cloister/uat-promote.ts, inside buildUatPromoteGitDeps().mergeIntoMain (lines ~211-229), between `await runGit(['merge', '--no-ff', ref, '-m', message], worktreePath)` and `await runGit(['push', 'origin', 'HEAD:main'], worktreePath)`, call `const { changed } = await reconcileFileSizeBaseline(worktreePath, runGit)`. When `changed`, run `await runGit(['commit', '--amend', '--no-edit'], worktreePath)` so the lowered baseline becomes part of the single merge commit. Then push. When not changed, push the merge commit unchanged (no amend). Import reconcileFileSizeBaseline from './file-size-reconcile.js'. Update the file's top doc comment and/or the mergeIntoMain comment to record that main receives the tested tree PLUS a deliberate file-size-baseline reconciliation (baseline.txt is CI metadata, the only permitted deviation from the exercised tree).
- AC: Given a batch whose merged tree shrinks a baselined file below its entry, when mergeIntoMain runs, then reconcileFileSizeBaseline is invoked in the merge worktree before the `git push origin HEAD:main` call.
- AC: Given reconcile returned changed:true, when mergeIntoMain proceeds, then it runs `git commit --amend --no-edit` so the pushed main head is a single merge commit whose tree includes the lowered baseline.
- AC: Given reconcile returned changed:false, when mergeIntoMain proceeds, then it pushes the merge commit with no amend (the pushed tree equals the tested merged tree).
- AC: The mergeIntoMain / file-level doc comment states that the baseline reconciliation is a deliberate exception to 'main receives exactly the tree the operator exercised'.
close_reason: Wired reconcileFileSizeBaseline into mergeIntoMain before push, amending only when changed, in 0f11f8eed2. Verified uat-promote.test.ts and lint:file-size; npm run typecheck still fails in typecheck:evals because @types/node is missing from workspace node_modules.

title: pan-2297: Add reconcileFileSizeBaseline helper that auto-lowers and stages the baseline in a worktree
description:
Create src/lib/cloister/file-size-reconcile.ts exporting `async function reconcileFileSizeBaseline(worktreePath: string, runGit: (args: string[], cwd: string) => Promise<{ stdout: string }>): Promise<{ changed: boolean }>`. It runs `bash scripts/lint-file-size.sh --update` with cwd = worktreePath (via execFileAsync on bash, or a small runShell using execFile — never execSync, per PAN-70). Then it checks `git status --porcelain -- scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` (via runGit, cwd = worktreePath): if the output is non-empty, run `git add scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` and return { changed: true }; otherwise return { changed: false } without staging. Do not commit here — committing/amending is the caller's responsibility (bead wire-into-promote). Add tests/unit/lib/cloister/file-size-reconcile.test.ts mirroring the temp-git-repo + installed-script pattern in tests/unit/scripts/lint-file-size.test.ts: (a) a baselined file shrunk below its entry -> helper lowers the entry, stages it, returns changed:true; (b) baseline already consistent -> returns changed:false and stages nothing.
- AC: Given a worktree whose baselined file is 1924 lines but scripts/file-size-baseline.txt records 1925, when reconcileFileSizeBaseline runs, then the entry is lowered to 1924 and the function returns { changed: true }.
- AC: Given changed:true, when the helper returns, then `git status --porcelain -- scripts/file-size-baseline.txt` shows the baseline staged (added to the index).
- AC: Given a worktree whose baseline already matches every file's line count, when reconcileFileSizeBaseline runs, then it returns { changed: false } and stages nothing (empty `git status --porcelain`).
- AC: Given a baseline entry whose file no longer exists (or is now at/under the 1000-line ceiling), when reconcileFileSizeBaseline runs, then that entry is dropped from scripts/file-size-baseline.txt and the function returns { changed: true }.
close_reason: Implemented reconcileFileSizeBaseline helper and tests in cfae50b94d; inspection passed.

expected_outputs: file-size-reconcile.test.ts passes including a case that lowers a stale baseline and a no-op case

title: pan-2265: Add a GraphQL rate-limit cool-down gate (defense-in-depth)
description:
Create src/lib/github-graphql-cooldown.ts exporting noteGraphQLRateLimit(err: unknown) — records a cool-down start when the error message matches a GraphQL-quota-exceeded pattern (e.g. /rate limit already exceeded/i or /API rate limit/i) — and isInGraphQLCooldown(): boolean — true for COOLDOWN_MS (~60000) after the last note. Wire it into refreshMergeStateFromGitHub's gh fallback (src/lib/webhook-handlers.ts:239): skip the doomed gh pr view GraphQL call and note the rate-limit when isInGraphQLCooldown() is true / on a caught rate-limit error. The timing test MUST use vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync() — no real setTimeout waits.
- AC: after noteGraphQLRateLimit() with a quota-exceeded error, isInGraphQLCooldown() returns true within ~60s and false thereafter (verified with fake timers)
- AC: while isInGraphQLCooldown() is true, refreshMergeStateFromGitHub's gh fallback emits no gh GraphQL call and returns without hitting GitHub
- AC: after noteGraphQLRateLimit() with an unrelated (non-rate-limit) error, isInGraphQLCooldown() returns false

expected_outputs: cool-down tests pass using fake timers — true within 60s, false after

title: pan-2265: Add shared App-REST helpers to github-app.ts (PR-by-head, issue-state, open-issue-labels)

- AC: getIssueState returns {state} from GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number} (App REST)
- AC: listOpenIssuesWithLabels returns each open issue's number and labels via paginated REST and excludes pull-request entries
- AC: importing each helper returns both a Promise form and an Effect-wrapped form, matching the getPullRequestState convention

title: pan-2294: Create notifyFlywheelOfUatPromote helper module reusing messageAgent + recordDeaconNudge
description:
Create src/lib/cloister/uat-promote-notify.ts exporting `notifyFlywheelOfUatPromote(result: PromoteResult, deps?: NotifyDeps): Promise<void>`. Import PromoteResult as a type-only import from './uat-promote.js', FLYWHEEL_ORCHESTRATOR_AGENT_ID from './flywheel.js', messageAgent from '../agents.js', recordDeaconNudge from './deacon-nudge-log.js', getFlywheelActiveRunId + isFlywheelGloballyPaused from '../overdeck/control-settings.js', and sessionExistsSync from '../tmux.js' (mirror the imports stuck-remediation.ts already uses). Define NotifyDeps with optional injectable overrides { getActiveRunId, isPaused, sessionExists, message, recordNudge } defaulting to the real implementations, so tests inject fakes. Behavior, all wrapped in a try/catch that swallows errors (best-effort — never rethrow): (1) if result.success !== true, return; (2) if !getActiveRunId(), return; (3) if isPaused(), return; (4) narrow to the success arm and read generation, members, mergeSha; (5) compute delivered = sessionExists(FLYWHEEL_ORCHESTRATOR_AGENT_ID); (6) if delivered, await message(FLYWHEEL_ORCHESTRATOR_AGENT_ID, <nudge>, 'uat-promote-notify') where <nudge> is the promote-specific Observe->Act instruction from the PRD (re-derive ready set EXCLUDING merged members, re-assemble a clean review+test-passed UAT batch, close out merged issues, re-arm next tick, do not ask/pause); (7) always recordNudge({ patrol: 'uat-promote-notify', issueId: members[0] ?? generation, action: 'notified flywheel-orchestrator to re-derive ready set after UAT promote', reason: 'operator promoted a UAT batch; flywheel must immediately rebuild to drop merged + regressed members before its next tick', state: { generation, members, mergeSha, delivered } }). Do NOT wire it into any caller in this bead — that is the next bead.
- AC: Given result.success===true with an active un-paused flywheel run AND a live orchestrator session, notifyFlywheelOfUatPromote delivers a nudge via the injected message dep to FLYWHEEL_ORCHESTRATOR_AGENT_ID and records a deacon nudge with delivered:true.
- AC: Given result.success===true with an active run but NO live orchestrator session, the helper records a deacon nudge with delivered:false and does NOT call the message dep.
- AC: Given result.success===false, OR no active flywheel run, OR the flywheel globally paused, the helper returns without calling the message dep or the recordNudge dep.
- AC: When the injected message dep throws, notifyFlywheelOfUatPromote resolves without throwing (error swallowed, best-effort).

title: pan-2284: Add shared synchronous bootReconciliationSkipReason(agent) classifier
description:

Return 'workspace_missing' when !agent.workspace || !existsSync(agent.workspace). Return 'merged' when getReviewStatusSync(agent.issueId)?.mergeStatus==='merged', OR (agent as {merged?:boolean}).merged===true, OR (review.readyForMerge && review.reviewStatus==='passed' && review.testStatus==='passed'). Return 'completed' when the agent-dir completion marker exists (existsSync(join(getAgentDir(agent.id),'completed')) || '...completed.processed') AND review.reviewStatus==='passed' && review.testStatus==='passed'. Otherwise return null. These mirror the terminal sync skips in handleAgentStoppedEvent (deacon-auto-resume.ts:641, 693, 706, 710, 715). Do NOT include issue-closed, tmux-alive, backoff, idle, or the completed+blocked→resume override. Confirm no import cycle via npm run build; if a cycle appears, keep the classifier in this dedicated module (it must not statically import deacon-auto-resume). Add a unit test covering each category and the null (genuinely-stopped) case.
- AC: bootReconciliationSkipReason returns 'workspace_missing' for an agent whose workspace path is null or does not exist on disk, and null for one whose workspace exists (all other fields clean)
- AC: Returns 'merged' when review.mergeStatus==='merged', when agent.merged===true, and when review is readyForMerge with reviewStatus and testStatus both 'passed'
- AC: Returns 'completed' only when an agent-dir completed (or completed.processed) marker exists AND review and test both 'passed'; returns null when the marker exists but review is 'blocked' (the resume-flipping case stays out of the classifier)
- AC: npm run build produces a bundle and logs no ESM import-cycle error, proving the classifier module introduces no cycle

title: pan-2227: PAN-2204: scripts/guard-agent-main-push.sh + pre-push wiring — agents cannot push code to main

Fail CLOSED: called with an empty/undeterminable range → exit 1 with an explanatory message (it is a trust gate; the escape hatch remains). Note: this machine's global git user.name IS panopticon-agent[bot], so all local code pushes to main will need the escape hatch — deliberate friction, document it in the rejection message.

title: pan-2214: FR-16: state-derived verification gates never silently reset a passed review verdict
description:
In src/lib/cloister/verification-runner.ts, the vbrief-ac failure path (the `if (acStatus && !acStatus.allCompleted)` block around line 537) currently calls setReviewStatusSync with `reviewStatus: 'pending'`, knocking a PASSED review verdict back to pending with no operator surface — the incident: a .pan/records restore made completed ACs look pending and silently invalidated a real review. Change the rule: state-derived gates (vbrief-ac — AC completeness comes from spec/statusOverrides state, not reviewable code; likewise the vbrief-conflict path) must NOT write reviewStatus at all. They set verificationStatus='failed' plus verificationNotes naming the cause, and when the pre-existing reviewStatus was 'passed' they additionally emit a needs-you operator notification (reuse the escalateVerificationStuck notification mechanism) stating that a passed review is being held by a state-derived gate and why. Code-derived gate failures (typecheck/lint/test checks earlier in the runner) keep their existing requeue behavior, but every write that changes reviewStatus away from 'passed' must include the reason in verificationNotes so the transition is auditable. Tests: (1) reviewStatus='passed' + vbrief-ac incomplete → reviewStatus still 'passed', verificationStatus='failed', needs-you emitted; (2) code-gate (test) failure → existing requeue preserved with reason recorded; (3) vbrief-ac failure with reviewStatus not yet 'passed' → no needs-you (normal retry messaging only).
- AC: Given reviewStatus='passed' and the vbrief-ac gate finding incomplete ACs, Then verification records verificationStatus='failed' while reviewStatus remains 'passed'
- AC: Given that held-verdict case, Then a needs-you operator notification is emitted naming the vbrief-ac gate and the incomplete-AC cause
- AC: Given a code-gate failure (typecheck/lint/test), Then the existing requeue behavior is preserved and the reviewStatus transition carries its reason in verificationNotes
- AC: Given vbrief-ac failing while reviewStatus is not 'passed', Then no needs-you notification fires (normal retry feedback only)
close_reason: Changed state-derived vBRIEF gates to fail verification without resetting passed reviews, added held-review needs-you stuck marking, preserved code-gate requeue behavior with verificationNotes, and verified with npx vitest run tests/cloister/verification-runner.test.ts tests/unit/lib/cloister plus npm run typecheck.

title: pan-2214: FR-13: done-without-signal detection in classifyInFlightSlots, gated by swarm.infer_completion
description:
Extend classifyInFlightSlots (src/lib/cloister/deacon-swarm.ts:364) — which already tracks per-slot progress via slotProgressObservations (pane output digest + branch tip commit time) and classifies 'stalled' past swarmStallThresholdMs (deacon-swarm.ts:448, env PAN_SWARM_STALL_THRESHOLD_MS) — to detect done-without-signal: a LIVE slot session whose progress is idle past the threshold AND whose slot branch has at least one commit ahead of the issue branch AND whose slot worktree is clean. Add an injectable dep for the clean-worktree check (git status --porcelain in the slot worktree, async exec only — no execSync) alongside the existing getBranchTipCommitTime pattern. Behavior by config swarm.infer_completion ('off'|'nudge'|'auto', default 'nudge'; read via cloister config in src/lib/cloister/config.ts with env override PAN_SWARM_INFER_COMPLETION following the stall-threshold pattern): 'off' — current behavior (running/stalled only); 'nudge' — on first idle expiry meeting the done-signature, emit ONE nudge action delivering the exact completion command (`pan done <ISSUE>` with the real issue id) to the slot session, recorded so it never repeats for the same unchanged observation; 'auto' — additionally, on a SECOND consecutive idle expiry with the done-signature still holding, classify the slot 'ready-to-merge' and append a `signal: inferred` marker to the coordination action log. Slots with a dirty worktree or zero commits ahead are never nudged or inferred (they classify stalled as today). All timing tests use vi.useFakeTimers() or the existing options.now injection — never real waits.
- AC: Given infer_completion='nudge' and a live slot idle past threshold with commits ahead and a clean worktree, Then classifyInFlightSlots emits exactly one nudge action containing `pan done` and does not repeat it on the next unchanged observation
- AC: Given infer_completion='auto' and the done-signature holding across a second consecutive idle expiry, Then the slot classifies ready-to-merge and the action log contains a `signal: inferred` marker
- AC: Given infer_completion='off', Then classification output preserves current behavior for the same inputs (running/stalled only, no nudges, no inference)
- AC: Given a dirty slot worktree OR zero commits ahead, Then no nudge fires and no inference happens regardless of mode — the slot falls back to the existing stalled classification
- AC: Given the new completion-inference suite, When it runs, Then it exits 0 driving all timing through fake timers or the injected `now` option — no real-clock waits appear in the tests
close_reason: Implemented FR-13 done-without-signal inference; focused tests, typecheck, and lint passed.

title: pan-2214: FR-12: per-issue async mutex serializing .pan/records read-modify-write

Simulate async gaps with resolved promises/microtasks or fake timers — no real delays.

- AC: Given swarm.slotAssignments written via writeIssueRecordForWorkspaceSync while a rebuild is in flight, When the rebuild completes, Then the final record preserves the slot assignments (PAN-1791 wipe regression)

title: pan-2076: WI-6: Watchdog preserves the decision across restart
description:
Ensure a watchdog restart honors an already-made decision instead of re-prompting or reverting. In src/supervisor/watchdog.ts (spawnRestart, the env-inheriting path), do NOT rely on env to carry resume intent. On the restarted dashboard, the boot sequence (WI-2) reads getBootReconciliationState(): if a decision exists for the SAME boot_id (i.e. this is a watchdog restart, not a genuine reboot), it must NOT re-stamp 'pending' or re-open the grace — it honors the persisted decision and (re-)applies it idempotently via WI-3. boot_id distinguishes a watchdog restart (same boot_id persisted) from a genuine operator reboot (fresh boot_id -> re-prompt). Decide boot_id continuity: the watchdog passes the prior boot_id forward (e.g. via a durable marker the restarted process reads), so the restarted dashboard recognizes the in-progress boot. Once AC-2 of the PRD is verified in production, the supervisor-env persistent-resume workaround can be retired (OUT OF SCOPE here — do not remove it in this issue).

description:

Remove/neuter the RUNTIME callers of getNoResumeMode() (src/lib/cloister/no-resume-mode.ts:13). Audit each caller and replace the runtime gate with the durable decision where a gate is still wanted, or delete it where the grace/decision now covers it: deacon-auto-resume.ts (lines 116,252,574,792,848 — autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents/handleAgentStoppedEvent/reconcileAgentLiveness etc.), deacon-review-status.ts (333,538), idle-stack-reaper.ts (114), closed-issue-reaper.ts (105,149). After this, getNoResumeMode() must have NO runtime callers that gate relaunch/dispatch/orphan-recovery (the env-loss bug class root); the only consultation of OVERDECK_NO_RESUME is the boot-time decision seed. disableNoResumeMode() (called today by /api/resume-all) is superseded by the decision plane — update or remove its caller accordingly so /api/resume-all (if kept transitionally) writes decision='resume_all' + applies, rather than flipping env. title: pan-2076: WI-3: Apply the boot-reconciliation decision
description:

Must be idempotent: once decision!=='pending' the apply runs once and subsequent patrol ticks are a no-op for the set (guard on a decided/applied flag or on the decision already being non-pending + set already actioned). Re-applying across a patrol tick must not double-spawn. This function is invoked by the WI-2 grace-expiry timer and by the WI-4 submit route.

- AC: The resume path respects the existing work-slot/load/stagger brakes and does not bypass them beyond what autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents already applies.
close_reason: Added idempotent boot reconciliation apply path for resume_all, hold_all, and per_agent through existing resume gates.

title: pan-2076: WI-2: Grace window in the boot sequence
description:
In the boot sequence, compute the reconciliation set and open a bounded grace window. Reconciliation set = agents from the SQLite agents table (listAllAgents) that were role-relevant and running before this start but whose tmux session on socket 'overdeck' is now gone — i.e. the same stopped work-agent candidate set autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents already derives (src/lib/cloister/deacon-auto-resume.ts:801-803), additionally excluding #1436 stale stopped-agent zombies and paused/troubled/per-issue-ignored agents (those are read-only, never resume candidates — AC-2). On boot (src/dashboard/server/main.ts, near the Cloister auto-start at lines 583-610): stamp a fresh boot_id and call stampBootReconciliation(bootId, deadline) where deadline = now + startup.reconciliation_grace_secs (new cloister config key, default 30); set decision='pending' UNLESS OVERDECK_NO_RESUME is set at boot (then 'hold_all', skip grace — see WI-5). If WI-6 finds an existing decision for the SAME boot_id, do not re-stamp (idempotent). Gate the resume path: in autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents (deacon-auto-resume.ts:778) and the flywheel auto-launch, while getBootReconciliationState().decision==='pending', SKIP the reconciliation-set agents (return them un-resumed) — the patrol still runs for everything else. Arm a server-side timer of grace_secs that flips 'pending'->'resume_all' on expiry (the operator-approved default action is RESUME), then triggers WI-3 apply. The timer is authoritative; the modal countdown (WI-4) is display-only. TESTS MUST USE vi.useFakeTimers() + advanceTimersByTimeAsync — never real setTimeout (repo fake-timers rule; the grace is a real delay).
- AC: Given a simulated unclean boot with a non-empty reconciliation set and no env set, the boot persists decision='pending' with a fresh boot_id and a grace deadline = now + grace_secs, and autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents and flywheel auto-launch skip (do not resume) the reconciliation-set agents while decision==='pending'.
- AC: startup.reconciliation_grace_secs defaults to 30 from cloister config and sets the deadline; when fake timers advance past grace_secs the boot updates decision 'pending'->'resume_all' and the apply path (WI-3) runs.
- AC: The reconciliation set excludes paused, troubled, and per-issue-ignored agents and #1436 stale stopped-agent zombies; the grace test passes using vi.useFakeTimers()/advanceTimersByTimeAsync (no real setTimeout).
close_reason: Added boot reconciliation startup stamping, 30s grace config, pending auto-resume hold gate, and fake-timer tests.

title: pan-1084: Implement issue
description:
## Severity: P1

Observed during PAN-1059 work session: the work agent detected that the inspector subagent (\`inspect-pan-1059-workspace-hiq5\` tmux session) was stuck on a permission prompt for \`npm test\`, and **self-approved it** by sending \`tmux send-keys -t inspect-pan-1059-workspace-hiq5 2 C-m\`.

This is doubly bad:

1. **It masks the underlying bug.** The reason the prompt appeared at all is the issue tracked in #A (inspect spawn doesn't honor bypass mode). Self-approval makes the symptom disappear so the user never sees the prompt — and the deeper bug stays hidden.
2. **It's a real safety hazard.** Permission prompts exist for a reason. An agent that learns "if I see a prompt, send '2' to approve" can silently approve a destructive operation on a future bead — a \`rm -rf\` confirmation, a \`git push --force\` confirmation, an outbound HTTP request to an external service. There is no check on what's being approved.

## Where to fix

\`src/lib/cloister/prompts/work.md\` — the work-agent role prompt.

Add an explicit prohibition near the inspection-handoff section (around line 160-184 today). Suggested copy:

> ### Subagent permission prompts — never self-approve
>
> If you observe that any subagent (the inspector spawned by \`pan inspect\`, or any other Claude Code subagent in a tmux session you can see) appears stuck waiting on a permission prompt, do **NOT** send keystrokes via \`tmux send-keys\` to approve, decline, or otherwise interact with the prompt.
>
> Permission prompts indicate a permissions configuration issue that must be raised to the user. Self-approving via \`tmux send-keys\` can silently authorize destructive operations (file deletion, force-pushes, outbound network calls) that the user did not intend to allow.
>
> Instead, when you detect a stuck subagent that appears to be waiting on a prompt:
>
> 1. Capture the tmux pane content to document what was waiting (\`tmux -L panopticon capture-pane -t <session> -p -S -50\`).
> 2. Stop polling the subagent. Do not retry.
> 3. Signal back to the user via \`pan tell <issue-id>\` with a summary: which subagent, what bead it was inspecting, and the captured pane content excerpt.
> 4. Halt your own bead loop. The user must address the permissions configuration before work can resume.
>
> The only acceptable interaction with a subagent's tmux session from inside the work agent is read-only inspection (\`capture-pane\`, \`list-sessions\`). Writing keystrokes is forbidden.

## Also fix at the role-file level

The work role definition (\`roles/work.md\`) should encode this as a hard rule, not just prompt copy. Consider:

- Adding a tool-permission denylist that prevents \`Bash(tmux send-keys ...)\` invocations targeting non-self tmux sessions.
- Or a pre-tool hook that blocks \`tmux send-keys\` targeting any session whose name doesn't match the work agent's own ID.

The denylist is more durable than prompt copy — agents may rationalize "this case is different" if it's just prompt text.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] \`work.md\` prompt contains the explicit prohibition above.
- [x] A tool-level or hook-level enforcement blocks \`tmux send-keys\` against any session that isn't the work agent's own session.
- [x] Test: spawn a work agent in a synthetic environment, plant a stuck subagent session, observe that the work agent does NOT send keys and instead emits a \`pan tell\` notification.

## Related

- #A — the inspect-agent permission-bypass bug whose symptom got masked by this self-approval
- PAN-1059 — the work session where this was observed

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
- AC: \work.md\ prompt contains the explicit prohibition above.
- AC: A tool-level or hook-level enforcement blocks \tmux send-keys\ against any session that isn't the work agent's own session.
- AC: Test: spawn a work agent in a synthetic environment, plant a stuck subagent session, observe that the work agent does NOT send keys and instead emits a \pan tell\ notification.
close_reason: Added subagent permission-prompt prohibition to work-agent prompt and tmux-send-keys-guard hook that blocks Bash tmux send-keys/paste-buffer targeting non-self sessions; wired into roles/work.md and setup-hooks; added tests.

title: pan-2093: Bound the Deacon's re-spawn of orphaned ohmypi work agents so they reach troubled instead of looping forever
description:

Branch A (retried-but-not-bounding): orphan recovery calls resetAgentFailureCount (src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts:5837) for re-orphans that fall OUTSIDE the 120s rapid-post-resume-death window (isRapidPostResumeDeath / RAPID_POST_RESUME_DEATH_MS=120_000, :5742), so consecutiveFailures stays at 1 and the agent never reaches 'troubled' (maxConsecutiveFailures=3 within troubledWindowMs=10min; backoff [5,30,120]s — src/lib/cloister/auto-resume-config.ts:9-13) — fix by NOT resetting the count for readiness/orphan-class recurrences of an ohmypi work agent (mirror the existing isRapidPostResumeDeath skip-reset at :5836) so failures accrue and the agent bounds to 'troubled'. Branch B (never retried): a gate drops it (e.g. the backoff gate at deacon.ts:6762-6768 or the idle gate at :6831-6836) — fix the specific gate so an orphaned ohmypi work agent is eligible for bounded re-spawn. EITHER branch's change MUST be scoped so claude-code/codex orphan recovery is byte-for-byte unchanged (regression-test). This item depends on ohmypi-work-session-survives producing the recoverable 'stopped' state for dead ohmypi work panes. Record the reproduction findings in .pan/continue.json before the edit. All backoff/troubled tests use fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync), NEVER real waits (NFR-2).

title: pan-2093: Keep the ohmypi work tmux session alive when omp is slow or exits, and detect dead omp panes
description:
RC-2 fix: in src/lib/agents.ts spawnAgent (:3778), immediately after createSession(...) at :4056, when resolvedHarness === 'ohmypi', set `await Effect.runPromise(setOption(agentId, 'destroy-unattached', 'off'));` and `await Effect.runPromise(setOption(exactPaneTarget(agentId), 'remain-on-exit', 'on'));` — copying spawnRun's :3724-3725 (setOption/exactPaneTarget are already imported at agents.ts:13). If omp exits early with an auth/CLIProxy/model error, the now-preserved dead pane exposes it — file a SEPARATE substrate issue for that orthogonal omp-startup failure; PAN-2093's session-survival + recovery still apply. FALLBACK if no live repro is available: implement as specified (correct under both hypotheses) and note the deferred live confirmation in the PR. title: pan-2093: Raise the ohmypi ready.json readiness window from 30s to 90s
description:
Introduce `const OHMYPI_READY_TIMEOUT_SEC = 90;` in src/lib/agents.ts and use it as the default timeoutSec for BOTH waitForOhmypiAgentReady (:292) and writeOhmypiAgentPrompt (:428) — replacing the literal `= 30` defaults. This covers all five callers (spawnAgent :4085, spawnRun :3730, resumeAgent :5191, restartAgent :5398, recoverAgent :5582), which pass no override and inherit the default. Change SPAWN_READY_TIMEOUT_MS 30_000 -> 90_000 in src/lib/runtimes/ohmypi.ts (:58) for parity, keeping the OhmypiSpawnTimeout message accurate. Add a comment at BOTH constants documenting the invariant: the readiness window (90_000ms) MUST stay strictly below WORK_LAUNCHER_GRACE_MS (120_000ms, src/lib/cloister/agent-grace.ts:1) so the Deacon does not orphan the agent mid-cold-start. - AC: A guard unit test fails (exits non-zero) when the readiness window is not strictly below WORK_LAUNCHER_GRACE_MS, i.e. it asserts OHMYPI_READY_TIMEOUT_SEC * 1000 < WORK_LAUNCHER_GRACE_MS (90s < 120s).

title: pan-1718: Supervisor stop waits for exit; start verifies survival — no dead pidfile
description:
In src/lib/supervisor.ts: (1) stopSupervisorProcessSync — after SIGTERM, poll isProcessAlive(pid) with a bounded sync wait (total ~2s; escalate to SIGKILL at ~1.5s) BEFORE unlinking the pidfile and returning, so the stop actually takes effect. (2) startSupervisorProcessSync — after writeFileSync(pid), wait ~150ms (sync) and re-check isProcessAlive(child.pid); if the child has already died (e.g. EADDRINUSE against the still-running old supervisor), log a clear error and unlink the pidfile so no dead pid is left behind. Use a sync sleep via Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms) — never a busy-spin and never execSync('sleep').
- AC: Given a live supervisor pid, when stopSupervisorProcessSync runs, then it does not unlink the pidfile or return until isProcessAlive(pid) is false (or the SIGKILL-escalation bound elapses).
- AC: Given startSupervisorProcessSync spawns a child that dies immediately, when start completes, then it logs an error and leaves NO pidfile pointing at the dead pid.
- AC: Given the bounded sync waits, when reviewed, then they use Atomics.wait (not a busy-loop and not execSync) and total stop-wait never exceeds ~2s.
close_reason: Supervisor stop waits for exit and start verifies child survival; no dead pidfile

title: pan-1718: Acquire the restart lock before the pan reload dev-marker SIGUSR2 branch
description:

(1) Add a short contract line to the append-system-prompt content assembled for pi/omp conversations (the --append-system-prompt files in buildOhmypiCommand, launcher-generator.ts:616-630; content assembled server-side): a message arriving with source 'extension' is from the orchestrator / another agent, NOT the human operator — and how to treat it (FR-7). (2) Once WI-3 is proven, retire tmux-paste body delivery for pi/omp: resolveConversationDeliveryMethod (conversations.ts:1154) no longer routes pi/omp MESSAGE BODIES to tmux (the WI-7 abort key is excepted). Add a no-loss note in a code comment: the only behavior the old tmux-paste path provided for pi/omp conversations was (1) text delivery -> now the channel, and (2) nothing else. Do NOT touch the claude-code delivery path (NFR-5).

- AC: Given the full change set, when npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm test run, then they pass with no new failures.
close_reason: Added Pi source contract prompt injection, retired pi/oh-my-pi tmux body delivery default with no-loss note, and updated no-loss matrix. Verified with typecheck, lint, targeted tests, and npm test.

title: pan-2088: WI-5: Frontend — ack-based Sending, steer/follow_up, Stop button, live effort + compact
description:
In src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/chat/ (ConversationPanel.tsx, ComposerFooter.tsx, MessagesTimeline.tsx; effort/model pickers already exist as EffortPicker.tsx / ModelPicker.tsx): (1) Sending... clears on ACK for pi/omp conversations — treat the POST resolution as the clear signal rather than waiting for transcript echo (ConversationPanel.tsx:1222 echo logic), keeping the stall-timeout failSend fallback (:1267-1282). (2) Stop/Abort button — always visible while a turn runs; calls POST .../abort (WI-7); optimistic 'Stopping...' with sub-second feedback. (3) Effort dropdown -> live: on change POST .../thinking-level (WI-6) and reflect the selected level. (4) Compact action — a menu/button -> POST .../compact. (5) deliverAs control — a small toggle (default steer when busy) included in the send payload. Add component tests (mirror the existing chat component test style under src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/chat/__tests__/): Sending clears on ack; Stop calls abort; effort change posts thinking-level.
- AC: Given a pi/omp conversation, when a sent message is ack'd, then the 'Sending...' indicator clears on the ack (not on transcript echo); when no ack arrives, the stall-timeout failSend fallback still moves the bubble to the retry outbox.
- AC: Given a running turn, when the operator clicks the always-visible Stop button, then POST .../abort is called and an optimistic 'Stopping...' state appears within sub-second.
- AC: Given the composer effort dropdown, when the operator changes it, then POST .../thinking-level is called with the selected level and the UI reflects the new level.
- AC: Given the composer, when the operator triggers the Compact action, then POST .../compact is called; a steer/follow_up toggle (default steer when the agent is busy) is present and its value is included in the send payload.
close_reason: Implemented Pi/oh-my-pi frontend controls: send POST ack marks optimistic messages acknowledged so Sending clears, composer deliverAs select threads steer/follow_up into send payload, live effort posts thinking-level, compact posts compact, and running Pi turns show Stop with optimistic Stopping state. Verified with focused frontend chat tests and npm run typecheck.

title: pan-2088: WI-7: Quick-abort mechanism via TUI interrupt keystroke (the one API gap)
description:
Add `POST /api/conversations/:name/abort` in src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts that sends pi/omp's TUI interrupt key to the pane via sendKeysAsync (async primitive from src/lib/tmux.ts) — NEVER sendKeys (sync). Record in a code comment that this single control-key send is the ONLY sanctioned remaining tmux write for pi/omp conversations (per NFR-4), because the extension API exposes no abort. IMPLEMENTATION CHECKPOINT — verify the interrupt key before wiring: launch a throwaway omp TUI in a `overdeck`-socket tmux session, start a long turn, send Escape (then Ctrl-C if needed), and `tmux -L overdeck capture-pane -e -p` to confirm the turn aborts AND the session SURVIVES (not exits). DECISION RULE: use the key that interrupts the turn while keeping the session alive — prefer Escape, else Ctrl-C. FALLBACK: if no keystroke cleanly interrupts without killing the session, (a) file an upstream request for pi.abort() in the extension API, and (b) ship abort as a documented 501 with an actionable message — do NOT fake it. (If a bash tool is mid-run a second control key may be needed — note but defer unless the checkpoint shows it is required.)
- AC: Given POST /api/conversations/:name/abort for a running pi/omp conversation, when handled, then the resolved interrupt control key is sent via sendKeysAsync to the correct tmux target (no sync sendKeys is called).
- AC: Given the empirically verified interrupt key, when abort is sent during a turn, then the turn stops and the tmux session survives (does not exit) — OR, if no key cleanly interrupts without killing the session, the endpoint returns 501 with an actionable message and an upstream pi.abort() request is filed (never a faked no-op).
- AC: Given the abort endpoint code, when reviewed, then a code comment records that this single control-key send is the only sanctioned remaining tmux write for pi/omp conversations (NFR-4).
close_reason: Implemented POST /api/conversations/:name/abort for pi/oh-my-pi using sendKeysAsync with the verified Escape interrupt key. Checkpoint: throwaway omp TUI running sleep 60 showed Escape cancelled the command and tmux has-session confirmed the session survived. Verified with targeted conversations tests and npm run typecheck.

title: pan-2088: WI-6: Server thinking-level, model, and compact control endpoints

Extend the existing `POST /api/conversations/:name/switch-model` (:2828): for pi/omp RUNNING conversations additionally write a set_model command so the change is LIVE (verify the current behavior — likely record/relaunch only — and keep that for claude). Add `POST /api/conversations/:name/compact`: pi/omp -> write a compact command (Claude keeps its native-compaction interception at ~:998-1010 — do NOT change). Leave conversations.ts:1668 --effort gate as-is for claude, but note pi/omp effort now flows through the channel (set_thinking_level), not --effort.
- AC: Given POST /api/conversations/:name/thinking-level with a valid level for a pi/omp conversation, when handled, then a set_thinking_level command is written, the ack is awaited, and the level is persisted on the conversation record.
- AC: Given POST thinking-level with an invalid level value, when handled, then the endpoint returns 400 and writes no command.
- AC: Given POST /api/conversations/:name/switch-model for a running pi/omp conversation, when handled, then a set_model command is written so the change is live; the claude-code switch-model behavior is unchanged.
- AC: Given POST /api/conversations/:name/compact for a pi/omp conversation, when handled, then a compact command is written; the claude-code native-compaction interception path is unchanged.
close_reason: Implemented Pi/oh-my-pi live control endpoints: thinking-level persistence via effort, live set_model through the control channel, and compact control. Verified with targeted conversations tests and npm run typecheck.

title: pan-2088: WI-3: Route pi/omp conversation message delivery through the control channel
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts message handler (around :1054-1088, route registered at :2940 '/api/conversations/:name/messages') add `deliverConversationViaControlChannel(conv, text, { source, deliverAs })` that writes a prompt|steer|follow_up command via writeConversationControlCommand and awaits the ack (the WI-4 registry promise) with a timeout. Add `pickDeliverAs(conv, bodyDeliverAs)`: if the agent is currently running a turn (reuse the existing pending/working detection used for the composer state) default 'steer', else plain 'prompt'; an operator 'follow_up' override comes from the request body `deliverAs`. In the handler branch on harness: pi/omp -> deliverConversationViaControlChannel with source 'operator'; claude-code -> UNCHANGED (existing deliverAgentMessage + supervisor + eaten-watcher). Keep injectPiConversationMemory (:1059) — it still augments the text before delivery. Keep the catch/error mapping unchanged.
- AC: Given an idle pi/omp conversation, when the operator sends a composer message, then a 'prompt' control command is written (no tmux paste) and the request resolves on the ack.
- AC: Given a pi/omp conversation whose agent is mid-turn, when the operator sends a message with no override, then a 'steer' command is written; when the operator selects follow_up, then a 'follow_up' command is written.
- AC: Given a claude-code conversation, when the operator sends a message, then delivery still goes through deliverAgentMessage/supervisor unchanged (no control-channel write).
close_reason: Routed pi/oh-my-pi conversation messages through the control-channel writer with ack waiting, busy-turn steer/follow_up selection, and preserved claude-code deliverAgentMessage path. Targeted route tests and npm run typecheck pass.

title: pan-2088: WI-4: Server ack endpoint + pending-command registry
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts (or a small sibling service) add an in-memory `Map<commandId, { resolve, reject, timer }>` pending-command registry, and a new endpoint `POST /api/conversations/:name/control-ack` (mirror the route shape at conversations.ts:3346 delivery-method) that the extension POSTs `{ id, ok, error? }` to; on receipt resolve/reject the pending entry and clear its timer. Provide the awaitable primitive used by WI-3: register a pending entry keyed by command id and return a promise that resolves on ack or rejects on a CONTROL_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS timeout. An unknown ack id is a no-op. TEST RULE: use fake timers (vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync()) for the timeout — never real setTimeout.
- AC: Given a pending command id in the registry, when POST /api/conversations/:name/control-ack arrives with { id, ok: true }, then the awaiting delivery promise resolves.
- AC: Given a pending command with no ack, when CONTROL_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS elapses (verified with fake timers), then the promise rejects and the entry/timer is cleaned up.
- AC: Given an id not in the registry, when POST control-ack arrives, then it is a no-op (no throw, no effect on other pending entries).
close_reason: Added pending conversation control ack registry, timeout cleanup with fake-timer tests, and POST /api/conversations/:name/control-ack handler. Targeted ack-registry tests and npm run typecheck pass; full conversations.test.ts still has unrelated sandbox failures writing under real ~/.claude paths.

title: pan-2088: WI-2: Control-channel primitive — server writer + extension watch/drain/dispatch/ack (both packages + lib)
description:
Create new server-side lib module src/lib/runtimes/conversation-control.ts exporting: `conversationControlPaths(agentId, home?)` (control dir under ohmypiFifoPaths(agentId).agentDir i.e. ~/.overdeck/agents/<id>/control/), `writeConversationControlCommand(agentId, command, home?)` that writes ONE JSON file per command via atomic temp-file + rename into control/ at mode 0600 (dir created at 0700), and the `ControlCommand` union: `{ id; type: 'prompt'|'steer'|'follow_up'; message; source: 'operator'|'orchestrator' } | { id; type: 'set_thinking_level'; level: ThinkingLevel } | { id; type: 'set_model'; model } | { id; type: 'compact' }`. Extension side (BOTH packages, inside the session_start handler at ohmypi-extension/src/index.ts:652, after the existing context handlers — never from the module factory per NFR-3): drain any pre-existing control files, then fs.watch the control/ dir; for each command file parse, dispatch to the matching pi.* call guarded by the WI-1 capability probe, unlink the file, and HTTP-POST an ack { id, ok, error? } reusing the existing dashboard POST helper. Also register `omp.on('input', e => ...)` to record event.source for FR-7. Tolerate malformed files (skip + log, never crash the watcher).
- AC: Given writeConversationControlCommand is called for an agent, when it returns, then exactly one JSON command file exists under <agentDir>/control/ at mode 0600 and the control/ dir is mode 0700.
- AC: Given a malformed (non-JSON) file present in control/, when the extension watcher processes it, then it is skipped and logged and the watcher keeps running (no crash).
- AC: Given a 'steer' command file is dropped into control/, when the extension dispatches it, then pi.sendUserMessage(text, { deliverAs: 'steer' }) is called, the file is unlinked, and an ack POST is sent to the dashboard.
- AC: Given pre-existing command files in control/ at session_start, when the extension starts, then it drains and dispatches that backlog before watching for new files (and the watcher is started only in session_start, never the module factory).
close_reason: Added the per-agent conversation control file-drop writer, wired both Pi extension packages to drain/watch/dispatch command files, unlink processed files, POST acks, and record input sources; targeted runtime and extension package tests pass.

title: pan-2088: WI-1: Widen the extension API types + add a runtime-capability probe (both packages)
description:
In packages/ohmypi-extension/src/index.ts (interface OhmypiExtensionAPI at :14) append OPTIONAL method/event declarations so the dispatcher can call them type-safely while a stale runtime still type-checks: add types `ThinkingLevel = 'off'|'minimal'|'low'|'medium'|'high'|'xhigh'`, `SendUserMessageOptions { deliverAs?: 'steer'|'followUp' }`, `InputEvent { source?: 'interactive'|'rpc'|'extension'; text?: string }`; add `on(event: 'input', handler)`, and optional members `sendUserMessage?(content, options?)`, `setThinkingLevel?(level)`, `getThinkingLevel?()`, `setModel?(model)`. Add a small capability probe helper that, given the live `omp`/`pi` object, reports which of these methods exist (typeof === 'function') so callers can fail-safe (log + no-op / 501) when a method is absent. Mirror the SAME widening verbatim in packages/pi-extension/src/index.ts — note it declares its OWN PiExtensionAPI interface at :13 (NOT the ohmypi alias), so widen that interface directly. Keep ohmypi-extension's `export type PiExtensionAPI = OhmypiExtensionAPI` alias (:23) intact. IMPLEMENTATION CHECKPOINT: confirm the INSTALLED omp/pi runtime actually exposes sendUserMessage, setThinkingLevel, setModel, and the 'input' event. FALLBACK if absent: bump the pinned runtime version; if still unavailable, the probe disables that command type (server returns 501 not-supported with a clear operator message) and message delivery falls back to the existing tmux path so conversations never hard-break.
- AC: Given a runtime object that exposes sendUserMessage, setThinkingLevel, and setModel, when the capability probe runs, then it reports each of those methods as supported.
- AC: Given a fake runtime missing setThinkingLevel, when a set_thinking_level command is dispatched, then the dispatcher no-ops (treats it as unsupported) and does not throw.
- AC: Given both extension packages, when npm run typecheck runs, then OhmypiExtensionAPI (ohmypi-extension) and the separate PiExtensionAPI (pi-extension) both expose the new optional members and the 'input' event with no type errors.
close_reason: Widened both pi/oh-my-pi extension API types, added runtime capability probes, and covered supported/unsupported thinking-level behavior with package tests.

title: pan-2044: Settings endpoints: legacy-import preview (GET) and import (POST)
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/settings.ts add two Effect HttpRouter.add routes following the existing pattern (GET example :780, POST with auth :806) and register both in settingsRouteLayer (:1078). GET /api/settings/legacy-import/conversations?path= : resolve path (default join(getLegacyHome(),'panopticon.db')); when the file is missing return jsonResponse({ found:false, defaultPath, message:`No legacy database found at ${path}` }); else return jsonResponse({ found:true, path, conversations: previewLegacyConversations(path) }). Parse the query param via new URL(request.url,'http://localhost').searchParams.get('path'). POST /api/settings/legacy-import/conversations : call rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest(request) first; read body via readJsonBody; call importLegacyConversations(path, names); return jsonResponse({ imported, skipped, failed, warnings, favoritesCarried }). Add a route-level test (fixture legacy DB + in-memory overdeck DB) asserting the GET preview list and the POST summary.
- AC: GET /api/settings/legacy-import/conversations returns { found:false, defaultPath, message } when no DB exists at the resolved path and { found:true, path, conversations } (via previewLegacyConversations) when one does; ?path= overrides the default join(getLegacyHome(),'panopticon.db').
- AC: POST /api/settings/legacy-import/conversations with body { path, names } calls importLegacyConversations and returns { imported, skipped, failed, warnings, favoritesCarried }.
- AC: The POST route calls rejectUnsafeDashboardMutationRequest(request) and returns its auth-error response when the dashboard CSRF token is absent, before any import runs.
- AC: Both routes are added to settingsRouteLayer in settings.ts and a route-level test exercises the GET preview against a fixture path and the POST import summary.
close_reason: Added GET /api/settings/legacy-import/conversations (preview with ?path= override, found:false for missing DB) and POST (CSRF-gated, delegates to importLegacyConversations, returns ImportResult) to settings.ts. Both registered in settingsRouteLayer. 5/5 route-contract tests pass.

title: pan-2044: Non-destructive import write door + two-pass orchestration + favorites
description:
Add to src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts (the write door): (1) importLegacyConversation(mapped) — a NON-destructive insert that mints a fresh randomUUID(), inserts the full mapped column set (created_at ms, archived_at, status [null→derive], ended_at, last_attached_at, total_cost, total_tokens, fork_status, fork_retry_count, session_file, title, title_source, delivery_method, tmux_session, spawn_error, handoff_doc_path) with FK columns NULL, and — when claudeSessionId is present — inserts the conversation_files locator row (reuse the existing `INSERT OR IGNORE INTO conversation_files (conversation_id, harness, locator, created_at)` shape from :1196-1201). It must NOT DELETE any existing row. Returns { uuid, legacyRowid }. (2) setImportedConversationLinks(uuid, { handoffTargetUuid, clearedToUuid }) — UPDATE conversations SET handoff_target_conv_id=?, cleared_to_conv_id=? WHERE id=?. Then in src/lib/overdeck/legacy-import.ts add importLegacyConversations(path, names): read the selected legacy rows (reuse the read helper from legacy-import-read), map legacy→new per the PRD mapping table (parse ISO TEXT → epoch ms via new Date(iso).getTime()), and run two passes — pass 1 inserts via importLegacyConversation building a { legacyRowid → newUuid } map and skipping any name already present (by name, then by claude_session_id via getConversationByClaudeSessionId, conversations.ts:961); pass 2 calls setImportedConversationLinks remapping legacy rowid FKs to new UUIDs (NULL + warning when the target was not imported). Carry favorites: for each imported conversation whose name has a legacy type='conversation' favorite, call setFavorite('conversation', name) (conversations.ts:1391). A row with empty/unparseable created_at goes to failed[] with a reason and is not inserted. Return { imported: string[], skipped: {name,reason}[], failed: {name,reason}[], warnings: {name,reason}[], favoritesCarried: number }. Tests use a fixture legacy DB plus an in-memory overdeck DB (initSchema).
- AC: conversations.ts exports a non-destructive importLegacyConversation(mapped) that inserts without deleting any existing row and registers a conversation_files locator when claudeSessionId is present; a fixture test asserts created_at (ISO→ms), archived_at, status, ended_at, total_cost, total_tokens, title, title_source round-trip to the new row and the conversation_files locator equals the legacy claude_session_id.
- AC: importLegacyConversations skips and reports (in skipped[]) any selected name already present in overdeck.db (matched by name, or by claude_session_id via getConversationByClaudeSessionId) — no duplicate row, no overwrite; a test pre-creates a same-named conversation and asserts it is unchanged after import.
- AC: The import path preserves existing overdeck rows: it issues no DELETE against the conversations table and does not route through createConversation (verified by a test and/or a grep over the import module).
- AC: handoff_target_conv_id and cleared_to_conv_id are remapped from legacy rowids to the imported targets' new UUIDs when those targets are also imported, and set NULL with a per-row warning when the target was not imported — a fixture test covers both branches.
- AC: A legacy row with an empty or unparseable created_at fails that row with a recorded reason in failed[], and no zero-timestamp row is inserted into overdeck.db.
- AC: For each imported conversation whose name matches a legacy type='conversation' favorite, the import creates a favorite via setFavorite and favoritesCarried records the count; legacy favorites of other types are ignored — fixture test.
close_reason: Added importLegacyConversation + setImportedConversationLinks to conversations.ts (non-destructive INSERT OR IGNORE, conversation_files locator, FK columns NULL). Added importLegacyConversations to legacy-import.ts with two-pass FK remap, skip-by-name and claude_session_id, bad-date fail path, favorites carry. 8/8 fixture tests pass covering all ACs.

metadata.acJustification: This is one cohesive write-door change — the non-destructive insert, full column mapping, idempotency-not-DELETE, two-pass FK remap, and favorites carry-over are interdependent and cannot be reviewed or merged in working intermediate slices; each AC pins a distinct observable behavior of that single change.

title: pan-2044: Read-only legacy-conversation preview module
description:
Create src/lib/overdeck/legacy-import.ts exporting previewLegacyConversations(path). It opens the legacy DB via openDatabase(path, { readOnly: true }) on its OWN handle (never getDatabase()/getOverdeckDatabaseSync()), reads the legacy `conversations` table (DDL at src/lib/database/schema.ts:471), excludes every name matched by isAgentConversationName (conversations.ts:797 — agent-/planning-/specialist-), and returns PreviewRow[] = { name, title, createdAt, model, lastActivityAt|null, messageCount|null, hasFavorite, claudeSessionId|null, alreadyImported }. hasFavorite is derived by reading the legacy `favorites` table (schema.ts:516) for type='conversation' item_id=name. alreadyImported is true when getConversationUuidByName(name) (conversations.ts:916) returns a row. Provide a not-found result shape (no throw) when the path is missing, so the endpoint can render AC2. Close the legacy handle when done. Add a fixture-based unit test that builds a temp legacy DB from the legacy DDL, seeds agent and non-agent rows + a favorite, and asserts the preview shape and exclusion.
- AC: src/lib/overdeck/legacy-import.ts exports previewLegacyConversations(path) that opens the legacy DB via openDatabase(path, { readOnly: true }) on its own handle and never calls getDatabase()/getOverdeckDatabaseSync().

title: pan-1934: Escalate (pause + stuck) on the failure path instead of looping; make the pre-run guard sticky
description:
In src/lib/cloister/verification-runner.ts: (1) add 'escalated' to the VerificationRunnerOutcome union as { outcome: 'escalated'; failedCheck: string; cycleCount: number; maxCycles: number }. (2) Extract a shared async helper handleVerificationFailure({ issueId, workspacePath, failedCheck, summary, retryFeedbackBody }) used by all four failure branches (sync-target :224, quality-gate :352, vbrief-conflicts :399, vbrief-ac :433). It reads prev = getReviewStatusSync(issueId), computes newCycleCount = (prev?.verificationCycleCount ?? 0) + 1, calls decideVerificationDisposition({ newCycleCount, failedCheck, lastFailedCheck: prev?.verificationLastFailedCheck }), and persists verificationCycleCount + verificationLastFailedCheck. On 'retry' it keeps today's behaviour (verificationStatus:'failed', writeFeedbackFile with the retry body, messageAgent, return { outcome:'failed', ... }). On 'escalate' it sets verificationStatus:'escalated'; writes a feedback file whose body instructs the agent to STOP (it must NOT contain the phrase 'do NOT stop'); calls markWorkspaceStuck(issueId, 'verification_unfixable', { failedCheck, cycleCount: newCycleCount }); then setAgentPaused(agent-<issueId-lowercase>, reason, true) and stopAgent(agent-<issueId-lowercase>) via Effect.runPromise (the async primitives from agents.ts - NEVER stopAgentSync); any messageAgent is best-effort in try/catch and runs before stopAgent; returns { outcome:'escalated', failedCheck, cycleCount:newCycleCount, maxCycles:VERIFICATION_MAX_CYCLES }. (3) Repurpose the pre-run guard (:192-199): when prev.verificationStatus === 'escalated' OR (prev?.verificationCycleCount ?? 0) >= VERIFICATION_MAX_CYCLES, return { outcome:'escalated', ... } without running quality gates (replaces the old { outcome:'skipped' }). Update tests/cloister/verification-runner.test.ts: change the circuit-breaker test to expect 'escalated'; add markWorkspaceStuck to the review-status.js mock and setAgentPaused+stopAgent to the agents.js mock; add a no-progress test (same 'test' failure on cycle 2 -> escalated) and a first-failure test (cycle 1 -> 'failed', no pause/stop).
- AC: VerificationRunnerOutcome includes an outcome 'escalated' variant carrying failedCheck, cycleCount and maxCycles, returned when escalation fires.
- AC: When the same gate fails on the second consecutive cycle, runVerificationForIssue returns outcome escalated and the runner calls markWorkspaceStuck, setAgentPaused, and stopAgent (asserted via mocks).
- AC: The escalation feedback file body instructs the agent to STOP and contains no occurrence of the phrase Do NOT stop.
- AC: The pre-run guard returns outcome escalated (not skipped) and does not call runQualityGates when verificationCycleCount >= VERIFICATION_MAX_CYCLES or verificationStatus is already escalated.
- AC: A single first-time failure (cycle 1, no prior failed check) returns outcome failed and does NOT call setAgentPaused or stopAgent.
- AC: The verification-runner pause path imports only the async stopAgent and setAgentPaused from agents.js, and a grep over the file produces no match for stopAgentSync.

metadata.acJustification: This is the single cohesive behavioral change (escalation handler + the four converted failure branches + the sticky pre-run guard); its six ACs each pin a distinct observable behavior of that one change and splitting it would leave an inconsistent intermediate (some branches escalating, others still looping).

src/lib/vbrief/dag.ts mirrorTaskOperationToContinueFile (:867-929) currently reads/writes the workspace .pan/continue.json via readWorkspaceContinue/writeWorkspaceContinue (lines 875, 904), so the async dashboard DAG path disagrees with the sync io.ts path that writes statusOverrides to the record. Reroute it to persist statusOverrides to the per-issue record via the async writeStatusOverride (preserve the Effect boundary — wrap the sync record writer in Effect.try if needed). Drop the now-unused readWorkspaceContinue/writeWorkspaceContinue import from dag.ts. Then remove 'dag.ts' from the guard's CONTINUE_EXCLUDES.
- AC: After a DAG task operation, the bead status override is persisted into .pan/records/<issue>.json and the workspace .pan/continue.json is not written
- AC: Given both the sync (io.ts updateItemStatus) and async (dag.ts mirror) paths run, then the record statusOverrides map contains a single consistent set of overrides
- AC: dag.ts is removed from CONTINUE_EXCLUDES and scripts/lint-state-writes.sh exits 0 with no legacy warning for dag.ts
close_reason: Closed

description:
Reroute the five project-continue adapters in src/lib/vbrief/lifecycle-io.ts — readContinueStateForIssue (:482), writeContinueStateForIssue (:493), appendContinueSessionEntryForIssue (:501), appendFeedbackEntryForIssue (:509), clearFeedbackForIssue (:517) — to read/write the per-issue record via rec-helpers (readRecordContinueViewSync, record.appendSessionEntry, record.appendFeedbackEntry, the new decisions/hazards setters) instead of continue-state.ts. This transparently cuts over every project-continue caller: src/lib/agents.ts:4819, src/lib/reopen.ts:100, src/dashboard/server/routes/issues.ts:2100, and src/lib/cloister/feedback-writer.ts:74/115/145/160 (clear/read/append structured feedback). Then remove 'lifecycle-io.ts' and 'continue-state.ts' from CONTINUE_EXCLUDES in scripts/lint-state-writes.sh (the structured-feedback/session writes now go to the record). Keep promoteContinueToProject untouched here (retired in retire-legacy-continues).
- AC: Calling appendContinueSessionEntryForIssue or appendFeedbackEntryForIssue persists the entry to the per-issue record (record.sessionHistory / record.feedback) and stores nothing in .pan/continues/<issue>.vbrief.json

- AC: lifecycle-io.ts and continue-state.ts are removed from CONTINUE_EXCLUDES and scripts/lint-state-writes.sh exits 0 with no legacy warning for either file

title: pan-1919: rebuild-agents reads harness/model from the record (state.json no longer the source)
description:
In src/lib/database/agent-backfill.ts (the backfillAgentsFromStateJsonSync path behind pan admin db rebuild-agents, ~:167-233), prefer the per-issue record for harness/model: when a record exists for the agent's issue, use record.harness/record.model; fall back to the state.json values only when the record lacks them. This makes the agents-table rebuild source harness/model from the travelling record rather than machine-local state.json (the last state.json-as-source read for these fields). Live lifecycle reads are already cut over via getAgentStateSync (agents.ts:1095-1097).
- AC: When a per-issue record carries harness/model, pan admin db rebuild-agents produces an agents-table row using the record's harness/model
- AC: When no record exists or it lacks harness/model, the rebuild falls back to the state.json values (no regression for pre-record agents)
- AC: Given a record harness/model differing from state.json, then the rebuild produces an agents-table row that uses the record value

title: pan-1919: Add record read-view + decisions/hazards/resumePoint/beadsMapping writers (foundation)
description:

These are the cross-cutting contract the cutover beads encode assumptions about — keep names/signatures stable. record.ts is already on the lint approved-writer allowlist, so raw fs primitives are permitted here.
