title: pan-1832: RolesPanel: single↔distribution toggle and weighted-rows editor for top-level roles
description:
Extend RolesPanel.tsx (top-level roles only) with a 'Single model' ↔ 'Distribution' toggle. Distribution mode renders a list of rows, each = the existing ModelPicker (for the entry model) + a positive-integer weight input + a remove button, plus an 'Add model' button and a live computed percentage per row (weight / sum). Saving sends model as WeightedModelRef[] through the existing PUT /api/settings (saveRoleConfig). Toggling back to single sends a scalar ModelRef. Sub-role pickers remain single-model only (no toggle). Add helper text stating weights are relative and each spawn is distributed statistically. Follow pan-style-guide: reuse the existing select/input classes, muted text, no pill badges, no decorative color.
- AC: Toggling a top-level role to 'Distribution' shows editable weighted rows (model select + weight input + remove button).
- AC: 'Add model' appends a row, 'remove' deletes a row, and editing a weight updates the displayed percentage live.
- AC: Saving in distribution mode persists model as a WeightedModelRef[] via PUT; toggling back to single persists a scalar ModelRef.
- AC: Each sub-role picker shows only the single-model dropdown and displays no distribution toggle.
- AC: The panel displays helper text explaining relative weights and per-spawn statistical distribution.
close_reason: Closed

title: pan-1832: Thread a per-spawn sampling key into the role-level spawn paths
description:
Add an optional `spawnKey?: string` to determineModel({model, role, spawnKey}) in src/lib/agents.ts (~:2791) and pass it into resolveModel(role, undefined, config, spawnKey). Thread `${role}:${issueId}` from the role-level spawn sites: determineModel callers at routes/agents.ts:2981 (dashboard start), agents.ts:3308 (spawnRun), sequencer-agent.ts:53; plus the direct role-level resolveModel calls at spawn-planning-session.ts:553 (plan), review-agent.ts:306 (only when opts.subRole is undefined — the review orchestrator), and specialist-context.ts:128 (when subRole undefined). Do NOT add a key to display/router callers (router-config.ts, misc.ts, specialists.ts, flywheel.ts, flywheel-actions.ts) — they intentionally get the representative. Preserve the sample-once invariant: determineModel returns a non-empty `model` override unchanged, so downstream re-entry (runtimes/claude-code.ts:350) and restart/resume (agents.ts:3637) must pass the already-persisted concrete model, never re-resolve from scratch.
- AC: determineModel({role:'work', spawnKey}) with a work distribution returns the same model for the same key and can return different models for different keys.
- AC: Each enumerated role-level spawn site passes a `${role}:${issueId}` spawnKey into resolveModel/determineModel (visible in the diff at each call site).
- AC: determineModel returns a concrete `model` override unchanged — never resampling it — locking the sample-once invariant.
- AC: On restart/resume the restart path passes the persisted state.json model as the override, so resolveModel returns it without resampling.
- AC: The harness for a sampled spawn is resolved from the sampled model (resolveHarness receives the concrete sampled model, so a work distribution can yield mixed harnesses across agents).
close_reason: Closed

title: pan-1832: RolesPanel: accept and display a distribution (read-through, no editor yet)
description:
In src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/Settings/RolesPanel.tsx add local types `WeightedModelRef { model: ModelRef; weight: number }` and `RoleModelRef = ModelRef | WeightedModelRef[]`; widen RoleConfig.model and RoleConfigPatch.model to RoleModelRef. Update getRoleModel to return RoleModelRef and saveRoleConfig to accept an array model. When a top-level role's model is an array, render a distribution SUMMARY chip (e.g. '70% kimi-k2.7-code / 30% gpt-5.5', percentages computed from relative weights) instead of feeding the array to the single-select ModelPicker (which must not receive an array). Single-model roles and all sub-role pickers render exactly as today. This bead is display/read-through only; the editor is the next bead.

- AC: A single-model role renders unchanged (existing dropdown + 'Default:' chip).
- AC: npm run typecheck produces no new errors with getRoleModel returning and saveRoleConfig accepting WeightedModelRef[].

title: pan-1832: Extend settings-api validateModelRef to the distribution form (roles only)
description:
In src/lib/settings-api.ts add an `allowDistribution = false` parameter to validateModelRef (~:417). When ref is an array AND allowDistribution: require non-empty, each entry weight a positive integer, and recurse the existing scalar checks on each entry.model (reusing allowWorkhorseRef). When ref is an array and NOT allowDistribution: push a 'distribution not allowed here' error. Pass allowDistribution=true ONLY at the roles.<role>.model call (~:531); workhorses (~:511) and sub-roles (~:563) keep false. Extend the model-aware effort check (~:534-547): when the model is a distribution, the role effort must be supported by EVERY entry's resolved model (resolveModelRefToId per entry); reject otherwise.
- AC: PUT /api/settings with a valid roles.work.model distribution returns success and persists the array to config.
- AC: The settings API rejects a distribution with a non-positive/non-integer weight, an invalid model ref, or an empty list, with a descriptive validation error.
- AC: The settings API rejects a distribution placed on a sub-role model or a workhorse slot (allowDistribution is false there).
- AC: The settings API rejects a role-level effort that is not supported by at least one model in the distribution.
- AC: A scalar model ref still validates exactly as before (no regression).

title: pan-1832: Validate the distribution form at config load and preserve it across merge
description:
In src/lib/config-yaml.ts validateRoleFields(role, roleConfig) (load path ~:1711): when roleConfig.model is an array, require a non-empty list where every entry is { model: non-empty string, weight: positive integer }; throw a precise `config.yaml: roles.<role>.model[<i>].weight …` error otherwise. Arrays are valid ONLY for the top-level role model — reject array-shaped sub-role/workhorse models. Confirm mergeRoleConfig (~:1658) and cloneRoles (~:1478) replace the `model` key wholesale (spread already does this); defensively clone the array in cloneRoles so a later mutation cannot alias the merged config.
- AC: loadConfig accepts a valid roles.work.model distribution and resolveModel returns the array's sampled model unchanged.
- AC: An empty distribution array for a role model throws a field-path config-load error.
- AC: config load rejects a distribution entry whose weight is 0, negative, or non-integer, with a precise field-path error.
- AC: An existing scalar role-model config still loads and resolves unchanged.

title: pan-1832: Extend resolveModel to sample an array role model by spawnKey
description:
In src/lib/config-yaml.ts add an optional `spawnKey?: string` parameter to `resolveModel(role, subRole?, config, spawnKey?)`. After computing `ref = subModel ?? roleModel ?? DEFAULT_MODEL_REFS[role]`: if `ref` is an array, choose `pickWeightedModelRef(ref, spawnKey)` when spawnKey is provided else `representativeModelRef(ref)`, then `derefWorkhorse(picked, config, fieldPath)`. Scalar refs are unchanged. Because subModel (a sub-role's scalar model) takes precedence, a sub-role resolve never reaches the array branch. derefWorkhorse still resolves workhorse refs inside picked entries.
- AC: resolveModel('work', undefined, config, key) with an array role model returns the derefed model id of the entry sampled by that key.
- AC: resolveModel('work', undefined, config) WITHOUT a spawnKey, with an array role model, returns the representative (highest-weight) model — deterministic for display/router paths.
- AC: A scalar role model resolves to exactly the same model id as before, with or without a spawnKey (back-compat preserved).
- AC: resolveModel('work', 'inspect', config, key) returns the sub-role's scalar model and never samples (sub-role precedence holds even when the parent role model is an array).
- AC: resolveModel resolves a workhorse ref (e.g. workhorse:mid) used as a distribution entry to its concrete model id after sampling.
close_reason: Closed

title: pan-1832: Add WeightedModelRef/RoleModelRef types and the deterministic weighted sampler
description:
In src/lib/config-yaml.ts add `interface WeightedModelRef { model: ModelRef; weight: number }` and `type RoleModelRef = ModelRef | WeightedModelRef[]`, and change `RoleConfig.model` to `RoleModelRef`. Add pure helpers: `fnv1a32(s: string): number` (32-bit FNV-1a, no Math.random/Date.now), `pickWeightedModelRef(entries, spawnKey): ModelRef` (relative weights: hash mod sum-of-positive-weights → cumulative band; throws if no positive weight), and `representativeModelRef(entries): ModelRef` (highest weight, first on tie). No call-site behavior change yet — this bead only adds the types + helpers and their unit tests. Defaults (DEFAULT_MODEL_REFS, DEFAULT_ROLES) stay scalar. RoleSubConfig.model stays ModelRef (scalar).
- AC: pickWeightedModelRef returns the SAME model for a given spawnKey on repeated calls (deterministic), and the type change compiles.
- AC: Over 1000 distinct keys, pickWeightedModelRef on [{a,70},{b,30}] produces counts within ±5 percentage points of 70/30 (realizes the intended ratio).
- AC: pickWeightedModelRef returns identical per-key picks for [{a,7},{b,3}] and [{a,70},{b,30}] — weights are proportional, not sum=100.
- AC: representativeModelRef returns the highest-weight entry's model (first entry on a weight tie).
- AC: pickWeightedModelRef throws when given a list whose entries all have weight <= 0 (no silent default).
close_reason: Closed

title: pan-1982: Add per-issue reviewMode field and the single resolveReviewMode helper behind isExtendedReviewEnabled(issueId?)
description:
Add `reviewMode?: 'quick' | 'full'` to the PanIssueRecord interface (src/lib/pan-dir/record.ts:99-122). Add ONE synchronous resolver resolveReviewMode(issueId?: string): 'quick' | 'full' that resolves per-issue (readIssueRecordSync(...).reviewMode) -> project/global (loadConfigSync().config.roles.review.mode) -> 'quick'. Change isExtendedReviewEnabled() (review-agent.ts:885) to isExtendedReviewEnabled(issueId?: string): boolean returning resolveReviewMode(issueId) === 'full'. The helper must stay synchronous and is the single source of mode truth; the per-issue read goes through the readIssueRecordSync door only. This bead is the foundation the spawn branch, dashboard gate, and CLI setter build on, so the contract (signature, resolution order, sync-only, single-helper) is what the inspector verifies.
- AC: Given an issue with no per-issue reviewMode and no config override, resolveReviewMode returns 'quick' and isExtendedReviewEnabled(issueId) returns false
- AC: Given a per-issue record with reviewMode 'full' while project and global resolve to 'quick', resolveReviewMode returns 'full' and isExtendedReviewEnabled(issueId) returns true (per-issue beats project and global)
- AC: Given global config roles.review.mode 'full' and no per-issue override, isExtendedReviewEnabled(issueId) returns true
- AC: isExtendedReviewEnabled returns its boolean synchronously and resolveReviewMode reads config and the per-issue record through loadConfigSync and readIssueRecordSync with no async I/O
close_reason: Added PanIssueRecord.reviewMode, synchronous resolveReviewMode(issueId) using readIssueRecordSync before loadConfigSync, wired isExtendedReviewEnabled(issueId), and covered default/config/per-issue precedence with focused tests plus typecheck.

title: pan-1982: Add roles.review.mode (quick|full) config field with global+project resolution

title: pan-1866: Tiered rendering + filters for a 500+ issue backlog
description:
Add tiered rendering + filters to the Backlog page so a 500+ backlog stays usable. Default to a top-tier view: top N + dependency neighbors + always the pinned/in-pipeline set. Render as a DAG up to a ~150-node budget; beyond it, fall back to a virtualized ranked list. Collapse the long tail behind a visible count. Add filters for importance, condition, in-pipeline, and ready. Tiers (Now/Next/Later/Someday) are DERIVED bands over rank/score, not AI-assigned.

title: pan-1951: Implement three-path warm dispatch: cold, resume-same-model, cold-on-model-change
description:
In `src/lib/cloister/inspect-agent.ts`, rewrite the dispatch block of `spawnInspectAgentPromise` (lines 161–221) to implement three paths. Before the existing `sessionExists` check, add: `const priorState = getAgentRuntimeStateSync(tmuxSession)`. Then compute: `const canResume = priorState?.claudeSessionId != null && priorState?.sessionModel === model`. Replace the always-cold spawn with: if `canResume` → use `buildInspectContinuationPrompt(context)` for the prompt and pass `resumeSessionId: priorState!.claudeSessionId!` to `generateLauncherScriptSync`; if not `canResume` → use `buildInspectPrompt(context)` (existing) and pass `sessionId: randomUUID()` (existing behavior). The `launcherSessionId` local variable (the UUID to save in runtime.json and to return as `runId`) is `priorState!.claudeSessionId!` on resume or the new `randomUUID()` on cold. The `killSession` call stays but moves before the `canResume` check — we always kill the existing dead-pane session before creating a fresh tmux session (whether resuming Claude's JSONL or not). The `createSession`, `setOption`, and `saveAgentRuntimeState` calls are unchanged structurally, now using `launcherSessionId`. In `src/lib/cloister/__tests__/inspect-agent.test.ts`, add three new describe('warm dispatch') tests: (1) 'cold spawns when no prior state' — `getAgentRuntimeStateSync` returns null → `generateLauncherScriptSync` receives object with key `sessionId` but not `resumeSessionId`; (2) 'resumes when prior state has same model' — `getAgentRuntimeStateSync` returns `{ claudeSessionId: 'uuid-1', sessionModel: 'claude-sonnet-4-6' }`, `resolveModel` returns `'claude-sonnet-4-6'` → `generateLauncherScriptSync` receives object with key `resumeSessionId: 'uuid-1'` and `runId` in result is `'uuid-1'`; (3) 'cold spawns on model change' — prior `sessionModel: 'claude-opus-4-8'`, current `'claude-sonnet-4-6'` → `generateLauncherScriptSync` receives object with key `sessionId` (new UUID, not `'uuid-1'`).
- AC: With no prior state, generateLauncherScriptSync receives { sessionId: <new-uuid> } (cold path; no resumeSessionId key)
- AC: With prior state { claudeSessionId: 'uuid-1', sessionModel: 'claude-sonnet-4-6' } and current model 'claude-sonnet-4-6', generateLauncherScriptSync receives { resumeSessionId: 'uuid-1' } and result.runId is 'uuid-1'
- AC: With prior state { sessionModel: 'claude-opus-4-8' } and current model 'claude-sonnet-4-6', generateLauncherScriptSync receives { sessionId: <new-uuid> } (model-change forces cold spawn)
- AC: On resume path, buildInspectContinuationPrompt is used (result prompt does NOT contain '# Inspect Specialist' header); on cold path, buildInspectPrompt is used (result prompt contains '# Inspect Specialist')

title: pan-1951: Update deacon crash watchdog to use isPaneDead for remain-on-exit sessions
description:
In `src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts`, add `isPaneDead` to the tmux.ts import (near the top of the file where `sessionExists` is imported). In `checkInspectAgentTimeouts` (lines 747–750), replace the crash detection logic with: `const sessionName = inspectSessionName(issueId)` (now always defined, no `beadId` needed; `inspectSessionName` was already changed by bead `per-issue-session-naming`). Then: `const sessionExists_ = await Effect.runPromise(sessionExists(sessionName)).catch(() => false)`. Then: `const paneDead = sessionExists_ ? await Effect.runPromise(isPaneDead(sessionName)).catch(() => false) : false`. Then: `const sessionAlive = sessionExists_ && !paneDead`. Then: `const crashed = !sessionAlive`. The `if (!timedOut && !crashed) continue` check (line 752) and all downstream logic (kill, notify, log) remain unchanged. Also update the `if (sessionName && sessionAlive)` guard at line 770 to just `if (sessionAlive)` (sessionName is always truthy now). Add tests in `src/lib/cloister/__tests__/inspect-agent.test.ts` or a new `deacon-inspect-timeout.test.ts`: (1) 'treats pane-dead session as crashed during inspection' — mock `sessionExists=Effect.succeed(true)`, `isPaneDead=Effect.succeed(true)`, `inspectStatus='inspecting'` → watchdog action is produced; (2) 'does not treat live-running session as crashed' — `sessionExists=true`, `isPaneDead=false` → no watchdog action; (3) 'treats missing session as crashed' — `sessionExists=false` → watchdog action.
- AC: checkInspectAgentTimeouts fires the watchdog when sessionExists=true and isPaneDead=true (remain-on-exit dead pane) while inspectStatus='inspecting'
- AC: checkInspectAgentTimeouts does NOT fire the watchdog when sessionExists=true and isPaneDead=false (inspector still running) while inspectStatus='inspecting'
- AC: checkInspectAgentTimeouts fires the watchdog when sessionExists=false (session gone entirely) while inspectStatus='inspecting'

Add a round-trip test (here or in verdict-restore.test.ts): seed full verdicts into review_status, mirror them to a record fixture, deleteReviewStatus(issueId) to clear the cache, run restoreReviewStatusFromRecords({issueId}), then assert every durable column returns to its pre-clear value, every ephemeral column is at its schema default, and ready_for_merge is re-derived consistently with the gate. - AC: Given the live review_status schema, when the audit test enumerates columns via PRAGMA table_info, then it asserts every column is classified into exactly one of DURABLE, DERIVED or EPHEMERAL and fails closed naming any unclassified column.

title: pan-1922: Re-derive PR-owned merge-state live during restore via refreshMergeStateFromGitHub()

Wrap the call in try/catch per issue: a GitHub read failure (offline, missing gh auth, deleted or merged PR) must not fail the whole restore — log and continue, leaving the durable verdicts already restored. refreshMergeStateFromGitHub is already async and uses execFileAsync, so no execSync is introduced (NFR-3).

title: pan-1922: restoreReviewStatusFromRecords(): rebuild durable review_status columns from the per-issue record
description:
Create new file src/lib/pan-dir/verdict-restore.ts exporting async restoreReviewStatusFromRecords(options?: RestoreVerdictsOptions): Promise<RestoreVerdictsResult>, modelled on backfillIssueRecords() in records-backfill.ts. First export the currently-private collectInFlightIssueIds() from records-backfill.ts (change 'async function' to 'export async function') and reuse it for the issue set when no issueId is given. For each target issue: resolve the project, call readIssueRecord(); if there is no record or no record.pipeline, push {action:'skipped'} and continue (FR-6). Otherwise map record.pipeline (PanIssuePipelineRecord) to a Partial<ReviewStatus> containing ONLY the durable columns listed in PRD section 4 — do NOT copy blockerReasons (refreshed live in blocker-refresh) and do NOT copy readyForMerge (recomputed). Write via setReviewStatusSync(issueId, durableUpdate) on purpose: it recomputes ready_for_merge, re-fires the harmless idempotent PAN-1908 mirror, and seeds ephemeral columns at schema defaults via the upsert. Under dryRun, tally without writing. Return {restored, skipped, failed, details}. Surgical: do not refactor records-backfill.ts beyond the one export, and do not touch getReviewStatusSync or the mirror write path.
- AC: Given a per-issue record with pipeline verdicts and an absent review_status row, when restoreReviewStatusFromRecords({issueId}) runs, then the durable columns (review_status, test_status, merge_status, inspect_status, inspect_notes, verification_status, verification_notes, review_notes, test_notes, merge_notes, pr_url, pr_number, pr_head_sha, reviewed_at_commit, last_verified_commit, auto_merge, deacon_ignored, deacon_ignored_at, deacon_ignored_reason) match the record values.
- AC: Given the same record, when restore runs twice, then both runs produce identical durable columns (idempotent).
- AC: Given an issue with no per-issue record or no pipeline block, when restore runs, then it records the issue as skipped, returns without throwing, and creates no review_status row.
- AC: Given a record whose pipeline carries readyForMerge true and non-empty blockerReasons, when restore runs with no live GitHub call, then review_status.blocker_reasons defaults to empty and ready_for_merge is recomputed by the PAN-1650 gate rather than copied from the record.
- AC: Given restore completes for an issue, then the ephemeral counters merge_retry_count, verification_cycle_count, auto_requeue_count, review_retry_count, test_retry_count and stuck each default to their schema values.
- AC: Given a caller imports verdict-restore.ts, then restoreReviewStatusFromRecords accepts an optional RestoreVerdictsOptions and returns a Promise that resolves to a RestoreVerdictsResult with numeric restored, skipped and failed plus a details array.
close_reason: Implemented restoreReviewStatusFromRecords in src/lib/pan-dir/verdict-restore.ts, exported collectInFlightIssueIds, added unit tests (7 passing)

title: pan-1925: Emit agent.output_received stream-only via emitOnly() instead of persisting with appendAsync()
description:
In src/dashboard/server/services/agent-output-service.ts pollOnce() (lines 124-137), replace the persisting write `await eventStore.appendAsync(event as never)` (and its surrounding try/catch) with the in-memory-only `eventStore.emitOnly(event as never)`. emitOnly is synchronous, returns void, and does not throw, so remove the try/catch and the await. Add a short comment that terminal output is ephemeral (state model) and reconstructable from tmux. Update the producer test src/dashboard/server/services/__tests__/agent-output-service.test.ts to mock `emitOnly` instead of `appendAsync` and update every assertion (mockEmitOnly called/not-called, event type/payload). Verified end-to-end: streamEvents (domain-services.ts:280) is backed by store.subscribe(), so emitOnly still feeds RPC subscribeAgentOutput (ws-rpc.ts:627), subscribeIssueEvents, the SSE live tail, and the frontend god view; the reducer (event-reducers.ts:534) and frontend recoveryCoordinator (recoveryCoordinator.ts:72-75) already handle sequence -1.
- AC: pollOnce emits agent.output_received via eventStore.emitOnly() and never calls appendAsync() for this event
- AC: The emitted event preserves type 'agent.output_received' and payload { agentId, lines } (the diffed new lines)
- AC: pollOnce persists no agent.output_received row to the events table — zero durable writes while agents produce output
- AC: Updated producer test asserts emitOnly is called (and appendAsync is not) for new lines, is not called when output is unchanged, and is not called for non-tmuxActive agents; npm test passes

title: pan-1925: SSE: omit id: for in-memory-only (sequence < 0) frames; document agent.output_received as live-only
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/events.ts formatFrame() (lines 84-92), only include the SSE `id: <sequence>` line when event.sequence >= 0; emit no id: line for sequence < 0 (emitOnly events carry sequence -1). Per the SSE spec, omitting id: leaves the client's Last-Event-ID unchanged, so a live-only agent.output_received frame can no longer disable replay for other event types on the same connection (the replay guard at events.ts:177 requires since >= 0). Persisted rows are AUTOINCREMENT >= 1, so real-event resume is unaffected. Update docs/EXTERNAL-EVENT-STREAM.md: change the agent.output_received catalog row (line 99) and/or the Retention & Replay section to mark it live-only — streamed in real time but not persisted, so ?since=/Last-Event-ID replay will NOT include it. Add a unit test for formatFrame covering sequence -1 (no id: line) and sequence >= 1 (id: line present).
- AC: formatFrame produces an SSE frame with no 'id:' line when sequence < 0, and a frame with 'id: <sequence>' when sequence >= 0 (unit test covers both branches)
- AC: Live SSE consumers still receive agent.output_received frames over /events/stream (the event remains in PUBLIC_CATALOG and passes matchesFilter)
- AC: docs/EXTERNAL-EVENT-STREAM.md marks agent.output_received as live-only — streamed live but not persisted/replayable via ?since= or Last-Event-ID
close_reason: Omitted SSE id: line for sequence < 0 in formatFrame; updated EXTERNAL-EVENT-STREAM.md to mark agent.output_received live-only; added unit tests.

title: pan-1925: One-time startup purge of existing agent.output_received rows + immediate page reclamation
description:
In src/dashboard/server/event-store.ts initEventStore(), inside the .then((db) => …) after the existing issues.snapshot purge (~line 381), add `const purgedOutput = store.purgeType('agent.output_received');` and, when purgedOutput > 0, log the count and run `db.exec('PRAGMA incremental_vacuum')` inside a try/catch (non-fatal; the 15-min periodic reclaimer in src/lib/database/index.ts is the backstop). The purge is safe to run unconditionally — purgeType is a no-op (0 rows) once the poller no longer persists. Do NOT add agent.output_received to the readFromStmt exclusion list at event-store.ts:187. Add a unit test that seeds agent.output_received rows in a temp event store, runs the purge path, and asserts the rows are deleted (count -> 0) and a second run deletes 0.
- AC: On startup, initEventStore deletes all pre-existing agent.output_received rows from the events table via purgeType('agent.output_received')
- AC: When rows were purged, PRAGMA incremental_vacuum runs so freed pages return to the OS (Node production path, auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL); wrapped so a pragma failure is non-fatal
- AC: Unit test: seeding agent.output_received rows then running the purge leaves 0 such rows; a second run deletes 0 (idempotent no-op)
- AC: Preserves the readFromStmt exclusion list at event-store.ts:187 unchanged — agent.output_received is NOT added and no per-type retention window is introduced
close_reason: Added startup purgeType('agent.output_received') in initEventStore with conditional PRAGMA incremental_vacuum; preserved readFromStmt exclusion list; added unit tests for purge idempotency and preservation of other types.

title: pan-1758: Document the server/LLM auto-merge convergence boundary
description:

title: pan-1758: Executor: process multiple due entries in PAN-1691 merge order
description:

Disjoint candidates flow first; conflicting ones serialize broadest-footprint first. No-op (no branch-diff git work) for 0 or 1 due entries. Inject the diff/order deps for tests.

- AC: Given two conflicting due entries with different footprints, when the tick runs the broadest-footprint entry is attempted first

title: pan-1758: Executor: resurrect stranded blocked/failed entries that are eligible again
description:
In the executor tick, before/alongside processing due entries, scan listProblemAutoMerges (status IN 'blocked','failed'). For each: skip if attempts >= the cap (genuinely stuck — leave for the LLM/PAN-1240 via auto-merge/problems); re-check isAutoMergeEligible; if eligible call resurrectStrandedAutoMerge(id, now) so this or the next tick merges it. Never touch 'cancelled' or 'merged'. This makes convergence deterministic and server-side, removing the dependence on a server restart or an LLM re-schedule (NFR-4). Use injected deps + fake timers in tests.
- AC: Given a 'blocked' entry whose issue is eligible again, when the tick runs the entry is resurrected to 'pending' and becomes due
- AC: Given a 'failed' entry at the attempt cap (attempts>=3), when the tick runs it is not resurrected and survives in the auto-merge/problems list
- AC: Given an operator-'cancelled' entry, when the tick runs it is never resurrected (cancel is preserved)
- AC: Given a 'blocked' entry that is still ineligible, when the tick runs it stays 'blocked' (no resurrection)

title: pan-1758: Executor: defer transient ineligibility with backoff; cap expensive merge failures at 3
description:
In tickAutoMergeExecutor (src/dashboard/server/services/auto-merge-executor.ts:68): when isAutoMergeEligible is ineligible, classify the code (classifier bead). If retryable: if the entry's age (now - scheduledAt) exceeds a staleness ceiling (e.g. STALE_CEILING_MS = 2h) markBlocked('stuck: ineligible over 2h') + surface stuck; otherwise deferPendingAutoMerge(now + DEFER_BACKOFF_MS) and DO NOT count it against the merge cap. If terminal: markBlocked(reason) as today. On the merge path, when triggerMerge returns success=false for a recoverable failure: increment attempts; if attempts < 3 requeueToPending(now + backoff); if attempts >= 3 markFailed + emit a 'stuck' activity entry (the announceFailure TTS already exists). Keep the executor single-flight; never spawn a review/test convoy (NFR-1). Inject deps for tests; per the repo rule ALL retry/backoff tests MUST use vi.useFakeTimers() + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync() (NFR-2).
- AC: Given a due pending entry that is transiently ineligible (e.g. checks_pending), when the tick runs the entry stays 'pending' with scheduledMergeAt pushed out and is not marked 'blocked' (fake timers)
- AC: Given a due pending entry with a terminal ineligibility (e.g. pr_closed), when the tick runs the entry is marked 'blocked'
- AC: Given an entry whose triggerMerge attempt fails recoverably, when the tick runs three times attempts reaches 3 and the entry is marked 'failed' and emits a stuck activity entry on the third failure
- AC: Given a transiently-ineligible entry older than the staleness ceiling, when the tick runs it is marked 'blocked' with a stuck reason (cheap retries are bounded)

title: pan-1862: Pure reviewersToRerun() helper implementing the quality-first changed domain map

'changed' (operator-confirmed Quality-first, continue.json D1) -> a reviewer is in scope if it blocked last cycle OR any of its prior-flagged files changed OR a changed file is in its DOMAIN, where: correctness domain = ALL changed files (always re-runs on any change); requirements domain = ALL changed files (always re-runs); security domain = changed paths matching security-sensitive patterns (auth, crypto/secrets, input parsing, network/http, dependency manifests e.g. package.json/bun.lock); performance domain = changed paths matching a small DOCUMENTED hot-path allowlist. When the mapping is ambiguous, INCLUDE the reviewer (fail-safe toward quality, NFR-1). Document the security/performance pattern sets inline next to the helper.
- AC: scope='all' returns all four sub-roles; scope='blockers' returns exactly the prior-blocked sub-roles
- AC: Given scope='changed' and any changed file, reviewersToRerun returns correctness and requirements (always included)
- AC: Under scope='changed', security is included when a changed path matches a security-sensitive pattern or a prior-flagged file changed; performance when a changed path matches the hot-path allowlist or a prior-flagged file changed

Add handleDiscoveryReady(issueId) (server) that: (1) confirms the parent is quiescent; (2) for each sub-role forks the parent via forkSession({ fullHistory:true, remainOnExit:true }) and delivers the review-<subRole>.md kickoff + 'context already loaded; write findings to <outputPath>; signal contract unchanged'; (3) wires the existing PAN-977 reviewer-exit signal contract so the still-alive parent synthesizes unchanged (FR-4). Record discoveryReadyAt/convoyLaunchedAt on the run for the TTL heuristic.
- AC: On 'full' first-cycle review, spawnReviewRoleForIssue spawns exactly one parent (review/discovery) session and does NOT spawn any convoy reviewer inline
- AC: Given a discovery-ready signal, the server spawns exactly four reviewer sessions forked from the parent's session id (full history) and preserves the parent session alive to synthesize

title: pan-1868: Fleet-level burn-rate guard (alert; optional brake)
description:

title: pan-1868: Auto-remediate harness-deadlock: restart on resolved provider-default harness
description:
In src/lib/cloister/cost-bleed.ts TRIP path, when config.auto_remediate is true AND the detected signature.kind === 'harness-deadlock', instead of leaving the agent in the troubled terminal state, resolve the provider-default harness via `await resolveHarness({ explicit: undefined, role: state.role, model: state.model })` (src/lib/harness-resolve.ts:62 — this enforces canUseHarnessSync, so NEVER hardcode 'pi'; NFR-4) and call `await restartAgent(agentId, { harness: resolvedHarness, message: <diagnosis + 'restarting on provider-default harness'> })` (src/lib/agents.ts:4959). Record remediation { attemptedAt, attempts } in cost-bleed-state and cap attempts at 1 (a second harness-deadlock detection for an agent that already has a remediation attempt must NOT restart again — H4 loop guard). Emit an activity entry naming old->new harness. Still pause/stop the agent before restart per restartAgent's own lifecycle; do not double-trouble after a successful remediation.
- AC: On a harness-deadlock trip with auto_remediate=true, the patrol spawns a restart (restartAgent) using the harness resolveHarness({explicit:undefined,...}) returns, and the agent is not left in the troubled terminal state.
- AC: With auto_remediate=false, a harness-deadlock trip marks the agent troubled and refuses to call restartAgent.

title: pan-1868: Create costBleedMonitor patrol (warn/trip state machine) and wire into runPatrol
description:
Create src/lib/cloister/cost-bleed.ts exporting `async function costBleedMonitor(opts?: { now?: number; config?: CostBleedConfig; agents?: AgentState[] }): Promise<string[]>`. Default now=Date.now(), config=loadCloisterConfigSync().cost_bleed ?? DEFAULT_CLOISTER_CONFIG.cost_bleed, agents=listRunningAgentsSync(). If config.enabled is false, return []. For each running agent: skip remote agents (location:'remote') and agents already paused/troubled/stopped or already in stage 'tripped'. Build the current sample (cumulativeCostUsd via sampleAgentCostUsd, headSha via readWorkspaceHeadSha(workspace), lastActivity) and appendSample(state, sample, config.sample_window_count). Compute burnRate (computeBurnRateUsdPerMin) and progress (evaluateProgress vs the prior sample). Scan the tmux tail via the async capturePane(agentId, 80) and detectDeadlockSignature(tail, { harness, model }). Decide: TRIP when signature.kind !== null OR (no progress AND cost accrued since firstFlaggedAt >= config.trip_usd AND elapsed since firstFlaggedAt >= no_progress_minutes); else WARN when burnRate >= warn_usd_per_min AND !progress (set firstFlaggedAt if unset); else reset stage to 'none' and clearCostBleedState. WARN emits emitActivityEntrySync({source:'cloister',level:'warn',...}) + emitActivityTtsSync({priority:1,...}) naming agent, $/min, 'no progress'. TRIP: setAgentPausedSync(id, reason, true) + stopAgentSync(id) + markAgentTroubled(id) + emitActivityEntrySync({level:'error', details: diagnosis}) + emitActivityTtsSync({priority:0,...}); set stage 'tripped'. Guard trip side-effects per agent with a module-level createInFlightGuard() keyed by agentId. Return an action string per warn/trip. Then in deacon.ts: import costBleedMonitor and call it in runPatrol() immediately after the checkStuckAgentRemediation block (deacon.ts:5210-5212) using the existing pattern: `const costBleedActions = await costBleedMonitor(); actions.push(...costBleedActions); for (const a of costBleedActions) addLog('action', a, state.patrolCycle);`. costBleedMonitor itself is inside runPatrol so it is already gated by isDeaconGloballyPaused(). Tests inject now/config/agents and mock readEvents/git/capturePane/setAgentPausedSync/stopAgentSync/markAgentTroubled/emit* via vi.hoisted (mirror stuck-remediation.test.ts); use vi.useFakeTimers only if a real setTimeout is introduced.
- AC: Given a synthetic agent with rising cumulative cost, unchanged headSha and unchanged lastActivity across the no_progress window, the patrol pauses and stops the agent, marks it troubled, and emits an error-level activity entry + TTS naming the cause.
- AC: A synthetic agent whose headSha changes between samples is never paused or troubled, even when its burn rate exceeds warn_usd_per_min and accrued cost exceeds trip_usd (proves progress-awareness, not a flat cap).
- AC: An agent crossing warn_usd_per_min with flat progress but below trip_usd / the window emits a warn-level activity entry + TTS and is NOT paused.
- AC: Given an already-tripped (paused+troubled) agent, a second costBleedMonitor pass marks and pauses it at most once and emits no new trip side effects (idempotency spies asserted called exactly once across both passes).
- AC: runPatrol() invokes costBleedMonitor() and pushes its returned action strings into the patrol actions and addLog stream (wiring verified by reading deacon.ts).

title: pan-1868: Create cost-bleed-signatures.ts deadlock-signature scanner
description:
Create src/lib/cloister/cost-bleed-signatures.ts. Export detectDeadlockSignature(tail: string, ctx: { harness?: string; model: string }): { kind: 'harness-deadlock'|'context-overflow'|'rate-limit-storm'|null; diagnosis: string }. Reuse CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS / isContextOverflowTail from src/lib/context-overflow.ts. harness-deadlock = ctx.harness === 'claude-code' AND getProviderForModelSync(ctx.model) is NOT the anthropic provider AND the tail matches /exceeded model token limit|token limit: \d+|400[^\n]*token limit/i. rate-limit-storm = the tail contains at least K (e.g. 3) occurrences of /rate.?limit|\b429\b|retrying in/i. context-overflow = isContextOverflowTail(tail). Precedence: harness-deadlock > context-overflow > rate-limit-storm > null. diagnosis is a human-readable string naming the model, harness, and cause (e.g. 'context-limit deadlock — model kimi-k2.7-code on harness claude-code, expected provider-default pi').
- AC: Given a tail with repeated 'exceeded model token limit: 262144' and ctx { harness:'claude-code', model:'kimi-k2.7-code' }, returns kind 'harness-deadlock' with a diagnosis naming the model and harness.
- AC: Given the same tail but ctx { harness:'pi', ... } or an Anthropic model on claude-code, returns kind 'context-overflow' or null — never 'harness-deadlock'.
- AC: Given a tail with at least K '429 ... retrying in' lines and no overflow, returns kind 'rate-limit-storm'.
- AC: Given a clean tail with no signatures, returns kind null with an empty diagnosis.

title: pan-1868: Create cost-bleed-signals.ts: cost sampling, burn rate, progress proxies
description:
Create src/lib/cloister/cost-bleed-signals.ts. sampleAgentCostUsd(agentId, startedAt, readEvents = readEventsSync): number sums `.cost` of readEvents({ agentId, startDate: startedAt }) from src/lib/costs/events.ts (DECISION D1: the events ledger is the cost source, NEVER state.costSoFar). computeBurnRateUsdPerMin(samples: CostBleedSample[]): number returns (newest.cumulativeCostUsd - oldest.cumulativeCostUsd) / minutes(newest.ts - oldest.ts), returning 0 when fewer than two samples or Δt is ~0. readWorkspaceHeadSha(workspacePath): Promise<string|null> runs git via async execFile+promisify (NEVER execSync — NFR-1) ['-C', workspacePath, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'] and returns null on error. evaluateProgress(prev: CostBleedSample, cur: CostBleedSample): boolean returns true when (cur.headSha && prev.headSha && cur.headSha !== prev.headSha) OR cur.lastActivity advanced past prev.lastActivity, else false. Inject the cost reader so tests need no real ledger.
- AC: sampleAgentCostUsd returns the summed .cost of the agent's cost events since startedAt using an injected reader, and returns 0 when the reader yields no events.
- AC: computeBurnRateUsdPerMin returns Δcost/Δminutes across the sample window and returns 0 for fewer than two samples.
- AC: evaluateProgress returns true when headSha changed, true when lastActivity advanced, and false when neither moved.
- AC: readWorkspaceHeadSha invokes git via async execFile (no execSync anywhere in the module) and returns null on error instead of throwing.

title: PAN-1872: Implement issue
pan-1813: Verify and repair dependency edges after creation
description:
After the create loop in createBeadsFromVBriefPromise, add a post-condition verification: if plan.edges contains any `blocks` edge and beadIds is non-empty, issue ONE batched `bd dep list <beadId…> --json` over all created bead IDs (records carry issue_id = the dependent bead and id = the blocker it depends on, with dependency_type 'blocks'). Build the expected set from plan.edges (edge from→to means bead(to) depends on bead(from), i.e. expect a dep record with issue_id=bead(to), id=bead(from)). For each expected edge whose both endpoints were created but is absent from the actual set, repair it with `bd dep add <bead(to)> <bead(from)>`. After repairs, push an error for any expected edge that is still absent so createBeadsFromVBrief returns success:false (finalize exits non-zero). Edges whose endpoints were not both captured are reported as errors, not repaired. Use resolveBdTimeout for the dep-list/dep-add calls.
- AC: Given a plan with edge A→B where B was created without the --deps to A (simulated), finalize issues `bd dep add <beadB> <beadA>` and createBeadsFromVBrief returns success:true.
- AC: Given the batched bd dep list already contains every plan.edges blocks edge, no `bd dep add` call is issued and createBeadsFromVBrief returns success:true.
- AC: Given a missing edge whose `bd dep add` repair fails, createBeadsFromVBrief returns success:false with an error naming the unrepaired edge.
- AC: Given a plan with zero `blocks` edges, the verification step issues no bd dep list and no bd dep add calls and createBeadsFromVBrief returns success:true.
close_reason: Implemented verifyAndRepairDependencyEdges helper: one batched bd dep list, compare against plan.edges, repair missing edges with bd dep add, hard-fail for still-missing edges. Called after create loop in createBeadsFromVBriefPromise. Added AC1-AC4 tests. Inspection PASSED.

title: pan-1813: Recover a bead ID by exact-title re-query after a create timeout
description:
In the create loop of createBeadsFromVBriefPromise (src/lib/vbrief/beads.ts ~:378-402), when `bd create` throws (timeout) OR returns empty stdout, recover the ID before recording failure: re-query `bd list --json -l <issueLabel>` and select the bead whose title strictly equals the full title `${plan.id}: ${item.title}`. If exactly one matches, set beadIds.set(itemId, recoveredId) and push(fullTitle) into created, then continue so later items' --deps resolve. If none match, record the failure as today (genuine create failure). If more than one matches, push an explicit ambiguity error and do NOT set beadIds for that item. The re-query should use the adaptive timeout from resolveBdTimeout (and may use retryBd).
- AC: Given a bd create that times out but a subsequent bd list returns a bead whose title equals `${plan.id}: ${item.title}`, beadIds gains that item's recovered ID and a dependent item created afterward includes the recovered ID in its --deps argument.
- AC: Given a bd create timeout AND the re-query returns no bead with the matching full title, the item is recorded in errors and beadIds has no entry for it.
- AC: Given the re-query returns two beads with the matching full title, the function pushes an ambiguity error naming the title and does NOT set beadIds for that item (no silent pick).
- AC: Given a bd create that returns a non-empty bead ID, the normal path is taken and no recovery `bd list` is issued for that item (assert no list call follows a successful create).
close_reason: Implemented recoverBeadIdByTitle helper: after bd create throws or returns empty stdout, re-query bd list by issueLabel and match title === ; exactly one match recovers the ID, ambiguity/no-match surfaces an error. Added AC1-AC4 tests. Inspection PASSED.

title: pan-1813: Bounded exponential-backoff retry for idempotent bd reads (create excluded)
description:
Add a retryBd(fn, { attempts = 3, baseDelayMs = 500 }) wrapper in src/lib/vbrief/beads.ts that retries fn on failure with exponential backoff (delay = baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1)) and surfaces the last error after attempts are exhausted. title: pan-1813: Adaptive, configurable bd op timeout routed through all bd calls in beads.ts
description:
Add a resolveBdTimeout(workspacePath) helper to src/lib/vbrief/beads.ts. Behavior: if process.env.PANOPTICON_BD_TIMEOUT_MS parses to a positive integer, return it verbatim WITHOUT probing. Otherwise run `bd ping --json` once (using a fixed bootstrap timeout constant BD_PING_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT_MS = 8000 — the resolver must NOT call itself), read total_ms from the JSON, and return Math.min(180000, Math.max(30000, total_ms * 20)). If the ping throws or its JSON is unparseable, return the floor 30000 (never throw). Cache the resolved value for the lifetime of one createBeadsFromVBriefPromise call so the probe runs once per finalize. Replace the hardcoded operational timeout literals — bd list (beads.ts:80), bd delete (:98), bd create (:382), and the init/doctor/config recovery ops (:179,:183,:220,:238,:242,:206,:230) — with the resolved value. Leave the non-bd `which bd` check (:155, timeout 5000) and the resolver's own bootstrap ping unchanged.

- AC: With no env override: bd ping total_ms=5000 ⇒ resolveBdTimeout returns 100000; total_ms=255 ⇒ returns 30000 (clamped to floor); total_ms=12000 ⇒ returns 180000 (clamped to ceiling).
- AC: When bd ping throws or returns unparseable JSON, resolveBdTimeout returns 30000 and does not throw.
- AC: The bd create call in beads.ts passes the resolved timeout — a unit test asserts the timeout option mockExecAsync received for `bd create` equals the resolved value, and grep finds no remaining 15000/10000/30000 literal on the list/delete/create calls.
close_reason: Implemented adaptive configurable bd op timeout via resolveBdTimeout(): env override wins, else bd-ping probe with floor/ceiling clamp; routed all bd operational timeouts in beads.ts; added AC1-AC4 tests. Inspection PASSED.

title: pan-1821: Expose backoffMs/suspendedUntil/rateLimited in cache-status diagnostics

title: pan-1821: Honor getSuspensionMs in scheduleNext to suspend exhausted trackers
description:
In scheduleNext (issue-data-service.ts:570-598), after computing effectiveInterval, call this.cache.getSuspensionMs(tracker). When > 0, set the next-poll delay to Math.min(suspendMs, 3_600_000) (D4 ceiling), bypassing the intervals.max clamp, log a warn line, and store it on state.currentInterval. When 0, use the existing effectiveInterval unchanged (NFR-1: non-exhausted cadence untouched). The setTimeout callback body (poll dispatch + reschedule) is unchanged.

- AC: Given getSuspensionMs returns a value above 3_600_000, the armed delay is clamped to 3_600_000 (D4 ceiling).
- AC: Given getSuspensionMs returns 0, scheduleNext arms the timer at the existing effectiveInterval (clamped to [min,max]) — GitHub/Rally/normal-Linear cadence is unchanged (NFR-1).
- AC: After a suspension delay elapses and the window resets (remaining restored), the next scheduleNext call returns to the normal interval — polling resumes automatically with no manual intervention.
close_reason: scheduleNext now honors getSuspensionMs, clamps to 1 hour, bypasses intervals.max for suspension, normal cadence untouched. Added 4 fake-timer tests. Typecheck/lint pass.

title: pan-1821: Record quota exhaustion on Linear 429 / RATELIMITED before throwing
description:
In fetchLinearIssues, when response.status === 429 OR the GraphQL error indicates rate-limiting (message contains 'rate limit' or 'RATELIMITED', consistent with linear-client.ts:139), ensure 'linear' is recorded as exhausted via cache.updateRateLimit('linear', { remaining: 0, total, resetAt }) before the existing throw. If the rate-limit headers were absent (ac of linear-rl-headers recorded nothing), derive resetAt from the Retry-After header (now + seconds) or default to now + 3_600_000 ms. Preserve the existing thrown Error so pollLinear's catch still sets lastError.

- AC: Given a 429 with no rate-limit headers but a Retry-After header of N seconds, the recorded resetAt equals now + N seconds (asserted with fake timers).
- AC: Given a GraphQL body whose error message contains 'RATELIMITED' (HTTP 200), fetchLinearIssues still records remaining:0 and throws, defaulting resetAt to now + 1 hour when no reset/Retry-After is present.
close_reason: Added recordLinearExhaustion, detect HTTP 429 and GraphQL RATELIMITED, derive resetAt from Retry-After or +1h default, added 4 unit tests, typecheck/lint pass.

title: pan-1821: Add getSuspensionMs(tracker) to CacheService
description:
Add a pure method getSuspensionMs(tracker: string, now: number = Date.now()): number to CacheService (cache-service.ts). It reads getRateLimit(tracker); returns 0 when there is no limit row, when remaining > 0, when resetAt is unparseable, or when resetAt <= now; otherwise returns (resetMs - now). The `now` parameter makes it deterministically testable with fake timers. No schema change (NFR-3) — derived entirely from the existing rate_limits row. Callers are responsible for the 1-hour ceiling clamp (D4).
- AC: getSuspensionMs returns 0 when getRateLimit(tracker) is null, and 0 when remaining > 0 regardless of resetAt.
- AC: Given remaining === 0 and resetAt one hour in the future, getSuspensionMs returns approximately 3_600_000 (within tolerance, asserted with a fixed `now`).
- AC: Given remaining === 0 but resetAt already in the past (or unparseable), getSuspensionMs returns 0 (window already reset — no suspension).
close_reason: Added CacheService.getSuspensionMs with tests; returns 0 unless remaining <= 0 and resetAt is in the future. Typecheck/lint pass.

title: pan-1821: Parse Linear rate-limit headers and feed updateRateLimit('linear', …)
description:
In fetchLinearIssues (issue-data-service.ts ~:1089-1102), after `await fetch(...)` resolves and BEFORE `response.json()` / the json.errors throw, parse Linear's rate-limit headers and call this.cache.updateRateLimit('linear', { remaining, total, resetAt }). Use header names x-ratelimit-requests-remaining / -limit / -reset, falling back to the bare x-ratelimit-* names if absent. Normalize the reset value defensively (D2): a value < 1e12 is Unix seconds (×1000), otherwise Unix ms. Extract/reuse a parseIntegerHeader(headers, name) helper (see substrate-bug-poller.ts:105-110) that returns null on missing/unparseable values; skip the update (never throw) when remaining or total is null. Mirror the GitHub callback at :854-862.
- AC: Given a Linear fetch response carrying x-ratelimit-requests-remaining/-limit/-reset, fetchLinearIssues calls cache.updateRateLimit('linear', …) so getRateLimit('linear') returns the parsed remaining/total/resetAt (verified by a unit test with a mocked fetch).
- AC: Given a reset header value in Unix seconds (~1.7e9) and one in Unix milliseconds (~1.7e12), normalization produces the same correct future ISO-8601 resetAt (values <1e12 treated as seconds).
- AC: When the rate-limit headers are missing or unparseable, fetchLinearIssues does NOT call updateRateLimit and does NOT throw from the header-parsing step — issue fetching proceeds unchanged.
- AC: Header parsing runs before the json.errors throw, so a response that both carries rate-limit headers and a GraphQL error still records the rate limit (verified by a test where json.errors is set).
close_reason: Implemented Linear rate-limit header parsing in fetchLinearIssues, extracted parseIntegerHeader to cache-service.ts, added 7 unit tests, typecheck/lint pass.

title: pan-1802: Truncate (head+tail) and retry once when a summary chunk overflows
description:
In src/lib/conversations/smart-compaction.ts, make generateSummaryFromPrompt (:791) resilient to context overflow. Add a head+tail truncation helper (preserve the first and last portions, insert an elision marker like '[... N characters truncated ...]'). When the underlying runModelSummary call rejects AND isContextOverflowError(err) is true (from the overflow-detector bead), rebuild the prompt with the serialized chunk truncated head+tail to a per-model ceiling derived from getChunkBudgetChars(model), also capping previousSummary, and retry exactly once. If the retried call also overflows (or any non-overflow error occurs), reject so the caller's fallback handles it. Do not loop. This single chokepoint covers all generateSummaryFromPrompt call sites (chunked loops and non-chunked) and authorHandoffExternal precompaction.
- AC: Given the first runModelSummary call rejects with a context-overflow error, generateSummaryFromPrompt truncates the serialized chunk head+tail and retries once, returning the degraded summary from the second (truncated) call instead of throwing.
- AC: The head+tail truncation helper, given input longer than the ceiling, returns text containing both the original head and the original tail plus an elision marker, and is no longer than the ceiling plus the marker; verified by a unit test on a long string.
- AC: When the retried (truncated) call also rejects with overflow, generateSummaryFromPrompt rejects (no third attempt, no infinite loop), surfacing the error to its caller.
- AC: When the first runModelSummary call succeeds, generateSummaryFromPrompt returns that result unchanged and makes no second call (asserted by call count), so normal-sized summaries are unaffected.
close_reason: Added truncateHeadTail helper and one-retry logic to generateSummaryFromPrompt; capping serialized chunk and previousSummary to getChunkBudgetChars(model) on context overflow. Covered by unit tests.

title: pan-1802: Mark the conversation ended when a fork pipeline fails terminally
description:

title: pan-1802: Guard the handoff fallback summary so the pipeline always spawns
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts runForkPipeline (:3862), the handoff fallback paths (catch blocks at :3948-3953, :3956-3961, :3963-3972) call buildSummary() unguarded — a throw escapes the pipeline. Wrap the fallback so a throw drops to generateFallbackSummary(parentSessionFile) (heuristic, no LLM, cannot overflow), and a further throw drops to an empty summary string; prependFallbackFocus(...) still preserves the operator focus. After the handoff block, the pipeline must continue to updateForkStatus('spawning') + ensureForkSessionReady + injectForkSummary + markConversationActive + updateForkStatus(null) regardless of which fallback tier produced the summary. forkFallbackReason continues to be persisted via updateConversationForkFallbackReason.
- AC: Given authorHandoffExternal throws AND the LLM fallback summary throws a context-overflow error, runForkPipeline seeds the successor from generateFallbackSummary and resolves successfully — ensureForkSessionReady is invoked and forkStatus is cleared to null (the pipeline does not reject).
- AC: Given the heuristic generateFallbackSummary ALSO throws, runForkPipeline spawns with a focus-only seed (empty summary passed through prependFallbackFocus) and still clears forkStatus to null without rejecting.
- AC: After a fallback, the successor's forkFallbackReason is persisted (updateConversationForkFallbackReason called with the reason) so the CLI prints the yellow 'Handoff fell back to summary fork' notice.
- AC: A test mocking authorHandoffExternal and generateSummaryForFork to throw overflow asserts runForkPipeline invokes ensureForkSessionReady and resolves without rejecting.
close_reason: Hardened runForkPipeline fallback summary path to degrade from LLM summary to heuristic fallback to empty summary, always reaching ensureForkSessionReady. Added unit tests.

title: pan-1802: Add a claude -p context-overflow detector to context-overflow.ts
description:
Extend src/lib/context-overflow.ts with a pure matcher isContextOverflowError(err: unknown): boolean that recognizes the summarizer overflow signature. title: pan-1801: Partition PR failures against the base branch's failing checks; suppress all-inherited relays

Render inherited failures in a separate section titled 'Inherited from <baseRefName> — these are failing on <baseRefName> itself; do not chase them'. If every PR failure is inherited, log '[ci-relay] all failures inherited from <base> — suppressed' and return before writing feedback or messaging the agent. If the base fetch throws, proceed with all failures listed as the PR's own and append the note 'could not compare against <baseRefName> — some failures may be inherited'. Extend the relay unit tests for all three behaviors.
- AC: Given a PR failure whose check name also fails on the base branch HEAD, the feedback body renders it under an 'Inherited from <base>' section instead of the own-failures list

title: pan-1801: Create ci-failure-relay module: debounce, settle timer, live-agent gate, feedback write + nudge
description:
New file src/lib/cloister/ci-failure-relay.ts. Export scheduleCiFailureRelay(opts: {issueId: string; repo: string; prNumber: number; headSha: string}): void — synchronous: if debounce Map already has key `${issueId}:${headSha}` return; otherwise mark the key (Map bounded to 1000 entries, evict oldest insertion), then setTimeout(60_000).unref() invoking relayCiFailureNow(opts).catch(console.warn). relayCiFailureNow: (1) live-agent gate — dynamic-import ../tmux.js, sessionExistsSync(`agent-${issueId.toLowerCase()}`); absent => console.log and return; (2) gh pr view <prNumber> --repo <repo> --json statusCheckRollup,baseRefName,headRefOid via promisified execFile (timeout 15000); (3) abort if headRefOid !== opts.headSha; (4) collect failing checks from statusCheckRollup using FAILING_CHECK_CONCLUSIONS exported from webhook-handlers.ts:174 (fallback if an ESM cycle appears: define the const here and re-export from webhook-handlers); empty failing set => return; (5) build markdown body listing each failing check name + conclusion (log excerpts and inherited partition arrive in later beads); (6) dynamic-import ./feedback-writer.js, writeFeedbackFile({issueId, specialist: 'ci-monitor', outcome: 'ci-failure', summary, markdownBody}); (7) dynamic-import ../agents.js, deliverAgentMessage(`agent-${issueId.toLowerCase()}`, message containing 'MUST READ: <absolute feedback path>' plus 'fix, commit, push — Panopticon detects new commits and re-runs the pipeline', 'ci-failure-relay'). Also export _resetCiFailureRelayForTests() clearing the Map and pending timers (mirror clearAllReconciliationTimeouts, webhook-handlers.ts:179). Tests at tests/unit/lib/cloister/ci-failure-relay.test.ts with vi.useFakeTimers()/vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(60000) (repo rule: never real timers) and vi.mock of child_process, ../tmux.js, ./feedback-writer.js, ../agents.js.

- AC: Given no agent-<issue> tmux session, when the settle timer fires, the relay returns after a log line — writes no feedback file and sends no agent message

- AC: Given a live session and matching head with failing checks, the relay creates .pan/feedback/NNN-ci-monitor-ci-failure.md via writeFeedbackFile and sends a deliverAgentMessage whose text contains the absolute feedback file path
- AC: scheduleCiFailureRelay returns synchronously with an unref'd timer, and a rejection inside relayCiFailureNow logs a warning instead of propagating to the caller

title: pan-1807: Append completion contract to handoff briefs in runForkPipeline

title: pan-1807: Pure verdict logic evaluateHandoffCandidate + types

title: pan-1775: Seed session-tree feature candidates from active remote agent states
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/projects.ts fetchProjectSessionTree() (lines ~471-542): seed feature candidates from listActiveRemoteAgentStates() (exported by src/lib/remote/remote-agents.ts:82) in addition to the existing workspaces/feature-* directory scan (lines 503-510). title: pan-1799: Capture boot-death diagnostics via a bounded tmux remain-on-exit window

title: pan-1798: Warn loudly when the managed tmux server's cgroup is a tmux-spawn scope
description:
Per PRD WI-2, in src/lib/tmux.ts: (1) add exported pure function cgroupIndicatesSpawnScope(cgroupContent: string): boolean — true iff any line of /proc/<pid>/cgroup content has a path whose final component matches /^tmux-spawn-.*\.scope$/ (pure-function test seam, same pattern as paneTreeHasHarnessProcess); (2) add getManagedServerPid helper using `tmux -L panopticon display-message -p '#{pid}'` (verified to return the server PID with zero sessions), returning null on any failure; (3) wire a guard step into ensurePanopticonTmuxServer/Sync after the server is confirmed alive: resolve PID, read /proc/<pid>/cgroup, and when cgroupIndicatesSpawnScope is true emit a console.error prefixed '[tmux-founder-guard]' naming the offending scope unit and the server PID; warn at most once per server PID per process (module-level last-warned PID); silent no-op when /proc read fails (non-Linux); NEVER restart, signal, or migrate the server. Tests in tests/lib/tmux-founder-guard.test.ts: pure-function cases plus mocked-exec integration cases.
- AC: cgroupIndicatesSpawnScope returns true for cgroup content ending in tmux-spawn-<uuid>.scope and false for panopticon-tmux-*.scope, app.slice, and user session scope paths

title: pan-1808: Implement issue
description:
## Evidence (2026-06-12)

After the PAN-1803 work agent ran `npm test` locally in its workspace at 11:35, a leftover session appeared on the shared agent socket:

```
$ tmux -L panopticon list-sessions
agent-pan-resume-redeliver: 1 windows (created Fri Jun 12 11:35:55 2026)
```

The pane contains a live interactive `claude --resume` session picker ("No sessions match …"). The name matches the kickoff-redelivery tests in `tests/integration/agent-spawning.test.ts` ("resumeAgent re-delivers the original kickoff when kickoffDelivered is false", etc.).

## Why it matters

- Leaked interactive claude processes accumulate RAM and API-session weight.
- Sessions named `agent-*` on the panopticon socket are picked up by resource discovery / patrols and can confuse orphan detection.
- Tests that touch the real shared socket can interfere with live agents (cf. PAN-1798's shared-server kill blast radius).

## Desired behavior

Integration tests must never create sessions on the shared `panopticon` socket: use a per-run throwaway socket name (e.g. `-L pan-test-$PID`) injected via the tmux lib, and kill the socket's server in `afterAll`. The spawned command in these tests should be a stub, not the real `claude` binary.

## Cleanup
The leaked session was killed manually after capture.

title: pan-1803: Implement issue
description:
**Architecture bug (keystone).** Codex work agents are launched via `codex exec` (one-shot: runs one turn, writes its rollout only on the first turn, then exits). The work-agent lifecycle expects a **persistent** session — the same model claude-code (interactive `claude`) and pi (long-lived `--mode rpc`) use — so when a codex agent finishes its turn and exits, the lifecycle marks it `orphaned: tmux session missing at boot` and the deacon treats it as dead. Net: codex work agents boot (after PAN-1799), run once, vanish, and never complete the bead loop or accept `pan tell` feedback.

**One-shot is a deliberately-rejected architecture** (it has cost hundreds of hours historically) — agents must be live interactive sessions. The fix is to make codex work agents follow the **claude-code work-agent pattern**, which Panopticon spent its lifetime getting right.

**Reference pattern (claude-code, the template):**
- `buildNonConversationCommand` in `src/lib/launcher-generator.ts` emits interactive `claude --permission-mode auto --model ...`, wrapped via `wrapWithSupervisor` (PTY supervisor). The session stays alive between turns.
- Prompt delivery: `agents.ts` waits for a readiness signal (`waitForReadySignal` → SessionStart hook ready.json) then delivers the kickoff via tmux/supervisor. `pan tell` delivers subsequent messages to the same live session.
- Lifecycle: a live tmux session IS the normal running state; completion = `pan done`, not process exit.
- Codex **conversations** already run persistently as TUI (`buildCodexCommand` codexMode='tui' → `codex -c project_doc_max_bytes=0` under the supervisor) — proof codex can do this.

**Required change (mirror claude-code):**
1. `buildCodexCommand` — for WORK agents, emit interactive codex (NOT `exec`): `codex -m <model> -s <workspace-write> -c approval_policy=never --skip-git-repo-check` wrapped with the PTY supervisor; the kickoff prompt is delivered post-readiness, NOT embedded inline. Keep `getCodexLauncherFields` but drop the hardcoded one-shot `codexMode:'exec'` for work (add a work-tui mode or equivalent). Conversations keep their existing tui path; exec mode may remain only if some non-work caller still needs it (audit callers).
2. `agents.ts` delivery — codex work agents must take the tmux/supervisor delivery path (today `prompt && resolvedHarness !== 'codex'` SKIPS codex because exec embedded the prompt). Add a codex-TUI readiness check (capture-pane for the codex prompt, analogous to `waitForPiTuiReady`) before delivering.
3. Keep `waitForCodexRollout`/thread-id capture for resume; verify resume uses the interactive (not exec) path too.
4. Lifecycle: confirm the orphan-at-boot path no longer fires once the session persists; if an explicit codex-readiness gate is needed, add it.

**Acceptance:** a `pan start <id> --model gpt-5.5 --harness codex` work agent (a) survives >3 min idle after finishing its kickoff turn (tmux session stays alive), (b) processes a `pan tell <id> "..."` message delivered after it goes idle, (c) closes a bead and continues to the next without the process exiting, (d) is NOT marked orphaned by the deacon while alive. Test against a scratch issue; do not rely on unit tests alone — this is a live-session behavior. typecheck + lint green; existing codex conversation tests stay green.

Refs: PAN-1799 (boot fixes — prerequisite, merged), PAN-1574 (codex first-class — introduced the exec mode), and the claude-code work-agent path as the reference implementation.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: pan-1787: Unified resolveHarness() in new src/lib/harness-resolve.ts
description:
Per PRD WI-2: create src/lib/harness-resolve.ts exporting `resolveHarness(input: { explicit?: RuntimeName; role?: Role; model: string }): Promise<RuntimeName>` with precedence (first defined wins): 1) explicit, 2) loadYamlConfig().config.roles[role]?.harness, 3) config.providerHarnesses[provider] where provider = getProviderForModelSync(model).name, 4) getBuiltInDefaultHarness(provider), 5) 'claude-code'. The winner ALWAYS passes through canUseHarnessSync(winner, model, await getProviderAuthMode(model)); blocked ⇒ 'claude-code'. If the winner is 'pi' or 'codex' and its binary is not installed, collapse to 'claude-code' with a console warning — implement an async availability helper using promisified exec `command -v <bin>` with a module-level cache (do NOT reuse doctor's execSync-based checkCommand; resolveHarness is dashboard-server-reachable and execSync is forbidden there). When tier 4 (built-in default) decides, emit a one-line notice once per provider per process: "harness <h> chosen by provider default — override in Settings → Providers". Write tests/unit/lib/harness-resolve.test.ts covering the full precedence matrix: explicit>role>provider-override>built-in; empty config + anthropic⇒claude-code, + openai⇒codex, + kimi/google/zai⇒pi; policy-blocked winner (explicit pi + anthropic model + subscription auth) collapses to claude-code; missing binary collapses to claude-code with warning. Mock the availability check and policy/auth lookups in tests.
- AC: resolveHarness returns the explicit harness when provided, else the role override, else the provider override, else the built-in default — the full precedence-matrix unit suite passes
- AC: With empty providerHarnesses and no role override, resolveHarness returns claude-code for an Anthropic model, codex for an OpenAI model, and pi for kimi/google/zai models
- AC: Every winner passes through canUseHarnessSync: explicit pi + Anthropic model + subscription auth returns claude-code; existing harness-policy tests pass unmodified
- AC: When the winning pi/codex binary is absent, resolveHarness returns claude-code and logs a warning, using only async exec (no execSync anywhere in the new module)
- AC: The first resolution that lands on a built-in default emits the one-line override-hint notice exactly once per provider per process
close_reason: Added unified resolveHarness with precedence, policy gate, async binary fallback, provider-default notice, and unit coverage.

title: pan-1778: Implement issue
description:
## Problem

Long remote runs outlive the synced OAuth token. When the host's Claude Code refreshes its token, the VM's synced copy is orphaned (refresh tokens rotate) and the agent stalls on `API Error: 401 · Please run /login`. On PAN-1762 run 1 the agent sat stalled for ~1h, which then cascaded into the reap-patrol kill and total work loss (see PAN-1676 incident comment, 2026-06-11).

A **reactive** heal landed in 67530a96f: the reap patrol greps the pane tail for the 401 stall, re-syncs credentials, and nudges the session. That only fires at patrol cadence after the stall has already begun — the agent still loses minutes-to-an-hour of wall clock per occurrence.

## Fix

Proactive refresh: a deacon patrol step (or a timer inside the reap patrol loop) that, for every active remote agent in `listActiveRemoteAgentStates()`, periodically re-runs `fly.syncClaudeCredentials(vmName)` — e.g. every 15 minutes, or whenever the host credentials file mtime changes (the cheap, precise trigger: watch `~/.claude/.credentials.json` and push on change).

Notes for implementation:
- `syncClaudeCredentials` already exists on FlyProvider (src/lib/remote/fly-provider.ts) and is idempotent.
- mtime-watch beats fixed cadence: tokens rotate when the HOST refreshes, which is observable locally without any VM round-trip. Fall back to a periodic push if the watch is awkward in the patrol structure.
- Keep the reactive heal (healStaleRemoteAuth in src/lib/remote/remote-completion.ts) as the backstop; this issue removes the common path to it.
- Cheap no-op when no remote agents are active (local file scan only — same guard the reap patrol uses in deacon.ts).

## Acceptance
- With a remote agent running, rotating host credentials results in the VM's credentials file being updated without operator action, before the agent hits a 401.
- No fly API calls when zero remote agents are active.
- Unit tests use fake timers per the repo testing rules.

Refs: PAN-1676 (epic + incident report), 67530a96f (reactive heal).
- AC: syncClaudeCredentials already exists on FlyProvider (src/lib/remote/fly-provider.ts) and is idempotent.
- AC: mtime-watch beats fixed cadence: tokens rotate when the HOST refreshes, which is observable locally without any VM round-trip. Fall back to a periodic push if the watch is awkward in the patrol structure.
- AC: Keep the reactive heal (healStaleRemoteAuth in src/lib/remote/remote-completion.ts) as the backstop; this issue removes the common path to it.
- AC: Cheap no-op when no remote agents are active (local file scan only — same guard the reap patrol uses in deacon.ts).
- AC: With a remote agent running, rotating host credentials results in the VM's credentials file being updated without operator action, before the agent hits a 401.
- AC: No fly API calls when zero remote agents are active.
- AC: Unit tests use fake timers per the repo testing rules.
close_reason: Implemented proactive Fly remote Claude credential refresh in deacon patrol with mtime/fingerprint trigger, 15 minute fallback, zero-active no-op guard, and fake-timer unit coverage.

title: pan-1776: Server-side delivery engine: deliverViaPrimitives in pty-delivery-client.ts
description:
New src/lib/channels/pty-delivery-client.ts per PRD §B4: export async deliverViaPrimitives({socketPath, token, agentId, content, echoToStdout, caller?}) — throws on failure. Algorithm is the exact injectPtyMessage state machine over HTTP primitives, importing every constant/helper from pty-echo.ts: (1) GET /v1/info → baseOffset = outputEndOffset; (2) prefix = confirmationPrefix(trimmed), empty prefix skips to Enter; (3) attempts 1..INPUT_ECHO_CONFIRM_ATTEMPTS: attempt>1 first purges (POST /v1/write purgeBackspaces(len)) + sleep INPUT_PURGE_SETTLE_MS, then POST /v1/write {data: trimmedContent, echoToStdout} (transcript echo rides the CONTENT write), then poll GET /v1/output?since=baseOffset every INTERVAL_MS until TIMEOUT_MS — confirmed when normalizeForEchoMatch(accumulated) contains prefix OR PASTE_PLACEHOLDER_RE matches stripAnsi(accumulated); (4) unconfirmed → purge once more, log, throw (ladder falls back to tmux; purge keeps that single-copy-safe); (5) sleep INPUT_SETTLE_MS then POST /v1/write {data: '\r'} WITHOUT stdout echo; (6) appendChannelDeliveryLog with path 'supervisor-primitives'. Each primitive HTTP call timeout ≤ 2s; total engine budget must respect the ladder invariant documented at src/lib/agents.ts:1405 (client budget > worst-case write/confirm path).
- AC: Unit test vs fake unix-socket shim, happy path: exactly one content write (with echoToStdout), confirmation via /v1/output polling, then exactly one '\r' write — assert the exact ordered write sequence
- AC: Late-echo retry test: echo appears only after the purged second attempt — assert exact write sequence content → purge → content → '\r' (one purge between writes, single final submit)
- AC: Full-failure test: never-confirming output ⇒ exactly 2 purges total, deliverViaPrimitives throws, and NO '\r' is ever written
- AC: Placeholder confirmation test: '[Pasted text #N' output confirms without prefix match
- AC: All delay/poll paths use vi.useFakeTimers + advanceTimersByTimeAsync (fake-timers rule); no real setTimeout waits in unit tests

title: pan-1776: Socket protocol v1: URL-path routing + /v1/info, /v1/write, /v1/output, /v1/resize
description:
Extend createPtySupervisorServer() (src/lib/channels/pty-supervisor.ts:319) from POST-/-only to routing by req.method + url.pathname per PRD §B1 table. Legacy POST / stays byte-for-byte compatible ({content, echo?, caller?, meta?} → injectPtyMessage). New: GET /v1/info → {schemaVersion, pid, scriptSha256, capabilities, outputEndOffset}; POST /v1/write {data, echoToStdout?} → raw child.write(data), echoToStdout mirrors to supervisor stdout exactly like payload.echo does today, returns {ok: true, outputEndOffset}; GET /v1/output?since=<n> → ring slice {startOffset, endOffset, data}; POST /v1/resize {cols, rows} → child.resize bounds-checked 1..1000. Wire ONE child.onData subscription in main() appending to an OutputRing instance. All endpoints require the existing x-pan-pty-token header; unknown paths → 404; socket stays mode 0600 with no new listening surface. Append "primitives-v1" to the shared capabilities constant (sidecar + /v1/info now advertise ["legacy-post", "primitives-v1"]).
- AC: Subprocess integration tests: /v1/info returns identity + monotonically increasing outputEndOffset; /v1/write injects raw bytes into the child PTY and mirrors to stdout when echoToStdout; /v1/output?since returns the slice with correct offsets; /v1/resize resizes within bounds and rejects 0 or >1000
- AC: All /v1 endpoints reject requests without a matching pty token; unknown paths return 404; legacy POST / behavior is unchanged (all 12 pre-existing tests still green)
- AC: Sidecar and /v1/info both advertise capabilities ["legacy-post", "primitives-v1"] from a single shared constant

title: pan-1776: supervisor-status.ts: getSupervisorStatus + getCurrentDistSha
description:
New module src/lib/supervisor-status.ts per PRD §A2: export interface SupervisorStatus { running, identityPresent, stale, capabilities, runningSha?, distSha? }; export async getSupervisorStatus(agentId); export async getCurrentDistSha() — sha256 of resolvePtySupervisorScriptPath() (src/lib/agents.ts:1766), cached by (path, mtimeMs). running = socket exists AND identity pid alive (process.kill(pid, 0) in try/catch). stale = running && (no identity || scriptSha256 !== current dist sha) — a running socket with no supervisor.json is a pre-PAN-1776 supervisor: legacy-only AND unknown version, treated as stale. capabilities = [] when unknown. All IO async; this module is server-reachable so no execSync anywhere.
- AC: Unit tests with tmpdir fixtures cover: missing supervisor.json (running socket ⇒ stale, capabilities []), dead pid (running false), sha match (stale false), sha mismatch (stale true)
- AC: getCurrentDistSha caches by (path, mtimeMs): second call with unchanged mtime does not re-read the file; mtime change invalidates (testable via injected/fixture path)

title: pan-1776: OutputRing: 64KiB ring buffer with absolute offsets
description:
Per PRD §B2: export class OutputRing { append(s: string): void; slice(since: number): {startOffset, endOffset, data} } in src/lib/channels/pty-supervisor.ts. Capacity 64 KiB; tracks absoluteOffset = total bytes ever seen. slice(since) returns from max(since, bufferStart) — when since < buffer start, return from buffer start so the caller detects the gap via startOffset > since. Pure class, no IO.
- AC: Direct unit tests cover: append+slice happy path, wrap-around past 64KiB preserving absolute offsets, gap behavior (since < bufferStart ⇒ startOffset > since), and empty buffer (start === end, data '')

title: pan-1776: Supervisor identity sidecar (supervisor.json) + computeScriptSha256
description:
In src/lib/channels/pty-supervisor.ts, write ~/.panopticon/agents/<agentId>/supervisor.json immediately after the socket binds, atomically (write tmp + rename), per PRD §A1: { schemaVersion: 1, pid, scriptPath (process.argv[1]), scriptSha256 (sha256 of the file at process.argv[1] read at startup), capabilities, startedAt }. capabilities is a module-level constant set to ["legacy-post"] in this bead (b1-socket-endpoints later appends "primitives-v1"). Implement async writeSupervisorIdentity(agentId) — best-effort, never throws (same posture as the log appenders) — and export computeScriptSha256(path) for tests. Do NOT delete the file on shutdown: staleness checks validate liveness independently and the stale file is useful post-mortem. The rebuild-between-load-and-hash race is tolerable; document it in a comment, don't engineer around it.
- AC: Integration test (existing subprocess harness in src/lib/channels/__tests__/pty-supervisor.test.ts) spawns the supervisor and asserts supervisor.json exists with schemaVersion 1, the supervisor's pid, capabilities ["legacy-post"], and scriptSha256 matching computeScriptSha256 of the spawned script

- AC: Sidecar write is atomic (tmp + rename), never throws on failure, and is NOT removed on SIGTERM/shutdown (assert file survives the existing unlinks-socket-on-SIGTERM test flow)

title: pan-1765: HTTP trigger and review-request routes surface the gated outcome to humans
description:
