title: pan-1765: Deacon patrols and startup recovery treat gated dispatch as calm deferral — no retry-counter poisoning
description:
Update the three orchestrator call sites to recognize result.gated: (1) deacon.ts checkPostReviewCommits redispatch (~line 2904-2916): log action 'Deferred review re-dispatch for <issue> — merge conflict must be resolved first' instead of 'Failed to re-dispatch'; (2) deacon.ts orphan-pending redispatch (~line 1966-1986): same calm action wording; ensure the gated path does not increment reviewRetryCount and cannot trip the PAN-794 review-infra breaker (gated deferrals are expected steady-state while a resolver works, potentially for many patrol ticks); (3) service.ts startup recovery (~line 772): log deferral instead of claiming 'Re-dispatched recovery review'. Keep PAN-1665 advancing-ceiling logic untouched — the ceiling check may run before or after the gate, but a gated issue must not consume an advancing slot (release the slot if it was reserved before the gate result).

title: pan-1765: Wire the conflict gate into spawnReviewRoleForIssuePromise and extend its result with gated: true
description:
In src/lib/cloister/review-agent.ts spawnReviewRoleForIssuePromise (line ~296): after the session-idempotency block but BEFORE setReviewStatusSync({ reviewStatus: 'reviewing' }) and before any convoy/manifest work, call resolveConflictGate with real deps. If gated: leave reviewStatus 'pending' (do not flip to reviewing), set reviewNotes to a deferral explanation including the blocker detectedAt, and return { success: false, gated: true, message: 'Review dispatch deferred: merge conflict with <target> must be resolved first' }. Extend the function's return type ({ success, message, error?, gated? }) — the Effect wrapper spawnReviewRoleForIssue inherits it. Resolve targetBranch the same way the review context does (default 'main'). The gate must run for ALL callers including force:true (see autoDecisions). Do not disturb the PAN-1131 stale-runId logic or PAN-1531 feedback archiving above it — archiving may stay before or move after the gate, but a gated dispatch must NOT archive the previous cycle's feedback (the work agent still needs it).

- AC: Unit: stale blocker (probe 'clean') → blocker cleared and the convoy spawn proceeds normally (reviewing status set, spawnRun called)
- AC: Unit: gated dispatch does not archive .pan/feedback files and does not set reviewSpawnedAt
- AC: force: true does NOT bypass the gate (test asserts gated result with force set)

title: pan-1765: Implement the real conflict-resolver dispatch dep: work-role spawn with rebase-resolution prompt, idempotent
description:
In conflict-gate.ts (or a small sibling builder mirroring merge-train-deps.ts buildRealReconcileDeps), implement buildRealConflictGateDeps(): the dispatchResolver dep calls spawnRun(issueId, 'work', { prompt }) with a prompt modeled on merge-train-deps.dispatchConflictResolver but framed for a standing conflict with origin/main rather than a just-merged sibling: read what main changed AND what this issue intended, rebase onto origin/main preserving both intents, build/test/commit/push --force-with-lease, then re-request review (pan done / pan review request). Idempotency: spawnRun throws 'already running' when the session exists — catch it and treat as already-dispatched (do NOT crash the gate). On successful spawn: stamp conflictResolutionDispatchedAt via setReviewStatus and emitActivityEntrySync (source 'review', message 'Review deferred — conflict resolver dispatched for <issue>') so the dashboard shows why no convoy ran.
- AC: Unit: dispatchResolver spawns role 'work' with a prompt containing rebase-onto-origin/main + preserve-both-intents + re-request-review instructions
- AC: Unit: when spawnRun throws 'already running', dispatchResolver swallows it and reports already-dispatched (no throw, no duplicate activity entry)
- AC: Unit: successful spawn stamps conflictResolutionDispatchedAt and emits exactly one activity entry
close_reason: Added real conflict gate deps that dispatch a work-role resolver prompt, swallow already-running sessions, stamp conflictResolutionDispatchedAt, and emit activity

title: pan-1765: Implement resolveConflictGate() orchestrator: detect merge blockers, re-verify freshness, clear stale flags, request resolver dispatch
description:
In src/lib/cloister/conflict-gate.ts add resolveConflictGate(issueId, workspace, targetBranch, deps) with dependency-injected deps (getReviewStatus, setReviewStatus, probeMergeability, dispatchResolver, now, log) so it is unit-testable without git/DB/spawns — same pattern as merge-train-reconciler.ts. Behavior: (1) no merge_conflict/not_mergeable blocker in blockerReasons → { gated: false }. (2) Blocker present → probe mergeability. Probe 'clean' → remove merge_conflict/not_mergeable entries from blockerReasons (preserve other blocker types), return { gated: false, clearedStaleBlocker: true }. Probe 'conflicts' or 'unknown' → return { gated: true, reason } and request resolver dispatch UNLESS throttled: skip dispatch when conflictResolutionDispatchedAt is younger than 30 min (deps.now-based — fake timers in tests per CLAUDE.md rule). Probe results are cached in-module per issue for ~3 min keyed by issueId so 60s deacon patrols do not git-fetch every tick; expose a reset hook for tests. This bead defines the GateResult contract ({ gated, reason?, clearedStaleBlocker? }) and the deps interface that beads conflict-resolver-dispatch and gate-review-dispatch implement/consume.
- AC: Unit: status without merge blockers → { gated: false } and no probe call (other blocker types like failing_checks do not gate)
- AC: Unit: merge_conflict blocker + probe 'clean' → blocker entries removed via setReviewStatus (other blocker types preserved), result { gated: false, clearedStaleBlocker: true }, no resolver dispatched
- AC: Unit: merge_conflict blocker + probe 'conflicts' → { gated: true } and dispatchResolver called exactly once; a second call within the 30-min throttle window (fake timers) does not dispatch again
- AC: Unit: probe 'unknown' → gated (conservative) without throwing; dispatch still attempted subject to throttle
- AC: Unit: probe result cached per issue ~3 min — two gate calls within the window trigger one probe (fake timers advance past window → re-probe)
close_reason: Added resolveConflictGate orchestrator with merge-blocker detection, stale-clearing, conservative gating, dispatch throttle, probe cache, and tests

title: pan-1765: Merge-blocker reconcile service re-verifies blocker-flagged rows so stale conflict flags clear

Keep the existing skip for rows with only non-mergeability blockers. Update the file header comment to describe both reconcile directions. Tests MUST use vi.useFakeTimers per the CLAUDE.md retry/delay rule.

- AC: Unit: rows with only failing_checks/draft_pr/etc. blockers are still skipped (no GitHub call)

title: pan-1765: Add checkBranchMergeability() local merge-conflict probe in new conflict-gate module
description:
Create src/lib/cloister/conflict-gate.ts with checkBranchMergeability(workspacePath, targetBranch, deps?) returning 'clean' | 'conflicts' | 'unknown'. Implementation: `git fetch origin <targetBranch>` then `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only HEAD origin/<targetBranch>` (non-destructive, git >= 2.38); exit code / conflict markers classify the result. Any exec failure (missing workspace, old git, network error) returns 'unknown' — never throws. Inject the exec runner for unit tests (follow the DI style of merge-train-reconciler.ts). Async exec only — no execSync (server-reachable code).
- AC: checkBranchMergeability returns 'clean' for a branch that merges into origin/<target> without conflicts, 'conflicts' when merge-tree reports conflicts, and 'unknown' on exec failure — proven by unit tests with an injected exec runner
- AC: The probe never mutates the workspace: no merge commits, no index changes, no HEAD moves (merge-tree only; no 'git merge' fallback)
- AC: No execSync anywhere in the new module; all git calls use promisified exec with timeouts
close_reason: Added async non-destructive checkBranchMergeability probe with injected exec runner and unit tests for clean/conflicts/unknown outcomes

title: pan-1762: Footprint overlap signal for flywheel launch ordering
description:

Deliver the soft signal where the orchestrator already looks: (1) render predictedConflictsWith in the flywheel merge-queue CLI/status output the orchestrator consumes (src/cli/commands/flywheel.ts or the status payload it reads); (2) add launch-ordering guidance to docs/flywheel-brief.md: prefer not co-starting issues whose predicted footprints heavily overlap; treat it as a soft preference, never a gate. Keep the diff minimal — this bead is data plumbing plus one brief paragraph.

title: pan-1762: Foreman protocol in roles/work.md
description:
Evolve the 'Parallel work via subagents' section of roles/work.md into the foreman protocol. The work agent, when the plan is swarm-eligible (multiple unblocked items with populated files_scope): (1) compute waves via groupItemsByWave(); (2) within a wave, partition by hasFileOverlap() — non-overlapping items dispatch in parallel, overlapping items serialize; items with missing files_scope or files_scope_confidence: low are treated as overlapping-with-everything (serialize, never refuse); (3) per item choose a dispatch tier: in-context subagent with worktree isolation for cheap/mechanical items (< ~15 min), `pan slot spawn` registered slot agent for heavy items or when durability matters; (4) on slot completion run `pan slot merge` — never merge red; on conflict, resolve in the foreman's own context then merge; (5) at convergence items (metadata.requiresSynthesis), compose an in-context synthesis digest of what the merged parents actually did and inline it into the convergent item's dispatch prompt; (6) failure protocol: one redo with feedback, then serial fallback in the foreman's own context (extends the existing subagent protocol); (7) checkpoint wave progress in .pan/continue.json after each wave; (8) reconciliation-on-resume: a respawned foreman runs `pan slot status`, reconciles statusOverrides + slot branch state + running slot agents, adopts orphans, and continues the correct wave. Cap concurrent heavy slots (default ~3) to avoid bun install/build contention. Keep the existing in-context-only fan-out path for plans without scope metadata.
- AC: roles/work.md defines the full foreman loop: waves, overlap partition with the conservative missing/low-confidence rule, two dispatch tiers with selection criteria
- AC: Verify-then-merge is mandatory: the protocol forbids merging a slot whose verify_commands failed, and routes conflicts to foreman-context resolution
- AC: Synthesis digests at requiresSynthesis convergence points are composed in-context and inlined into the convergent item's dispatch prompt
- AC: The protocol includes wave checkpointing in continue.json and an explicit reconciliation-on-resume step using pan slot status

title: pan-1762: Surface scope drift in review status and review context
description:
Make the recorded scopeDrift visible to the review role: when review is triggered for an issue, read the workspace continue state's scopeDrift and (1) store a compact summary on the issue's review status record (src/lib/review-status.ts or wherever the review record is composed), and (2) include a short scope-drift section in the review role's spawn context (where the review prompt is assembled in src/lib/agents.ts / the review trigger path) listing out-of-scope files so reviewers scrutinize undeclared changes. Exact wiring points may shift during implementation — keep the change minimal and confined to the review trigger path.
- AC: An issue with recorded drift shows the drift summary in the review role's spawn context (out-of-scope files listed)
- AC: Issues without drift data trigger review exactly as before (no errors, no empty sections)

title: pan-1762: Predicted conflicts in merge queue from declared footprints
description:
Extend computeMergeQueue (src/lib/flywheel-merge-order.ts): for each queue item, load the declared footprint (issueFootprintForIssue); compute pairwise predicted overlap on declared footprints (hotspots excluded) and expose it as predictedConflictsWith: string[] on MergeQueueItem, distinct from the existing actual conflictsWith (from changedFilesVsMain). Convergence rule: when a branch exists with real commits, actual conflict data is authoritative — predicted is supplementary display data and must not change batchGroup partitioning. Surface predictedConflictsWith in the /api/flywheel/merge-queue response. Unit tests cover predicted-vs-actual distinction and the no-footprint case (empty predictions, identical behavior to today).
- AC: MergeQueueItem carries predictedConflictsWith computed from declared footprints with hotspots excluded, separate from actual conflictsWith
- AC: Actual conflict data remains authoritative for batch/serialize partitioning; issues without footprints behave exactly as today; tests pass

title: pan-1762: pan slot CLI command group (spawn/merge/status)
description:
Create src/cli/commands/slot.ts and register a `pan slot` command group in src/cli/index.ts, giving the foreman deterministic primitives: `pan slot spawn <issue> <item-id> [--model <m>] [--json]` (allocates next slot number, createSlotWorktree + spawnSlotAgent, prints agent id/branch/worktree); `pan slot merge <issue> <n> [--json]` (resolves the item bound to the slot, runSlotVerify in the slot worktree, refuses to merge on red verify with the failing command output, mergeSlotBranch on green, reports conflictFiles on conflict); `pan slot status <issue> [--json]` (lists each slot: number, item id, branch, worktree path, agent state from state.json, verify state if recorded, merged-into-feature-branch yes/no via git ancestry). Slot→item binding persisted in the slot worktree's .pan/ directory at spawn time. Add `pan slot` to the SKILLS-CONVENTION exclusion list (power-user verb documented in docs/SWARM.md and roles/work.md — no wrapper skill).
- AC: pan slot spawn creates the worktree/branch/registered agent and prints (or emits as JSON) agent id, branch, and worktree path

title: pan-1744: Replace clearStuckForks blanket-fail with a boot recovery pass (dispatch by stage + retry guard)
description:
Replace the blanket clearStuckForks() call in src/dashboard/server/main.ts boot sequence with a recovery pass. Implement recoverStuckForks() (near runForkPipeline so it can call it) that, for each conversation from getStuckForks(): (a) if fork_retry_count >= 2, mark failed with the current/standard message and skip; (b) otherwise call incrementForkRetryCount BEFORE attempting (so a crash during recovery still burns a retry and cannot loop); (c) parse fork_request — if missing/unparseable (legacy fork), mark failed and skip; (d) dispatch by observed state: if the tmux session is alive AND the runtime mirror reports active/waiting-on-human, the fork actually finished — markConversationActive + updateForkStatus(name, null) and do NOT kill it; otherwise re-enter the resumable runForkPipeline reconstructed from fork_request (re-resolving the parent conversation by name). Schedule the pass a few seconds after boot via setTimeout (not inline) so tmux/runtime-mirror/lifecycle services have settled; wrap each fork's recovery in try/catch so one failure cannot abort the others. Keep clearStuckForks only if still needed as the narrow terminal fail-marker, otherwise remove it and update/remove its test.
- AC: Boot no longer blanket-marks in-flight forks failed; recoverStuckForks() runs on a short post-boot delay and processes each conversation returned by getStuckForks().
- AC: Tmux-alive AND runtime-mirror-active fork is marked active with fork_status cleared and is never killed (test: simulate live session+mirror -> stays active).
- AC: A fork with a handoff doc already on disk is recovered by re-entering runForkPipeline, which reuses the doc and re-spawns/re-injects rather than re-authoring (test asserts no re-author).
- AC: A pre-doc (authoring-stage) fork is recovered by re-running the pipeline from scratch (test: in-flight with no doc and no tmux -> pipeline re-runs).
- AC: fork_retry_count is incremented BEFORE the attempt; a fork at retry_count >= 2 is marked failed and not re-attempted (test: third boot for the same fork yields failed, not a fourth attempt).
- AC: A legacy in-flight fork with no fork_request is marked failed (graceful fallback, no crash).
- AC: One fork's recovery throwing does not prevent the others from being processed (per-fork try/catch).
close_reason: Replaced startup blanket fork failure with delayed recoverStuckForks dispatch, retry guarding, legacy fallback, and tests.

Only print the green success block when forkStatus is null (truly complete).

title: pan-1744: Give in-flight fork pipelines a bounded grace window on shutdown
description:
Reduce how often recovery is even needed by letting in-flight forks finish before the process exits. Track in-flight fork pipelines (e.g. a module-level Set of in-flight runForkPipeline promises/names registered at launch and cleared on settle) and, in the handleShutdownSignal handler in src/dashboard/server/main.ts (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP), await their completion with a bounded timeout (e.g. up to ~10s) before process.exit. The wait MUST be bounded — if a fork hangs past the window, log it and exit anyway so a restart is never blocked indefinitely (boot recovery then catches that fork). This is the common-case complement: a pan reload during fork authoring lets the fork finish instead of relying on recovery.
- AC: In-flight fork pipelines are registered when launched and de-registered when they settle (success or failure).
- AC: On SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP the shutdown handler awaits in-flight forks up to a bounded timeout before exiting.
- AC: The wait is bounded: a fork that does not finish within the window is logged and the process exits anyway (test: a never-settling in-flight fork does not hang shutdown past the cap).
- AC: With no in-flight forks, shutdown is not measurably delayed (the grace path is a no-op when the in-flight set is empty).
close_reason: Tracked in-flight fork pipelines and added a bounded 10s shutdown wait with fake-timer tests.

title: pan-1744: fork-client: distinguish deadline-expiry-while-in-flight from completion

Today the poll loop returns the latest state whether it broke because forkStatus cleared/failed OR because the deadline expired with forkStatus still in flight. Add an explicit signal — e.g. a `timedOut: boolean` field on the returned ForkResultConv — set true only when the loop exits via the deadline with a non-null, non-failed forkStatus. Completion (forkStatus null) and failure (forkStatus 'failed') leave timedOut false.

- AC: A completed fork (forkStatus becomes null) returns timedOut=false; a failed fork (forkStatus 'failed') returns timedOut=false.

title: pan-1744: Make runForkPipeline resume-safe (reuse existing handoff doc, skip spawn when tmux already alive)
description:
Make runForkPipeline in src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts safe to call a second time for an already-in-flight fork, so boot recovery can re-enter it without re-authoring or double-spawning. Two idempotency guards in the handoff/summary path: (1) if the fork row already has handoff_doc_path set AND the file exists on disk, reuse that doc text instead of re-authoring (skip authorHandoffExternal / requestHandoffFromAgent); (2) before spawnConversationSession, if the tmux session already exists (sessionExists), skip the spawn and proceed straight to injection + markConversationActive. The normal first-run path (no doc yet, no tmux) must behave exactly as today. Keep the change confined to re-entrancy; do not alter authoring, fallback, or delivery semantics for the first run.

title: pan-1744: Add fork_request and fork_retry_count columns + DB accessors to the conversations table
description:

In src/lib/database/conversations-db.ts: read both columns into mapRow/the Conversation type (forkRequest: string|null, forkRetryCount: number), and add accessors — getStuckForks() returning conversations where fork_status IS NOT NULL AND fork_status != 'failed', setForkRequest(name, json), and incrementForkRetryCount(name) returning the new count. Define a single ForkRequest TypeScript shape capturing every runForkPipeline argument needed to re-enter (forkMode, summaryModel, localSummaryOnly, includeThinkingInSummary, summaryHarness, handoffFocus, handoffAuthor, handoffAuthorModel, handoffAuthorHarness, parent conversation name, sessionId) and export it for the persist and recovery beads to share. Newest ready generation supersedes older ready ones. Also export a force-reassemble entry for the API.

title: pan-1700: Deacon backstop: re-send the continue prompt to a work agent stalled since resume with zero user records
description:
Add a new deacon patrol in src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts (model it on nudgeIdleWorkAgentsWithOpenBeads, deacon.ts:5899) and register it in runPatrol (deacon.ts:4818). For each running work agent with a live tmux session that is idle (isAgentIdleForNudge), detect a stalled resume: zero user records appended to the session JSONL since the last resume (via the shared transcript-landing helper, keyed off the resume entry the resume path already appends to continue state, or the agent's resume timestamp). When stalled, re-send the continue prompt (the default 'You are resuming work on <ISSUE>…' message, or the redelivered kickoff if kickoffDelivered===false), bounded by a per-agent cooldown file (mirror the .last-bead-nudge pattern). Do not fire for orphans (handled by recoverOrphanedAgents), closed issues, paused/troubled agents, or agents that already have user records since resume.
- AC: A new patrol identifies a stalled resume: status=running, role=work, live tmux, isAgentIdleForNudge, and ZERO user records in the session JSONL since the agent's last resume.
- AC: On detection it re-sends the continue prompt (not a generic ping), using the redelivered kickoff prompt when kickoffDelivered===false, otherwise the default resume continue message.
- AC: A per-agent cooldown (own marker file) prevents re-sending more than once per cooldown window; an agent with ANY user record since resume is skipped.
- AC: Orphans (no live tmux), closed issues, and paused/troubled agents are skipped — consistent with the existing patrol's gating.
- AC: The patrol is registered in runPatrol and its actions are logged like the sibling patrols.
- AC: Tests assert: a zero-user-record idle resumed agent is re-sent once then cooled down; an agent with a user record since resume is never re-sent; an orphan/closed/paused agent is skipped. typecheck + lint pass.

title: pan-1700: resumeAgent: verify the auto-continue prompt landed and redeliver once before flagging success
description:
In resumeAgent (src/lib/agents.ts, the non-pi/non-codex Claude branch at ~4406-4416), take a transcript snapshot (transcript-landing-helper) just before delivering the auto-continue prompt. After deliverAgentMessage returns, poll within a bounded window for a new user record to appear in the session JSONL. If none appears, redeliver the same effectiveMessage once and poll again. Only set messageDelivered=true and call markKickoffRedelivered AFTER landing is confirmed; if it never lands, set messageDelivered=false and log so the deacon backstop / existing kickoff machinery re-sends — never record a phantom delivery (the PAN-1491 failure). Keep the existing waitForReadySignal gate and the pi/codex branches unchanged.

- AC: After delivery, the code polls (bounded) for a new user record; if none lands, it redelivers the same message exactly once and polls again.
- AC: messageDelivered=true and markKickoffRedelivered() are set ONLY after a landed user record is confirmed; if landing never confirms, messageDelivered=false and the failure is logged (no phantom success).
- AC: The pi and codex resume branches and the existing waitForReadySignal gate are unchanged.
- AC: Tests (using vi.useFakeTimers for the bounded poll/redelivery) assert: landing-on-first-delivery → no redelivery + messageDelivered true; never-lands → exactly one redelivery + messageDelivered false; lands-after-redelivery → messageDelivered true and markKickoffRedelivered called once when redeliveringKickoff.
- AC: typecheck, lint, and the resume tests pass.

title: pan-1700: Shared helper: detect whether a user record landed in a session JSONL after a snapshot point
description:
Add a small, pure, well-unit-tested helper that answers 'has a user record been appended to this session JSONL since snapshot S?'. It resolves the JSONL via sessionFilePath(workspace, sessionId) (src/lib/paths.ts:230), reads the file tail tolerantly (ignore unparseable trailing lines, mirroring waitForReadySignal's JSON.parse try/catch), and returns enough to take a 'before' snapshot and compare 'after' (e.g. a count of user-type records, or the timestamp/uuid of the last user record). It must never throw on a missing/empty/mid-write file — return a safe default. This is consumed by both resume-verify-redeliver and deacon-backstop-patrol; keep it free of dashboard-server imports so it does not bloat the agents.ts/deacon.ts import graph.
- AC: A helper resolves the Claude session JSONL from (workspace, sessionId) via sessionFilePath and returns a snapshot of user-record presence (count or last-user-record identity).

- AC: The helper has no import dependency on dashboard-server services (verified by it living in a lib module importable from both agents.ts and deacon.ts without cycles).
- AC: Unit tests cover: no new record, a new user record, an assistant-only append, and the three not-throwing cases; typecheck + lint pass.
close_reason: Added shared transcript landing snapshot helper with tolerant JSONL parsing and unit coverage for missing, malformed, user, assistant, and tool-only records.

title: pan-1700: Supervisor echo-confirmation before Enter (shared root-cause fix; also resolves #1697)
description:
In src/lib/channels/pty-supervisor.ts, change injectPtyMessage so that after writing the message content it observes the child PTY output stream (child.onData) and confirms a normalized prefix of the message echoed in the input box BEFORE writing the standalone \r. Strip ANSI and normalize whitespace before matching; match a bounded prefix (mirror the tmux verifyLine slice(0,40) approach in src/lib/tmux.ts:790-858). Poll up to a bounded window (~1.5s) × 2 attempts, re-writing the content once on the first miss. On confirmation success, proceed exactly as today (echo-to-stdout transcript mirror unchanged, send \r, log). On final confirmation failure, make createPtySupervisorServer return a non-2xx response so postUnixSocketJson (src/lib/agents.ts:1303-1309) rejects and deliverAgentMessage records an honest supervisor failure (falling through to the tmux path in auto mode). Reconcile the caller side: raise the supervisor POST timeout in deliverAgentMessage (src/lib/agents.ts:1375, currently 2000ms) to exceed the confirmation budget so a legitimate confirmation is not cut short. Preserve all behavior for the success path; do not change the payload schema or the stdout transcript mirror.
- AC: After writing content, injectPtyMessage waits for a normalized (ANSI-stripped, whitespace-collapsed) prefix of the message to appear in the child PTY output before sending \r.
- AC: On confirmation timeout the content write is retried exactly once; on a second timeout the POST returns a non-2xx status (not 200).
- AC: When confirmation succeeds, the success path is byte-for-byte unchanged: content written, ~300ms settle, standalone \r sent, message echoed to stdout exactly once, socket_write logged.
- AC: deliverAgentMessage's supervisor POST timeout is raised to exceed the supervisor confirmation window so a confirmed delivery returns { ok:true, path:'supervisor' } within budget (no spurious tmux fallback).
- AC: Subprocess tests (extending src/lib/channels/__tests__/pty-supervisor.test.ts) cover both cases: a child that echoes its input → POST 200 and the message is delivered; a child whose PTY output never reflects the input → POST non-2xx after one retry, within budget.
- AC: deliver-agent-message tests assert that a non-2xx supervisor response is surfaced as a supervisor failure (strict 'supervisor' method throws; 'auto' falls through to tmux).
- AC: npm run build, typecheck, lint, and the supervisor + delivery test suites pass.
close_reason: Addressed inspection feedback by replacing real delay waits with fake-timer coverage and keeping subprocess tests as fast smoke coverage.

title: pan-1712: Add `pan conv jsonl <conv-id>` command (alias `transcript`) + registration + tests
description:
Add `src/cli/commands/conversations/jsonl.ts` exporting `jsonlAction(convId: string, opts: { json?: boolean })`. Parse convId as an integer (exit 1 with a clear stderr error if non-numeric); look up the conversation with `getConversationById()` (exit 1 'Conversation <N> not found' if missing); call `resolveConversationTranscript(conv.cwd, conv.claudeSessionId)`. Plain mode: on 'ok' print the absolute path to stdout and exit 0; on 'expired' print a Claude-Code-retention message to stderr and exit 1; on 'unknown' print a 'no claude_session_id recorded for this conversation' message to stderr and exit 1. `--json` mode: print one JSON object `{ status, path, conversationId, claudeSessionId, cwd }` to stdout and exit 0 regardless of status. Register the subcommand in `src/cli/commands/conversations/index.ts`: `.command('jsonl <conv-id>').alias('transcript').description(...).option('--json', ...)`, with a description that states the argument is the conversation id (the number in pan.localhost/conv/<N>) — distinct from `pan conv show`. - AC: On status 'ok', prints only the absolute JSONL path to stdout and exits 0.
- AC: On 'expired' prints a retention-explaining message to stderr and exits 1; on 'unknown' prints a no-claude_session_id message to stderr and exits 1.

- AC: `--json` prints a single object `{ status, path, conversationId, claudeSessionId, cwd }` to stdout and exits 0 for ok/expired/unknown alike (status conveyed in the payload).

title: pan-1712: Add status-aware resolveConversationTranscript() helper + tests
description:
Create `src/lib/conversations/transcript-path.ts` exporting `resolveConversationTranscript(cwd: string | null | undefined, claudeSessionId: string | null | undefined): { path: string | null; status: 'ok' | 'expired' | 'unknown' }`. Derive the path with the existing `sessionFilePath(cwd, claudeSessionId)` from src/lib/paths.ts. Resolution order, mirroring conv-find.py's resolve_session_file(): (1) if claudeSessionId is falsy → { path: null, status: 'unknown' }; (2) compute derived = sessionFilePath(cwd, sessionId); if it exists on disk → { path: derived, status: 'ok' }; (3) else glob `~/.claude/projects/*/<sessionId>.jsonl` (one level only) and return the first match as { path: match, status: 'ok' }; (4) else → { path: derived, status: 'expired' }. Add a unit test file under src/lib/conversations covering all four outcomes with a temp HOME / ~/.claude/projects fixture. This helper is the single source of truth for status-aware transcript resolution that the CLI command and (transitively) the skill depend on — keep its status taxonomy and return shape stable.
- AC: Exported `resolveConversationTranscript(cwd, claudeSessionId)` returns `{ path: string | null, status: 'ok' | 'expired' | 'unknown' }` and derives via sessionFilePath() from src/lib/paths.ts.
- AC: Returns status 'ok' with the absolute derived path when `sessionFilePath(cwd, sessionId)` exists on disk.
- AC: When the derived path is absent, returns status 'ok' with the first `~/.claude/projects/*/<sessionId>.jsonl` glob match (one directory level), preserving conv-find.py's fallback for cwd-encoding drift.
- AC: Returns 'expired' (path = the expected derived path) when claudeSessionId is set but no JSONL exists on disk or via glob; returns 'unknown' (path = null) when claudeSessionId is null/empty.
- AC: Unit tests cover all four outcomes (ok-derived, ok-glob, expired, unknown) using a temp ~/.claude/projects fixture; `npm run typecheck` and the new test pass.
close_reason: Fixed inspection blockers: canonical spec is clean; pipeline runtime status no longer writes metadata into .pan/specs

title: pan-1705: cancelQueries before invalidateQueries on panopticon:reconnected so restart-stalled fetches recover instantly
description:
In src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/CommandDeck/index.tsx, the panopticon:reconnected handler (~lines 1030-1037) currently calls only queryClient.invalidateQueries(). Because React Query dedupes against an in-flight promise, a messages fetch that hung across a server restart blocks the refetch until the 20s fetchWithTimeout fires. Update the handler to call queryClient.cancelQueries() (abort all in-flight queries) BEFORE queryClient.invalidateQueries() (refetch active ones), so a conversation click that was loading when the server restarted resolves on reconnect in ~0s instead of ~20s. Keep the existing console.log; the handler may become async or fire-and-forget the cancel (void queryClient.cancelQueries()).
- AC: The panopticon:reconnected handler calls queryClient.cancelQueries() before queryClient.invalidateQueries().
- AC: Manual/observed: with a conversation panel stuck on Loading… because a server restart killed an in-flight messages fetch, dispatching panopticon:reconnected (transport reconnect) clears the spinner and shows messages without waiting the full 20s timeout and without a page reload.
- AC: Frontend typecheck/lint pass; no other reconnect listeners (EventRouter, NoResumeBanner) are altered.

title: pan-1704: Implement Tier 1 — lossless in-session /model switch via the PTY supervisor with statusline verification and Tier 2 fallback
description:
In the switch-model route, when strategy.tier === 1 (useModelCommand): do NOT kill the session and do NOT markRespawnPending. Persist the new model in the DB (setConversationModel), then deliver `/model <targetModel>` via deliverAgentMessage(conv.tmuxSession, '/model <targetModel>', 'switch-model-tier1', resolveConversationDeliveryMethod(conv)). Verify acceptance: poll capturePane(conv.tmuxSession) for the target model's displayName (getModelCapabilitySync(...).displayName) in the statusline within a bounded timeout (~5s). On success return active with the new model (sessionAlive:true, no respawn). On delivery error, timeout, or missed echo, fall back to the Tier 2 path (kill + respawn --resume, no compaction) so the switch always completes. Confirm the exact `/model` argument form Claude Code accepts (full id vs alias) during implementation and encode it.

- AC: Tier 1 persists the new model to the DB before delivery so a fallback respawn uses the correct model
- AC: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm test pass

title: pan-1704: Refactor switch-model route to be tier-aware (defer kill) and replace maybeCompactBeforeRespawn's modelChanged force-flag with a window-fit shouldCompact gate
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts (postConversationSwitchModelRoute, ~2401-2551): compute the tier BEFORE killing the session. Gather inputs — currentModel=conv.model, targetModel=model, harnessChanged, providerRoutingChanged = getProviderExportsForModel(currentModel) !== getProviderExportsForModel(targetModel), contextUsage = computeContextUsage(sessionFile, conv.model) to get contextTokens (estimatedTokens) and currentObservedCeiling (maxObservedInputTokens), cliproxyRouted = getProviderForModelSync(targetModel).name==='openai' && await getProviderAuthMode(targetModel)==='subscription', registryWindow = getModelCapabilitySync(resolveModelIdSync(targetModel)).contextWindow → effectiveTargetWindow via getEffectiveTargetWindow → strategy = decideSwitchStrategy(...). Wire Tier 4 (harnessChanged: existing converter branch, verbatim), Tier 3 (kill+markRespawnPending → compact via the updated maybeCompactBeforeRespawn with shouldCompact:true → respawn --resume), Tier 2 (kill+markRespawnPending → respawn --resume, shouldCompact:false → no compaction). Leave Tier 1 to the next bead: for now a Tier-1-eligible decision should fall through to the Tier 2 path (kill+respawn --resume, no compaction) so this bead is independently correct and mergeable. ALSO update maybeCompactBeforeRespawn (conversation-compaction.ts:176) and MaybeCompactBeforeRespawnOptions: replace `modelChanged: boolean` with `shouldCompact: boolean`; drop the internal COMPACT_TOKEN_THRESHOLD/estimateContextTokens gate; keep the isBackgroundFeatureEnabled('summaryFork') early-return; compact only when shouldCompact && summaryFork enabled. Update the single caller accordingly.
- AC: The session kill (formerly conversations.ts:2458) is moved to run only on Tier 2/3/4; markRespawnPending is set only on respawn tiers
- AC: Tier 2 (cross-provider same-harness, context fits window): respawn with --resume and NO compaction; the session JSONL gains no compact_boundary (AC#2 of the issue)
- AC: Tier 3 (context > effectiveTargetWindow*0.8): compaction runs and the summary references the correct pre-switch token count; respawn --resume follows (AC#3 of the issue)

title: pan-1704: Add pure tier-decision module (getEffectiveTargetWindow + decideSwitchStrategy) with unit tests
description:
Create src/lib/conversations/switch-strategy.ts with two PURE, side-effect-free functions plus a SAFETY_FACTOR = 0.8 constant. (1) getEffectiveTargetWindow({ registryWindow, currentObservedCeiling, cliproxyRouted, providerRoutingChanged }): number — returns CLIPROXY_CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW (150000) when cliproxyRouted; else max(1_000_000, registryWindow) when !providerRoutingChanged && currentObservedCeiling > registryWindow (mirrors the extended-context inference in conversation-service.ts:1148-1152); else registryWindow. (2) decideSwitchStrategy({ harnessChanged, providerRoutingChanged, contextTokens, effectiveTargetWindow }): { tier: 1|2|3|4, compact: boolean, useModelCommand: boolean } — Tier 4 first when harnessChanged; else Tier 3 (compact:true) when contextTokens > effectiveTargetWindow * SAFETY_FACTOR; else Tier 1 (useModelCommand:true) when !providerRoutingChanged; else Tier 2. The route (next bead) computes the async inputs and feeds these. Ship src/lib/conversations/__tests__/switch-strategy.test.ts covering every branch including the regression cases.
- AC: getEffectiveTargetWindow returns 150000 (CLIPROXY_CODEX_CONTEXT_WINDOW) for cliproxyRouted targets regardless of observed ceiling
- AC: getEffectiveTargetWindow lifts to 1_000_000 when !providerRoutingChanged and currentObservedCeiling (e.g. 206000) > registryWindow (200000); returns registryWindow when ceiling <= window
- AC: getEffectiveTargetWindow does NOT lift the window for a cross-provider (providerRoutingChanged) non-cliproxy target even if the source ceiling exceeds the registry window (H6 guard)
- AC: decideSwitchStrategy returns tier 4 when harnessChanged regardless of all other inputs
- AC: decideSwitchStrategy returns tier 1 (useModelCommand:true, compact:false) when !harnessChanged && !providerRoutingChanged && contextTokens <= effectiveTargetWindow*0.8
- AC: decideSwitchStrategy returns tier 2 (useModelCommand:false, compact:false) when providerRoutingChanged && contextTokens fits the window
- AC: decideSwitchStrategy returns tier 3 (compact:true) when contextTokens > effectiveTargetWindow*0.8, for both same- and cross-routing
- AC: Regression: 206000 tokens, same-routing Anthropic switch, effective window inferred to 1_000_000 → decideSwitchStrategy returns tier 1, compact:false (the exact observed incident at the decision layer)
- AC: Module is pure: no fs/network/process imports; unit tests run without mocks for the decision functions; npm run typecheck and the new test file pass
close_reason: Added pure switch strategy module with effective window and tier decision logic plus unit tests.

description:
In src/cli/commands/start.ts, classify the recovery/gate failure (via isTransientBdError). When the underlying failure is a transient/lock error — or when the issue's beads are known to exist (live count seen previously OR non-empty JSONL) — do NOT print 'No beads tasks found … Planning must create a task breakdown' and do NOT trigger destructive vBRIEF re-materialization. Instead print an honest message (e.g. 'beads database was temporarily locked by a concurrent operation; retried N times — re-run `pan start <id>` shortly') and exit with a distinct, non-zero, retryable status code. The 'planning must create beads' guidance must only appear when beads are genuinely absent (live query succeeded and returned empty AND JSONL empty).
- AC: A transient/lock failure during gate or recovery prints a 'temporarily locked — retry' message, NOT 'Planning must create a task breakdown'
- AC: A transient read failure does NOT trigger destructive vBRIEF re-materialization (no bead deletion on a lock error)
- AC: 'planning must create beads' guidance still appears only when beads are genuinely absent (live query returned empty AND JSONL empty)
- AC: The transient-failure exit code is distinct from the genuine-no-beads exit code so callers/Flywheel can distinguish retryable from re-plan
close_reason: Added honest retryable messaging for transient bd lock failures

title: pan-1629: Route the `pan start` beads-gate query and `beads-query.ts` through lock + retry (get the LIVE count, not stale JSONL)
description:
Make the beads-resolution gate reliably reflect live Dolt under contention. In src/cli/commands/start.ts: the gate (`hasBeadsTasks`/`countBeadsTasks` at lines 541/575, used only within start.ts) and `validateBeadsMatchPlan` must obtain the live count via the lock+retry helper before falling back to the JSONL snapshot — so a transient `bd list` failure retries and succeeds instead of spuriously returning 0 and triggering recovery. Prefer a bounded retry around the existing call (sync retry loop) or an async start-path helper; enumerate callers (all in start.ts) before changing signatures. In src/lib/beads-query.ts, wrap `queryBeadsForIssuePromise`'s `bd list` in retry too (the dashboard start-agent path). The JSONL fallback remains only as a genuine last resort.
- AC: Under simulated lock contention, the start gate retries `bd list` and returns the true live count (>0 when beads exist) instead of falling back to a stale/empty JSONL
- AC: queryBeadsForIssuePromise in beads-query.ts retries on transient lock errors before the JSONL fallback
- AC: No signature change leaks beyond start.ts callers; existing start.ts tests stay green
close_reason: Routed pan start beads gate and beads-query live reads through runBdWithRetry

title: pan-1629: Route create-beads/dedup (`clearBeadsForIssue` → `bd list`) through the cross-process lock + retry
description:
In src/lib/vbrief/beads.ts, make the dedup path resilient: route `listBeadsForIssue` and `clearBeadsForIssue`'s bd invocations through runBdWithRetry, and make the whole `createBeadsFromVBriefPromise` critical section additionally hold the cross-process lock (compose with the existing in-process withBdMutexPromise — do not replace it). The 'dedup failed: list failed:' abort (beads.ts:254) must no longer fire on transient lock contention; it should only fire on a genuine, retries-exhausted failure. Keep the existing bd-ping/doctor recovery and the create logic intact.
- AC: listBeadsForIssue/clearBeadsForIssue retry on transient lock errors instead of immediately returning 'list failed'
- AC: createBeadsFromVBrief holds the cross-process lock for its bd-touching section, composed with (not replacing) the existing in-process mutex
- AC: Existing src/lib/vbrief/__tests__/create-beads.test.ts stays green (dedup-failure-on-genuine-error cases still abort)
close_reason: Routed create-beads dedup through bd process lock and retry

title: pan-1629: Add a cross-process bd lock + bounded-retry wrapper (mirroring restart-lock.ts)
description:
Create src/lib/bd-process-lock.ts providing `withBdProcessLock(caller, fn, opts?)` and a `runBdWithRetry` helper. The lock is an atomic O_EXCL lockfile under `getPanopticonHome()/locks/bd-<slug-of-resolved-shared-beads-dir>.lock`, mirroring src/lib/restart-lock.ts: holder = {pid, ts, caller}; stale-reclaim when holder PID is dead OR age > bound; bounded acquisition wait with backoff+jitter; ALWAYS release in finally. Key the lockfile on the RESOLVED shared Dolt `.beads` dir (resolve `.beads/redirect` → main repo) so all worktrees of one project share one lock. `runBdWithRetry` wraps a bd invocation: acquire the process lock, run, and on isTransientBdError (from the classifier bead) retry with bounded exponential backoff+jitter; surface a typed/contextful failure when retries are exhausted. Provide both a Promise API and an Effect variant consistent with restart-lock.ts. This is the concurrency foundation the wiring beads build on — get the lock KEY (shared DB, not workspace) and stale-reclaim right or the bug persists / deadlocks.
- AC: withBdProcessLock serializes across SEPARATE processes (two concurrent acquirers do not both hold it); proven by a test that forks/simulates two holders
- AC: Lockfile path is derived from the resolved shared Dolt `.beads` dir so two worktrees of the same project share one lock
- AC: A stale lock (dead PID or age beyond bound) is reclaimed; a live holder is respected; the lock is always released in finally
- AC: runBdWithRetry retries on isTransientBdError with bounded backoff and stops after the bound, surfacing a typed transient failure (tests use vi.useFakeTimers — no real backoff sleeps)
- AC: Acquisition wait is bounded so a wedged holder degrades to a typed transient failure rather than hanging forever
close_reason: Added cross-process bd lock and bounded retry helper

title: pan-1629: Add a conservative transient/lock bd-error classifier
description:
Add a pure predicate `isTransientBdError(error): boolean` (e.g. in a new src/lib/bd-process-lock.ts or src/lib/bd-mutex.ts) that returns true ONLY for Dolt/beads lock-contention signatures observed when a concurrent process holds the DB lock — and false for everything else, especially 'genuine empty result' (which is exit 0 + `[]`, never an error). First confirm the real Dolt lock stderr text by running concurrent `bd list` against a throwaway temp DB, then match those signatures conservatively (lock held / database is locked / resource temporarily unavailable / could not acquire). Cover the error shapes execFile/execFileSync produce (error.stderr, error.message, error.code). Default to NON-transient when uncertain.
- AC: isTransientBdError returns true for confirmed Dolt lock-contention stderr signatures
- AC: isTransientBdError returns false for a successful-but-empty bd list result and for genuine fatal errors (corrupt db, command-not-found)
- AC: Unit tests cover execFile error shapes (stderr string, message, code) and the empty-result false case
- AC: The confirmed Dolt lock stderr text is documented in a code comment citing how it was reproduced
close_reason: Added conservative transient bd lock classifier and unit tests

title: pan-1658: Unit-test the testStatus-from-green-CI reconciler
description:

Cover the happy path and every guard path so the reconciler can never mask a red build.
- AC: Test: reviewStatus=passed + testStatus=pending + non-terminal mergeStatus + OPEN PR + green CI check-runs ⇒ reconciler sets testStatus=passed (with testNotes) and reports one action.
- AC: Test: CI still pending ⇒ testStatus unchanged, no action; Test: CI failed/red ⇒ testStatus unchanged, no action (the reconciler never masks a red build).
- AC: Test: non-candidate states are untouched — testStatus='testing', testStatus already 'passed'/'skipped'/'failed', reviewStatus!='passed', and terminal mergeStatus (merged/merging/queued/verifying) each produce no mutation.

title: pan-1658: Add a deacon reconciler that flips stuck testStatus=pending → passed from green CI, and wire it into the patrol
description:
Add a reconciler function (e.g. reconcileTestStatusFromGreenCi(): Promise<string[]>) in src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts, modeled on reconcileClosedPrReadyForMerge (deacon.ts:3333). Guard on isGitHubAppConfigured(). For each entry in loadReviewStatuses() where reviewStatus==='passed' AND testStatus==='pending' (exactly) AND mergeStatus is non-terminal (pending/undefined/null — never merged/merging/queued/verifying) AND a parseable GitHub PR URL exists: resolve the current PR HEAD (getPullRequestState → headSha, the same primitive reconcileClosedPrReadyForMerge uses), skip if the PR is not OPEN or is merged, then evaluate the bead-1 CI greenness signal on that HEAD SHA. If green, call setReviewStatusSync(issueId, { testStatus: 'passed', testNotes: '<cite the CI run + short SHA>' }) — do NOT set readyForMerge or any other gate; it re-derives. Maintain a per-issue cooldown Map (set it on 'CI still pending' and on API error, like closedPrReadyReconcileCooldowns) so transient states don't burn the GitHub rate budget each patrol. Push a human-readable action string per reconciled issue and console.log it, matching the sibling reconcilers. Finally, wire the reconciler into the deacon patrol loop alongside the other reconcilers (deacon.ts ~5028-5041): call it, actions.push(...) the result, and addLog each action with state.patrolCycle.
- AC: For an issue with reviewStatus='passed', testStatus='pending', non-terminal mergeStatus, an OPEN unmerged PR, and green CI check-runs on the current HEAD, the reconciler sets testStatus='passed' with testNotes citing the CI run and the HEAD short SHA.
- AC: The reconciler never marks testStatus='passed' when CI on the current HEAD is pending/incomplete or failed/red; in those cases testStatus is left unchanged.
- AC: The candidate filter excludes testStatus values other than 'pending' (so a running 'testing' role, or already 'passed'/'skipped'/'failed', is never disturbed) and excludes terminal mergeStatus values (merged/merging/queued/verifying). The reconciler mutates only testStatus/testNotes — uatStatus, verificationStatus, reviewStatus, and readyForMerge are never written by it.
- AC: After the reconciler flips testStatus='passed', the existing event-driven derivation makes readyForMerge become true (assuming no other blocker/uat gate), so triggerMerge no longer returns 'Cannot merge: review and tests have not passed yet'.
- AC: The reconciler is guarded by isGitHubAppConfigured(), uses a per-issue cooldown on pending-CI and API-error outcomes to throttle GitHub calls, and returns string[] action descriptions consistent with the sibling reconcilers.
- AC: The reconciler is invoked once per deacon patrol cycle from the patrol loop, with its actions pushed into the patrol actions list and addLog'd, placed alongside reconcileMergedButReviewing / reconcileClosedPrReadyForMerge.
close_reason: Added reconcileTestStatusFromGreenCi, wired it into patrol, and verified with targeted eslint plus typecheck.

title: pan-1658: Add a check-runs-driven CI greenness signal for a commit SHA in github-app.ts
description:
Expose a reusable function in src/lib/github-app.ts that reports whether GitHub Actions CI is green on a given (owner, repo, sha), computed from the /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{sha}/check-runs endpoint ONLY. It must NOT depend on the combined commit-status (/status) endpoint, because that folds in the self-reported panopticon/review and panopticon/test contexts that are stuck/absent after a rebase (see continue.json hazard H1). The existing private getCommitCheckState already fetches check-runs; refactor/extend it (or add a sibling like getCiCheckRunsState) so the reconciler can ask a single, unambiguous question: 'are the CI check-runs on this exact SHA complete and all-successful?'. Return enough detail to distinguish green (≥1 success, 0 pending, 0 failed), not-yet (any pending/incomplete), and red (any failed). Empirically confirm against a real rebased PR that an absent/empty combined commit-status does not contaminate the signal before finalizing.
- AC: An exported function in github-app.ts returns a green verdict for a SHA only when there is ≥1 successful CI check-run AND zero pending/incomplete check-runs AND zero failed check-runs.
- AC: The greenness verdict is derived from the /commits/{sha}/check-runs endpoint only; it does NOT block on, or require, the panopticon/review or panopticon/test self-reported commit-statuses (a commit missing those statuses can still be judged green if its CI check-runs are green).
- AC: Any pending/incomplete check-run yields a 'not yet green' verdict (distinct from 'failed'); any failed/timed-out/cancelled check-run yields a 'red' verdict; a commit with zero CI check-runs is NOT green.
- AC: Existing callers of getCommitCheckState / getPullRequestState (checksPending/checksFailed behaviour and reconcileClosedPrReadyForMerge) are unchanged — typecheck, lint, and the existing github-app/PR-state tests stay green.
close_reason: Added getCiCheckRunsState check-runs-only CI verdict helper with unit coverage, typecheck/lint verification, and empirical check-runs/status confirmation.

title: pan-1647: Correct projectRootFromWorkspace to resolve a workspace to its true project root (+ round-trip regression test)
description:
In src/lib/vbrief/io.ts, fix projectRootFromWorkspace (lines 146-151) so a workspace path resolves to its true project root. Remove the `if (existsSync(join(workspacePath,'.git')) && existsSync(join(workspacePath, PAN_DIRNAME,'specs'))) return workspacePath;` short-circuit branch — a git worktree always satisfies it (.git is a gitdir file; .pan/specs/ is checked out from main), which is exactly why reads were resolving to <workspace>/.pan/specs/ instead of the main root where writeAutoStartVBrief wrote the spec. The function should return resolve(workspacePath,'..','..') for the reachable case. This is safe because both callers (sync findPlanSync io.ts:189 and async findPlan io.ts:489) already return null earlier unless issueIdFromWorkspacePath(workspacePath) is non-null, i.e. the path is a genuine <projectRoot>/workspaces/feature-<id>/ worktree two levels below its project root. Removing the branch may leave the existsSync/join imports unused locally — clean up only imports YOUR change orphans. Then add a regression test (in src/lib/vbrief/__tests__/, e.g. io.test.ts or a new auto-start-roundtrip.test.ts) that reproduces the WORKTREE shape: a temp <root>/workspaces/feature-pan-<n>/ with a `.git` file and a `.pan/specs/` directory (mirror the fixtures in create-beads.test.ts), call writeAutoStartVBrief(root, workspace, issue), then assert readWorkspacePlanSync(workspace) (and findPlanSync(workspace)) returns the synthesized plan (non-null, with the expected item). With execFile/bd mocked per create-beads.test.ts, extend the test through createBeadsFromVBrief(workspace) and assert created.length >= 1. The test MUST fail before the fix and pass after.
- AC: projectRootFromWorkspace(workspace) returns resolve(workspacePath,'..','..') (the main project root) for a feature-<id> worktree that has a .git file and a checked-out .pan/specs/ directory — it no longer returns the workspace itself.
- AC: A regression test reproduces the worktree shape (<root>/workspaces/feature-pan-<n>/ with a .git file and a .pan/specs/ dir) and asserts that after writeAutoStartVBrief(root, workspace, issue), readWorkspacePlanSync(workspace) and findPlanSync(workspace) resolve the synthesized plan (non-null). The test fails on the pre-fix code and passes on the post-fix code.
- AC: With execFile/bd mocked (per create-beads.test.ts), the round-trip writeAutoStartVBrief → createBeadsFromVBrief(workspace) returns success with created.length >= 1 — proving the 0-beads rollback no longer occurs.
- AC: Any import (existsSync/join) left unused in io.ts solely by removing the short-circuit branch is cleaned up; typecheck and lint pass.
close_reason: Fixed projectRootFromWorkspace to resolve workspaces to project root and added auto-start worktree round-trip regression covering createBeadsFromVBrief.

title: pan-1686: Add GET /api/workspaces/:issueId/uat-context endpoint
description:
Add a new route GET /api/workspaces/:issueId/uat-context in src/dashboard/server/routes/workspaces.ts. Compute changedFiles + diffStat by calling the exported review-context helpers against the workspace path (getDiffBase then getChangedFiles/getDiffStat), mapping ChangedFile to { path, status, additions, deletions }, truncated/sorted as already done by the helper. Wrap git work in try/catch: on any failure return changedFiles:[] and a null/empty diffStat. title: pan-1681: Add checkCompletedButUnsignaledTests deacon failsafe (mirrors checkCompletedButUnsignaledReviews)
description:
Add an exported async function checkCompletedButUnsignaledTests() in src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts, structurally mirroring checkCompletedButUnsignaledReviews (deacon.ts:2441): a SETTLE window (reuse the 5-minute constant pattern), a module-level dedup Map (mirror unsignaledReviewNudges) so each test cycle is nudged at most once, and the same guard discipline. For each issue with reviewStatus==='passed' and testStatus in {'testing','pending'}: resolve the workspace, locate .pan/test/result.json, and recover the verdict. When the test session agent-<id>-test is dead and the artifact exists → auto-complete via setReviewStatusSync({ testStatus: <status>, testNotes: <notes or default> }). When the session is alive but isAgentIdleForNudge reports idle past the settle window: on first pass nudge once (pan admin specialists done test <id> --status <status> [--notes ...], mirroring deacon.ts:2525); on a subsequent pass with the verdict still unsignaled, auto-complete from the artifact. When the artifact is ABSENT, never auto-complete to passed/failed — at most nudge once to write+POST. Skip closed issues (isIssueClosed) and stuck/ignored issues. Wire the function into the patrol loop in deacon.ts right after checkCompletedButUnsignaledReviews (~line 4790), pushing+logging its actions like the neighbours. Use vi.useFakeTimers in tests per the project's retry/delay test rule.
- AC: checkCompletedButUnsignaledTests() is exported from deacon.ts with settle-window + dedup-Map structure mirroring checkCompletedButUnsignaledReviews
- AC: Only acts on issues with reviewStatus==='passed' && testStatus∈{'testing','pending'}; skips closed (isIssueClosed) and stuck/ignored issues; gates on isAgentIdleForNudge(agent-<id>-test) + settle window

title: Conversation resume reattaches to a dead session instead of respawning
description:
## Problem

`POST /api/conversations/:name/resume` decides reattach-vs-respawn purely on
`tmuxSessionExists(conv.tmuxSession)` (src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts:2144).
When the session exists it reattaches and returns immediately; it only respawns
when the session is gone.

But a conversation's launcher.sh ends with a keep-alive loop:

    echo "Conversation session ended. Close this panel or click Resume..."
    while true; do sleep 60; done

So after Claude exits (crash, error, normal end), the **tmux session stays
alive** running that loop. `tmuxSessionExists` returns true, resume "reattaches"
to a corpse, and the dead Claude is never relaunched. The user clicks Resume and
nothing happens.

## Repro (observed 2026-06-06)

7 conversations died on Claude Code 2.1.158 hitting the legacy channels-flag
error (`server:panopticon-bridge · no MCP server configured`). Each left its
tmux session alive in the keep-alive loop. Hitting resume returned
`{"reattached": true}` and did NOT relaunch Claude. The only way to force a
clean respawn was to `tmux -L panopticon kill-session` first, then resume —
which then regenerated the launcher and relaunched correctly.

## Fix direction

Resume must detect "tmux session alive but Claude process dead" and treat it as
respawn, not reattach. Options:
- Check whether the live Claude/pty-supervisor process is actually running in
  the session (not just whether the tmux session name exists).
- Or have the launcher NOT keep the tmux session alive after Claude exits for
  the supervisor path (let the session die so the existing respawn branch fires).

Either way, a dead-Claude session should respawn on resume without manual
kill-session intervention.

## Acceptance
- Resuming a conversation whose Claude has exited (but whose tmux session is
  still in the keep-alive loop) relaunches Claude via spawnConversationSession,
  regenerating launcher.sh from current config.
- `reattached: true` is returned ONLY when Claude is genuinely still running.

Use fake timers for any grace/backoff waits per the repo's fake-timer rule; do not rely on real wall-clock delays.

title: pan-1617: Verify, persist, retry and escalate kickoff delivery at work-agent spawn
description:
In both work-agent spawn paths — spawnAgent (work) and spawnRun when role==='work' in src/lib/agents.ts — make kickoff delivery verified instead of fire-and-forget. Set state.kickoffDelivered=false before delivery and save. Ensure the kickoff is persisted to <agentDir>/initial-prompt.md for later resume re-delivery. After waitForReadySignal: if ready, deliver and inspect the DeliveryResult; on a confirmed path set state.kickoffDelivered=true and save. On ready=false OR an unverified delivery, retry the ready-wait + delivery ONCE. If it still fails, do NOT silently markAgentRunning as a healthy running agent — call recordAgentFailure with reason 'kickoff delivery failed' and emit an activity-level error so the failure surfaces. Set kickoffDelivered=true on the Pi (writePiAgentPrompt) and Codex (inline exec) delivery paths too so those harnesses are never falsely flagged (hazard H5). Per hazard H3, treat tmux-only ok as weak: confirm via the ready signal, and only flip kickoffDelivered=true when the agent reached the prompt and a delivery was issued.
- AC: spawnAgent and spawnRun(work) set kickoffDelivered=false before delivery and flip it to true only after a verified delivery (ready signal observed + delivery issued / supervisor ack)

title: pan-1617: Classify kickoff-stalled work agents as 'stalled' in determineHealthStatus
description:
Add an early stall rule to determineHealthStatus in src/dashboard/lib/health-filtering.ts, placed BEFORE the lastActivity-based staleness logic and AFTER the liveness (alive) check. When state.role==='work' && agentStatus==='running' && state.kickoffDelivered===false && (Date.now() - Date.parse(state.startedAt)) > 5*60*1000, return { status: 'stalled', reason: 'Work agent running with no kickoff delivered since spawn' }. The rule must NOT consult lastActivity (the heartbeat masks it — that is the root cause of the misreport). Only fire on explicit ===false, never undefined (hazard H1). Verify the /api/health/agents consumer (src/dashboard/server/routes/misc.ts) and any frontend status switch tolerate the new 'stalled' value; map it to an appropriate severity if a strict union exists (hazard H6).

title: pan-1614: Add bounded recoverStalledReviewConvoys() patrol (cooldown + attempt cap + escalate-once)
description:
In src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts add and export async function recoverStalledReviewConvoys(): Promise<string[]>, modeled structurally on recoverUnhealthyTestStack (deacon.ts:1291-1365). Iterate loadReviewStatuses(); for each issue: skip unless reviewStatus is in-flight ('reviewing' or 'pending'); skip if status.stuck or status.deaconIgnored. For the surviving candidates, resolve the canonical tracker state via getAutoCloseOutCanonicalState(issueId) and require it to equal 'in_review'. Call reviewConvoyLiveness(issueId); require anyLive===false AND anyGated===false. For a matching stalled convoy, apply a per-issue in-memory recovery-state Map<string,{lastAttempt:number;attempts:number;escalated:boolean}> with a 15-minute cooldown and a cap of 3 attempts: (a) if attempts>=cap, escalate once (emitActivityEntrySync level:'error' with a 'stalled-review-convoy-unrecoverable' message AND setReviewStatusSync stuck:true with a dedicated stuckReason e.g. 'review_convoy_unrecoverable'), then return; (b) if within cooldown, defer this cycle; (c) otherwise increment attempts, set lastAttempt, resolve workspace via resolveProjectFromIssueSync + findWorkspacePath (skip without consuming an attempt if unresolvable), and force-re-dispatch via Effect.runPromise(spawnReviewRoleForIssue({ issueId, workspace, branch: `feature/<lower>`, force: true })). On a successful dispatch, delete the issue's map entry. Push a descriptive string to the actions array for every branch (re-dispatched / deferred-cooldown / escalated / skipped-unresolvable). Wrap the body in try/catch like checkOrphanedReviewStatuses so one bad issue never aborts the whole patrol.
- AC: Re-dispatches the convoy (spawnReviewRoleForIssue with force:true) exactly when canonical state==='in_review' AND reviewStatus in {'reviewing','pending'} AND reviewConvoyLiveness reports anyLive=false AND anyGated=false AND not stuck AND not deaconIgnored.
- AC: Does NOT re-dispatch when any convoy agent is live (anyLive=true), when any agent is paused/troubled (anyGated=true), when reviewStatus is terminal (passed/failed/blocked), when status.stuck or status.deaconIgnored is true, or when canonical state is anything other than 'in_review' (e.g. verifying_on_main, in_progress, done, canceled, null).
- AC: Within the 15-minute cooldown after an attempt, a subsequent call defers (no second spawnReviewRoleForIssue call) and records a 'deferring — cooldown' action.
- AC: After the attempt cap (3) is reached, the patrol escalates exactly once: emits one emitActivityEntrySync error AND calls setReviewStatusSync with stuck:true and a dedicated stuckReason; subsequent calls neither re-dispatch nor re-escalate (escalated flag prevents duplicate activity entries).
- AC: A successful re-dispatch clears the issue's entry from the in-memory recovery-state map so a future independent stall gets a fresh attempt budget.
- AC: When the workspace/project cannot be resolved, the patrol records a skip action and does NOT consume an attempt from the cap.
- AC: getAutoCloseOutCanonicalState is only consulted for issues whose reviewStatus is already in-flight (candidate set filtered first), and a thrown error from any single issue is caught so the patrol returns its accumulated actions without aborting.
- AC: Unit tests in tests/lib/cloister/ cover the full matrix in ac1-ac6 (recover, each skip reason, cooldown defer, cap exhaustion+escalation+stuck, successful-dispatch map clear, unresolvable-workspace skip), mocking review-status, agents (getAgentStateSync/spawn), spawnReviewRoleForIssue, and getAutoCloseOutCanonicalState. npm run typecheck, lint, and test pass.
close_reason: Implemented bounded stalled-review-convoy recovery patrol with cooldown, attempt cap, escalation, forced re-dispatch, and unit tests

title: pan-1614: Add reviewConvoyLiveness(issueId) helper enumerating work + synthesis + sub-role agents

For each, read state via getAgentStateSync. anyLive is true if any agent's status is 'running' or 'starting'. anyGated is true if any agent has paused===true or troubled===true. Absent state.json (null) counts as stopped and ungated. Keep it pure/synchronous (no spawning, no status mutation).
- AC: Helper enumerates exactly six agent IDs: agent-<id>, agent-<id>-review, and agent-<id>-review-<subRole> for each of security, correctness, performance, requirements (sourced from REVIEW_SUB_ROLES, not hardcoded literals).
- AC: anyLive === true iff at least one enumerated agent has state.json status 'running' or 'starting'; a null/absent state.json is treated as stopped.
- AC: anyGated === true iff at least one enumerated agent has paused===true OR troubled===true.
- AC: Helper performs no side effects (no spawnRun, no setReviewStatus, no tmux kills) — confirmed by a unit test that asserts no mocked mutators are called.
- AC: Unit tests cover: all stopped → anyLive=false/anyGated=false; one sub-role running → anyLive=true; work agent paused → anyGated=true; a sub-role troubled → anyGated=true; all state.json absent → anyLive=false/anyGated=false. npm run typecheck, lint, and test pass.

title: pan-1615: Add the /clear + reseed recovery tier to the deacon escalation ladder
description:
In src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts checkApiErrorAgents(), extend the existing context-overflow escalation so it no longer dead-ends at /compact. New ladder: (1) /compact as today (works while under the ceiling); (2) if after CONTEXT_COMPACT_SETTLE_MS the overflow is STILL present (isContextOverflowTail true), send /clear followed by the reseed-message nudge — never re-sending the transcript; track clear attempts separately in contextOverflowRecoveryState; (3) if the overflow persists after the /clear tier's own attempt budget, markWorkspaceStuck(issueId, 'context_overflow', ...) as the terminal state. Preserve the existing settle-window, cooldown, and stuck/deaconIgnored guards. Emit activity-feed events for the /clear tier as for /compact.

close_reason: Extended deacon context-overflow ladder from compact to /clear+reseed, with separate clear attempts and stuck escalation tests.

title: pan-1615: Persist a self-clearing contextSaturatedAt marker on the agent runtime.json

title: pan-1615: High-water-mark proactive /compact before the hard ceiling
description:
Add a proactive compaction trigger to the deacon patrol: when an agent's server-side context usage (percentUsed from the conversation-service computation, against the conservative ceiling from proactive-verify) crosses a high-water mark (~85%) AND the agent is idle/at-prompt AND still under the hard ceiling (no overflow yet), send /compact to pre-empt the 400. Cooldown-guarded per agent so a wrong threshold cannot spam /compact, and a no-op once an overflow is already present (the recovery ladder owns that case). This makes the wedge preventable, not just recoverable.
- AC: When percentUsed crosses the high-water mark and the agent is idle and not yet overflowing, the deacon sends a single /compact (cooldown-guarded)
- AC: The proactive trigger is a no-op when the agent is already overflowing (recovery ladder owns that) and when within the cooldown window
- AC: Tests cover: crosses-threshold → compact, below-threshold → no-op, already-overflowing → no-op, within-cooldown → no-op
close_reason: Added idle high-water context usage compaction trigger with cooldown and tests for threshold/no-op cases.

title: pan-1615: Pure builder for the post-/clear reseed nudge

- AC: The message explicitly tells the agent NOT to start over and that its prior conversation was cleared to recover from a context-window overflow

title: pan-1613: Add a terminal-close teardown reaper that stops running agents on closed issues
description:
Add a new reconciler (e.g. src/lib/cloister/closed-issue-reaper.ts, exporting reconcileClosedIssueAgents()) and wire it into runPatrol() (deacon.ts ~4212, alongside the other reconcilers like reconcileOrphanProposedSpecs). It enumerates running agents via listRunningAgents(), and for each agent whose parent state.issueId resolves isIssueClosed===true, stops it via stopAgent(agentId) (which kills the tmux session, kills the orphan launcher, and marks state stopped — workspace, branches, and state.json are preserved; this is NOT deep-wipe). It must be idempotent (skip agents already stopped) and emit a clear activity log per reaped agent ('[deacon] reaped <agentId> — parent issue <issue> is closed'). To bound cost, dedupe isIssueClosed calls per issueId within a single patrol pass (the helper's 5-min cache already amortizes the live gh fallback across passes).
- AC: reconcileClosedIssueAgents() stops every running agent (any role: work, review, test, ship, inspect) whose parent issue isIssueClosed===true, using stopAgent() — never deep-wipe and never teardownWorkspace.

- AC: The reaper is invoked from runPatrol() and is guarded by the same no-resume / globally-paused gates the sibling reconcilers respect (it does not run when the deacon is globally paused).
- AC: A test asserts: a running ship agent on a closed issue is stopped; a running work agent on an open issue is left alone; a stopped agent on a closed issue is not touched; a second invocation reaps nothing new.
- AC: isIssueClosed is evaluated at most once per distinct issueId per patrol pass.
- AC: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm test pass.
close_reason: Added closed-issue running-agent reaper wired into patrol with stopAgent and deduped closed checks

title: pan-1613: Gate the deacon review/test safety-net patrols on isIssueClosed

title: pan-1616: Deacon watchdog: detect hung/dead inspect sessions, fail loud, deliver verdict to parent
description:
Add an inspect-timeout patrol to the Deacon (src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts), wired into the existing ~60s patrol cycle alongside checkStuckWorkAgents/orphan/api-error patrols. Each cycle, for every issue whose review status has inspectStatus==='inspecting': compute elapsed = now - inspectStartedAt; trip if (elapsed > INSPECT_TIMEOUT_MS) OR (the inspect-<issue>-<bead> tmux session no longer exists). INSPECT_TIMEOUT_MS is a documented constant (~12 min, above the inspect-agent.md 10-min budget). On trip, atomically: (1) set inspectStatus='error' with inspectNotes explaining timeout-vs-crash so the next cycle skips it (idempotency guard — never re-trip an 'error'); (2) kill the inspect tmux session if still present (killSession); (3) deliver an 'INSPECTION ERROR for bead <id>: inspection could not complete (timeout/crash) — no verdict was produced. Treat as infrastructure failure: do not silently proceed.' verdict to the PARENT work agent via pan tell using the UPPERCASE issue id (routes to agent-<issue>, the blocked session), mirroring inspect-agent.md's verdict delivery. If the parent session is also gone, log and leave inspectStatus='error' for a human/patrol to surface. Use async tmux primitives only (no sync sendKeys, no execSync).
- AC: Patrol trips when an 'inspecting' status exceeds INSPECT_TIMEOUT_MS measured from inspectStartedAt
- AC: Patrol also trips when inspectStatus==='inspecting' but the inspect-<issue>-<bead> tmux session no longer exists (crash-without-verdict)
- AC: On trip: inspectStatus is set to 'error', the inspect tmux session is killed if present, and an INSPECTION ERROR verdict is delivered to the parent work agent via pan tell with the uppercase issue id
- AC: Idempotent: a status already in 'error' is never re-tripped on subsequent patrol cycles (no duplicate verdicts / no oscillation)
- AC: INSPECT_TIMEOUT_MS is a single named constant (~12 min) documented next to the inspect-agent.md 10-minute budget; uses async tmux + no execSync
- AC: A unit test (fake timers) drives a stale 'inspecting' status past the timeout and asserts the trip actions fire exactly once
close_reason: Added Deacon inspect watchdog for timeout/crash, terminal error state, parent verdict delivery, idempotency, patrol wiring, and fake-timer coverage

description:

Present a better-sqlite3-compatible surface: exec(sql), prepare(sql)->{run(...params)->{changes,lastInsertRowid}, get(...params), all(...params), iterate(...params)}, close(). Shim pragma(sql, {simple?}) (exec for sets; prepare(`PRAGMA ${key}`).get() for {simple:true} reads, returning the scalar). title: pan-1101: Emit a runtime permission tripwire in auto-mode launcher scripts
description:
In src/lib/launcher-generator.ts (generateLauncherScriptSync), when the resolved permission mode is auto (permissionFlags includes the 'auto' token), emit a small bash guard immediately before the baked `exec claude ...` line. The guard inspects the baked claude invocation and, if a bypass token is present, prints a PANIC message to stderr and exits 70 (refusing to run). Build the forbidden-token pattern from the BYPASS_PERMISSION_MODE constant imported from claude-permissions.ts — do NOT write the literal 'bypassPermissions' string into launcher-generator.ts, or scripts/lint-permissions.sh will self-trip. The guard must be emitted ONLY for auto mode (bypass-mode launchers legitimately carry the token and must not be guarded). --agent launchers carry no permissionFlags and therefore correctly receive no guard. This is the only production-runtime hardening layer: it fires on every auto-mode agent start even if tests miss a future leak.
- AC: Auto-mode launcher scripts (permissionFlags include 'auto') contain a bash guard immediately before the exec line that exits 70 with a PANIC-to-stderr message if a bypass token is present in the baked claude invocation.
- AC: Bypass-mode launcher scripts and --agent launcher scripts (no permissionFlags) do NOT contain the guard.
- AC: The forbidden-token pattern is constructed from the BYPASS_PERMISSION_MODE constant (no quoted bypass literal added to launcher-generator.ts); `bash scripts/lint-permissions.sh` and `npm run lint` stay green without modifying the lint allowlist.
- AC: A unit test proves the guard fires: feeding an auto config whose baked command contains a bypass token produces a guard that exits non-zero when run in bash (or, equivalently, the test asserts the guard block greps for the token and exits 70).
- AC: Existing launcher-generator.test.ts auto-mode expectations are updated for the new guard lines; the full test file passes and bypass-mode expectations are unchanged.

title: pan-1242: Add `POST /api/issues` endpoint
description:
In `src/dashboard/server/routes/issues.ts`, add a new `POST /api/issues` Effect HTTP route. Body schema: `{ projectKey: string; targetStatus: 'backlog'|'todo'; title: string; description?: string }`. Resolve the project from `loadProjectsConfig()`, build a tracker via `createTrackerFromConfig(...)`, call `tracker.createIssue({ title, description, team: project.linearTeam, ... })`, then call `updateShadowState(newIssue.id, 'open', 'dashboard-new-issue', targetStatus)` so the card lands in the column the user clicked. Invalidate the appropriate `issueDataService.invalidateTracker(...)` and append an `issue.statusChanged` (or `issue.created`) event to the EventStoreService. Return the normalized `Issue` payload. Return 400 for missing/invalid body, 404 for unknown projectKey, 501 with a clear message for projects whose tracker is `gitlab` (since `GitLabTracker.createIssue` returns `NotImplementedError`).
- AC: POST `/api/issues` with valid `{projectKey,'todo',title}` returns 200 and the created `Issue` JSON; the issue appears on the next `GET /api/issues` call in the `todo` column.
- AC: POST with missing `title`, missing `projectKey`, or invalid `targetStatus` (anything other than `backlog`/`todo`) returns 400 with a structured error.
- AC: POST with an unknown `projectKey` returns 404; POST against a project whose `tracker` is `gitlab` returns 501 with an explanatory message and does not call `createIssue`.
- AC: On success, `issueDataService.invalidateTracker(<projectTrackerType>)` is invoked and an `issue.statusChanged` (or `issue.created`) event is appended to `EventStoreService` so live dashboards refresh.
- AC: Endpoint uses `execAsync` / Effect / promise-based I/O only — no `execSync`, `readFileSync`, `writeFileSync`, or other event-loop-blocking calls (per CLAUDE.md no-blocking-calls rule).
close_reason: Added POST /api/issues endpoint with validation, project-aware tracker creation, shadow-state placement, cache invalidation, and live event emission.
