title: pan-1512: agents.ts /api/agents: refuse to clear+recreate beads on a non-zero count mismatch — only repair from zero state
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/agents.ts (lines 2495-2556), tighten the auto-recovery branch. Currently any time beadCount !== planItemCount, hasBeads is set false and createBeadsFromVBrief is invoked, which (today) clears existing beads and recreates them — destroying partial state if recovery itself fails partway. After this change: if beadCount === 0, attempt recovery as today (now safe because B3 makes createBeads idempotent and the actual race is reduced to a no-op). If beadCount > 0 AND beadCount !== planItemCount, do NOT call createBeadsFromVBrief — return 422 with error: 'beads_count_mismatch', a descriptive message naming the counts, and hint: `pan plan ${issueId} --auto` to rerun planning end-to-end. This makes agents.ts a read-only verifier on partial state and pushes repair through the canonical planning path.
- AC: When beadCount > 0 AND beadCount !== planItemCount, /api/agents returns 422 with error code 'beads_count_mismatch' (NOT 'beads_required')
- AC: The 422 message includes both counts and the exact repair command `pan plan <ID> --auto`
- AC: When beadCount === 0, auto-recovery still runs (path is unchanged from today, just safer via B3)
- AC: New test exercises both branches: zero-beads → recovery attempted; mismatched beads → 422 with new error code

title: pan-1512: Make createBeadsFromVBrief idempotent: skip clear+recreate when existing beads already match the plan
description:
In src/lib/vbrief/beads.ts, modify createBeadsFromVBriefPromise (lines 134-393). After reading the workspace plan and BEFORE clearBeadsForIssue (line 249), call listBeadsForIssue and check whether existing beads already satisfy the plan exactly. The match criterion: (a) existing bead count === plan.items.length, (b) for every plan item, an existing bead exists whose title equals `${plan.id}: ${item.title}`, (c) every existing bead carries the issueLabel `plan.id.toLowerCase()`. If all three hold, build the beadIds map from existing beads and return { success: true, created: existingTitles, errors: [], beadIds } without clearing. If any criterion fails (extra beads, missing items, wrong titles), fall through to the legacy clear+recreate path unchanged. Add a single log line `[beads] Existing beads already match plan for ${issueLabel} — skipping clear+recreate (idempotent fast path)`.
- AC: When existing beads exactly match (count + per-item title + label), createBeadsFromVBrief returns success without invoking bd delete or bd create
- AC: When ANY plan item is missing a matching bead, function falls through to clear+recreate (legacy path)

title: pan-1491: Lib: computeSubstrateBugWeight(criteria, stats) → { weight, reason }
description:
Create `src/lib/flywheel-bug-weight.ts` exporting `computeSubstrateBugWeight(criteriaIds: readonly number[], stats: FlywheelStats): { weight: number; reason: string }`. For each criterion id 1..7 look up the corresponding `FlywheelStatsCriterion` (c1_bugRate, …, c7_flake). Apply: distance per criterion shape (rate/duration → `(value - target)/target`, ratio-higher-is-better → `(target - value)/target`, absolute count → `value`), clamped at zero. Status multiplier: red=3, yellow=2, green=1, insufficient_data=0. Resolve the per-criterion shape from the criterion's `value`/`target` JSON schema (rate/duration vs ratio vs count). Sum the contributions to produce `weight` (rounded to 2 decimals). Reason is a short sentence naming the top-contributing criterion, its current value, target, and status. Empty `criteriaIds` → `{ weight: 0, reason: 'no affected criteria declared' }`. Co-locate unit tests.
- AC: Bug affecting only c1 with c1.status=red, value=0.032, target=0.02 → weight ≈ (0.032-0.02)/0.02 × 3 = 1.80
- AC: Bug affecting c3 (passRate) with status=yellow, value=0.985, target=0.995 → weight ≈ (0.995-0.985)/0.995 × 2 ≈ 0.02
- AC: Bug affecting c2 (open P0s) with status=red, value=3 → weight ≈ 3 × 3 = 9 (absolute-count path)
- AC: insufficient_data criterion contributes zero even if value/target imply distance
- AC: Empty criteriaIds → `{ weight: 0, reason: 'no affected criteria declared' }` (never throws on missing telemetry)
- AC: `reason` names the top contributor by absolute contribution, formatted like `'criterion 1 (bug rate) at 3.2% vs target <2% — red'`
close_reason: Added computeSubstrateBugWeight with criterion mappings, status multipliers, distance/count paths, reason formatting, and tests for all acceptance examples; targeted test and root typecheck pass.

title: pan-1491: Lib: parseAffectedCriteria(body, labels) → number[]
description:

Parser recognises a `Flywheel-Affects-Criterion: 1,5,7` trailer (case-insensitive key, comma- or space-separated list of digits 1–7) anywhere in the body, plus any GitHub label matching `/^affects-criterion-([1-7])$/`. Result is the deduped sorted union, clamped to the 1–7 range. Empty input → `[]`. Co-locate unit tests in `src/lib/flywheel-affected-criteria.test.ts`.
- AC: `parseAffectedCriteria('Flywheel-Affects-Criterion: 1,5', [])` → `[1, 5]`
- AC: `parseAffectedCriteria('', ['affects-criterion-3', 'affects-criterion-5'])` → `[3, 5]`
- AC: Trailer + label union: body `'Flywheel-Affects-Criterion: 1'` with labels `['affects-criterion-5']` → `[1, 5]` (sorted, deduped)
- AC: Out-of-range or non-numeric ids are dropped; e.g., trailer `'1,8,foo'` → `[1]`
- AC: Empty body + empty labels → `[]`; never throws

title: pan-1509: fix(plan-finalize): use server-side autoSpawn; remove second POST to /api/agents
description:

title: pan-1509: fix(complete-planning): defer planning-session kill until after autoSpawn completes
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/issues.ts, the complete-planning route schedules setTimeout(killSession, 1500) at lines ~1276-1284 unless skipKill=true. When autoSpawn=true, this 1.5s deferred kill races against the work-agent spawn (which can take >1.5s under load). Move the killSession invocation to AFTER the spawn step has resolved (success or fail). For autoSpawn=true, the kill fires immediately on the Effect's success branch (no setTimeout needed — the response has already been generated by the handler's return value). For autoSpawn=false, keep the existing 1.5s deferred kill behavior (CLI compatibility). skipKill=true still skips the kill in both cases.
- AC: When autoSpawn=true, planning-pan-<id> tmux session is killed AFTER the spawn step has resolved (success or fail), not on a 1.5s timer
- AC: When autoSpawn=false, the existing 1.5s deferred kill behavior is preserved
- AC: When skipKill=true, no kill happens (existing behavior preserved in both branches)
- AC: If the spawn throws/rejects, the planning session is STILL killed (no leaked tmux session)
- AC: Unit test in __tests__/complete-planning.test.ts asserts kill timing in both autoSpawn=true success and failure paths
close_reason: Implemented post-autoSpawn planning-session kill timing with success, failure, delayed-default, and skipKill test coverage.

title: pan-1509: feat(pan-doctor): detect orphan proposed specs and surface remediation
description:

Print actionable hints per category (e.g. 'free disk and re-run planning' for beads-zero, 'pan start <id> --host to bypass stack-health temporarily' for no-agent). The check is informational (warns, does not fail the doctor exit code unless a --strict flag is added later).

title: pan-1509: feat(deacon): reconcile orphan proposed specs (auto-spawn safety net)
description:
In src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts (or a new src/lib/cloister/orphan-proposed-reconciler.ts wired into deacon's patrol loop), add a periodic reconciler that scans <projectRoot>/.pan/specs/ for vBRIEF files with plan.status='proposed'. When all four hold, the spec is an orphan — invoke the same work-agent spawn path that POST /api/agents uses (factor out the helper from server-side-autospawn bead if cleanest). On rejection (stack-unhealthy, guardrails, provider-down), log + skip — the next cycle retries. Run no more often than every 5 minutes to avoid thrash. Add a Deacon config gate (e.g. cloister.orphanProposedReconciler.enabled, default true) so operators can disable if it misbehaves.

title: pan-1509: feat(complete-planning): autoSpawn=true spawns work agent server-side after spec+beads succeed
description:
In src/dashboard/server/routes/issues.ts, extend the POST /api/issues/:id/complete-planning route to accept autoSpawn?: boolean in the request body (default false — preserves the kanban 'Done planning' button behavior). When autoSpawn=true AND spec+beads succeeded, invoke the same work-agent spawn logic that POST /api/agents uses today (factor out the existing logic in src/dashboard/server/routes/agents.ts lines ~2300-2900 into a shared helper if cleanest, OR call the existing handler via an internal in-process Effect invocation, OR call the /api/agents endpoint via localhost fetch — pick the cleanest given current architecture). The response shape gains optional fields: workAgentSpawned: boolean, workAgentSession?: string, workAgentError?: string, workAgentSkipReason?: string (e.g. 'stack-unhealthy', 'guardrails', 'paused'). All existing response fields (success, newState, gitPushed, beadsWarning, message) remain backward-compatible. When autoSpawn=true and the spawn is rejected by stack-health or guardrails, return 200 (NOT an error) with workAgentSpawned: false plus the reason — the reconciler will retry on later cycles.

title: pan-1509: fix(complete-planning): materialize beads before writing proposed spec

title: pan-1498: Implement pure-function requirements-trace validator with fixture-driven unit tests
description:
Add src/lib/cloister/review-requirements-validator.ts exporting:

  export interface RequirementsTraceValidationResult {
    ok: boolean;
    /** Titles of in_pr_scope Implemented/Partial ACs missing a usable trace */
    missingTraces: string[];
    /** Human-readable one-line reason for REVIEWER_FAILED; empty when ok */
    reason: string;
  }
  export function validateRequirementsTrace(markdown: string): RequirementsTraceValidationResult

The validator parses the reviewer's markdown:
  1. Walks the Coverage Matrix table to enumerate ACs and their (scope, status) tuple.
  2. Builds the required-trace set: ACs where status ∈ {Implemented, Partial} AND scope === 'in_pr_scope'.
  3. Locates the '## Live Code Path Traces' section (case-sensitive, anchored at line start).
  4. For each '### AC:' block under that section, extracts the **File:** line and validates that its value is a backticked token matching /^`\S+\.[A-Za-z0-9]+:\d+`$/ (path with extension and colon-line-number).
  5. Cross-references the trace blocks against the required-trace set. Any required AC that lacks a matching block, or has a block whose **File:** doesn't match the regex, goes into missingTraces.
  6. If the required-trace set is empty AND the section body is exactly the canonical 'None — no in_pr_scope ACs claimed Implemented or Partial.' sentinel, ok=true. If the required set is empty but the section is missing entirely, ok=false (because the substrate cannot distinguish 'reviewer addressed it' from 'reviewer forgot it').

The failure reason is 'requirements review missing live code path trace for ACs: <comma-separated titles>' (truncate to 240 chars to fit a `pan tell` payload comfortably).

Tests (src/lib/cloister/__tests__/review-requirements-validator.test.ts) use markdown fixtures under tests/fixtures/review-requirements/:
  - happy-path.md: two in_pr_scope Implemented ACs, both with valid traces → ok
  - whole-feature-only.md: one whole_feature_scope Implemented AC, sentinel body in traces section → ok
  - missing-section.md: section absent entirely → fail, reason names both ACs
  - missing-one-ac.md: two required, only one has a trace block → fail, reason names the missing one
  - bad-file-format.md: trace present but **File:** value is 'the dropdown' or a bare path with no extension/line → fail, reason names the AC
  - sentinel-when-not-needed.md: zero qualifying ACs, sentinel body present → ok
  - sentinel-when-needed.md: one qualifying AC but body is the sentinel → fail, reason names the AC
  - windows-path.md: trace **File:** value uses backslashes → fail (path regex rejects), reason names the AC
  - multiple-paths-one-block.md: a single block has two backticked paths, first valid → ok
  - case-variation.md: section header is '## live code path traces' lowercase → fail (case-sensitive contract)

The validator must be pure (no I/O, no process.cwd). The shim in bead 3 owns I/O.
- AC: validateRequirementsTrace exists with the signature above and is pure (no fs/exec)
- AC: All ten fixture cases above pass; each fixture lives as a separate .md file under tests/fixtures/review-requirements/ so future fixtures can be added without editing the test file
- AC: Failure reason starts with 'requirements review missing live code path trace for ACs:' and lists at least one AC title from the missingTraces array; reason is truncated to ≤240 chars
- AC: When the Coverage Matrix has zero in_pr_scope Implemented/Partial ACs AND the canonical sentinel body appears under '## Live Code Path Traces', the validator returns ok=true (this avoids blocking reviews that legitimately have nothing to trace)
- AC: When the Coverage Matrix has zero qualifying ACs but the section is missing entirely, the validator returns ok=false — the substrate cannot tell 'addressed' apart from 'forgotten' and must fail closed
- AC: The **File:** regex requires a non-empty path with at least one '.<ext>:<line>' suffix and rejects bare prose / Windows backslashes / missing line numbers (covered by bad-file-format.md and windows-path.md fixtures)
close_reason: Implemented pure-function validateRequirementsTrace with 10 fixture-driven unit tests; all pass.

title: pan-1500: Implement scanStubUi() — workspace + diff-base → StubUiFinding[]
description:

The function MUST use execAsync (never execSync — see no-execsync-server.md). Any internal failure (git non-zero exit, malformed hunk header, filesystem error) returns [] and logs a single non-fatal warning via console.warn, matching readPolicyNotes posture (review-context.ts:251-254). Unit tests use temp directories seeded via `git init`, write files mirroring PAN-1389 (a new FilesTab.tsx whose hook returns []) and PAN-1231 (a new TableMode.tsx in FleetAgentsView with a no-op handler), commit baseline + add the stubs, then call scanStubUi and assert the expected findings. Negative test: a workspace where the same file has a real implementation calling a fetch hook must produce zero findings.

title: pan-1487: Criterion 6: time-in-pipeline consistency per complexity bucket (p95 <= 2x median)
description:
Implement computeCriterion6: for each completed run in window, sum stage durations (plan+work+review+test+ship+merge) to get totalMs. Bucket by beads count: simple=1-3, medium=4-8, complex=9+. For each bucket compute median + p95 of totalMs; check p95/median ratio. Return {simple: {medianMs, p95Ms, ratio, status}, medium: {...}, complex: {...}}. Target per bucket: ratio<=2.0. Status: green if all three buckets <=2.0, yellow if any bucket 2-3, red if any bucket >3.
- AC: Bucket assignment uses beads count from .beads/issues.jsonl OR (fallback) plan_items count from the vBRIEF spec
- AC: Per-bucket median + p95 computed correctly; ratio = p95/median
- AC: Buckets with fewer than 3 runs are marked dataSufficient=false, not red
- AC: Headline status = worst-bucket status (green if all <=2.0, yellow if any 2-3, red if any >3)
- AC: Test fixture: 6 runs across 2 buckets with known totalMs distribution produces correct ratios
close_reason: Closed

Status green <0.05, yellow 0.05-0.20, red >0.20. UAT is explicitly NOT counted (no event emitted for UAT).
- AC: value = total interventions / completed runs in window
- AC: target=0.05; thresholds green<0.05, yellow [0.05,0.20], red>0.20

title: pan-1486: End-to-end integration test: cooldown respected, cancel works, executor fires on expiry
description:
Add src/lib/cloister/__tests__/auto-merge-integration.test.ts that wires the scheduler → executor → cancel together end-to-end with mocked merge function and mocked GitHub PR state. Three scenarios: (1) schedule + wait 4 minutes (fake timers) + cancel → entry removed, merge function never called; (2) schedule + wait full 5 minutes + executor tick → merge function called exactly once, entry status='merged'; (3) schedule + flip CI red during cooldown + executor tick → entry status='blocked', merge function never called.
- AC: Test uses vi.useFakeTimers() and vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync — no real-wall-clock delays.
- AC: Scenario 1 (cancel during cooldown): cancel returns 200, the pending list becomes empty, the mocked merge function is never invoked even after the cooldown elapses.
- AC: Scenario 2 (cooldown expires): the mocked merge function is invoked exactly once, the entry transitions pending→merging→merged.
- AC: Scenario 3 (eligibility flips during cooldown): the entry transitions pending→blocked with the eligibility reason; merge function is never invoked.
- AC: All three scenarios run in under 100ms wall-clock thanks to fake timers.
- AC: npm run typecheck and npm test pass; full suite is green.
close_reason: Closed

Cancel calls DELETE /api/flywheel/auto-merge/:id; on success the row disappears via query invalidation. Countdown updates every second from the entry's absolute scheduledMergeAt timestamp.

- AC: Each row's countdown updates every second based on Date.parse(scheduledMergeAt) - Date.now(); when remaining <= 0 the row shows 'merging…' (executor will pick it up).

title: pan-1486: Add server-side executor that fires pending auto-merges after cooldown via the existing merge code path
description:
Add a small interval-based executor (src/dashboard/server/services/auto-merge-executor.ts) started from main.ts when the dashboard boots. Tick every 30s: listPendingAutoMerges() with status='pending' AND scheduledMergeAt <= now; for each entry: re-check isFlywheelGloballyPaused() (skip if true), re-check isAutoMergeEligible (if no longer eligible mark status='blocked' with reason); then transitionToMerging(id) — if it returns false (lost the race), skip. On winner: invoke the same internal merge function the dashboard MERGE button uses in src/dashboard/server/routes/workspaces.ts; on success markMerged; on throw markFailed with reason. Stop the executor cleanly on dashboard shutdown.
- AC: Executor starts when the dashboard server boots and is registered alongside the existing Deacon patrol so dev-mode and prod both pick it up; it can be disabled via env (PANOPTICON_DISABLE_AUTO_MERGE=1) for tests.
- AC: Tick processes only entries whose scheduledMergeAt <= Date.now(); future-scheduled entries remain pending.
- AC: If isFlywheelGloballyPaused() is true at tick time, the executor logs '[auto-merge] flywheel paused, skipping tick' and does NOT fire any merge; entries remain pending.
- AC: If isAutoMergeEligible returns false at fire-time (e.g. CI flipped red during cooldown), the entry is marked status='blocked' with the eligibility reason and the executor moves on without firing.
- AC: transitionToMerging is called and only the winning concurrent call proceeds; the loser logs and continues.
- AC: Successful merge: status set to 'merging' then 'merged' with mergedAt timestamp; the existing dashboard merge function (the one wired to the MERGE button) is invoked unchanged — no second merge path is added.
- AC: Failed merge: status set to 'failed' with failureReason; TTS announces 'PAN-XXX auto-merge failed: <reason>'; entry persists for the orchestrator to surface.
- AC: Vitest tests with mocked merge function cover: future-scheduled-skipped, paused-skipped, eligibility-recheck-blocked, transition-race-loser-skips, successful-merge happy path, failed-merge marks failed and announces.
- AC: Tests use vi.useFakeTimers() — no real interval delays per the CLAUDE.md retry/delay rule.
close_reason: Closed

title: pan-1486: Add POST /api/flywheel/auto-merge/schedule + scanner that enqueues with cooldown and TTS
description:

On gate pass: scheduleAutoMerge() with scheduledMergeAt = now + 5 minutes; emit TTS via the same path as scripts/say.sh used by the dashboard ('PAN-XXX auto-merging in 5 minutes; pan merge cancel PAN-XXX to abort'); return the entry. Constant AUTO_MERGE_COOLDOWN_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000 in a new auto-merge-config.ts module.

- AC: POST /api/flywheel/auto-merge/schedule with valid {issueId} when require_uat_before_merge=false, flywheel running, and PR eligible: returns 200 with the persisted entry containing scheduledMergeAt = now + 300s (±2s tolerance for test wall-clock).

- AC: POST is origin-validated; missing/wrong origin returns 403.

title: pan-1486: Add pending_auto_merges SQLite table (schema v28) + CRUD module
description:
Bump src/lib/database/schema.ts CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION from 27 to 28; add a v27→v28 migration block CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pending_auto_merges (id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT, issueId TEXT NOT NULL, prUrl TEXT NOT NULL, prNumber INTEGER, projectKey TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK status IN ('pending','merging','blocked','failed'), scheduledMergeAt TEXT NOT NULL, scheduledAt TEXT NOT NULL, mergedAt TEXT, failureReason TEXT, cancelledAt TEXT, cancelledBy TEXT). Returns a reason string when ineligible so callers can use it in TTS / status messages.

title: pan-1501: Orchestrator: runTestRequirementCheck composes detector + counter + fetcher and returns failure lines
description:
Add `runTestRequirementCheck(workspacePath: string, issueId: string, waivedReason?: string): Effect<string[], ProcessSpawnError>` to src/lib/work/test-requirement-gate.ts. Flow: (1) if waivedReason is non-empty, return [] immediately (waiver is the escape hatch). (2) Call fetchIssueBodyForGate(issueId); if it returns null, return a failure line directing the operator to --force or --test-waived. (3) Run detectTestRequirements on the body; if empty, return []. (4) Compute diff base via `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` (fall back to `origin/main...HEAD` three-dot syntax) and run `git diff --numstat <base>...HEAD`. (5) Run countTestDeltaInDiff on the numstat output. (6) If requirements > 0 && delta === 0, return failure lines listing the matched keywords (with line numbers) and the two escape hatches (add tests / use --test-waived). title: pan-1457: Client usePathExists hook with LRU cache, in-flight dedup, and TTL
description:
Create src/dashboard/frontend/src/hooks/usePathExists.ts exporting a hook usePathExists(issueId: string | undefined, relativePath: string | undefined) -> { state: 'pending' | 'exists' | 'missing'; kind: 'file' | 'dir' | null }. Internally maintain a module-level LRU cache keyed by `${issueId}::${relativePath}` capped at 2000 entries, an in-flight Map<key, Promise> for dedup, and a TTL of 60_000 ms per entry. When issueId is undefined or relativePath empty, return state='pending' (effectively plain-text fallback). When the cache has a fresh hit, return state synchronously on first render — no useEffect tick — so chips don't flicker on re-mount. When the cache has a stale or absent entry, kick off the RPC via getTransport().request((client) => client[WS_METHODS.resolvePathExists]({ issueId, relativePath })), update the cache, and re-render. Strip ':<line>[:<col>]' from relativePath before forming the cache key and sending. Export a clearPathExistsCache() for tests. Unit tests cover: cache hit returns synchronously, two concurrent renders for the same key issue one RPC (dedup), TTL expiry triggers a re-fetch, error responses cache as 'missing' (do not retry-storm), undefined issueId short-circuits.
- AC: First render with an uncached key returns state='pending' and issues exactly one RPC call
- AC: After RPC resolves to exists=true, the next render returns state='exists' with kind='file' or 'dir'
- AC: Subsequent re-mount with the same (issueId, relativePath) within TTL returns state='exists' synchronously on the very first render — no flicker
- AC: Two simultaneous useTpathExists calls for the same key share a single in-flight RPC (dedup test counts mock invocations)
- AC: After 60s TTL elapses (via vi.useFakeTimers + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync), a re-mount issues a fresh RPC
- AC: Cache evicts least-recently-used entries when count exceeds 2000
- AC: Positional suffix ':12' / ':12:5' on relativePath is stripped before forming the cache key so 'src/App.tsx' and 'src/App.tsx:12' share one cache entry
- AC: Undefined issueId or empty relativePath short-circuits to state='pending' and issues no RPC
- AC: RPC error response caches as state='missing' for the TTL window — no retry storm

title: pan-1457: Server resolve-path-exists service with hardened path validation
description:
Create src/dashboard/server/services/resolve-path-exists.ts mirroring read-workspace-file.ts patterns: resolveProjectFromIssue(issueId), getWorkspacePathForIssue(...), realpath(workspaceRoot) for the sandbox root, resolve(workspaceRoot, relativePath) for the candidate, isInsidePath() guard against '..' escapes BEFORE stat, realpath() the candidate to detect symlink escape, isInsidePath() check AGAIN against the realpath result, then stat(). Return { exists: true, kind: 'file' | 'dir' } based on stat; return { exists: false, kind: null } for ENOENT and for any isInsidePath() rejection (do NOT throw an error for traversal — return missing so the client can't probe via timing). Throw PanRpcError only for invalid argument (relativePath > 4 KiB) and unexpected IO failures on entries that exist. Strip ':<line>[:<col>]' suffix from relativePath before stat. NEVER call readdir or readlink — only stat and realpath. Export both readPathExists(input) and a readPathExistsEffect(input) wrapper for the Effect RPC handler. Comprehensive tests covering: file exists → kind=file, dir exists → kind=dir, missing → exists=false, '..' escape → exists=false (NOT error), symlink-to-outside-workspace → exists=false, positional suffix stripped, oversized relativePath → invalid argument error, workspace-not-found → WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND error.
- AC: resolvePathExists({ issueId, relativePath: 'src/dashboard/server/server.ts' }) returns { exists: true, kind: 'file' } for an existing file under the workspace root
- AC: resolvePathExists({ issueId, relativePath: 'src/dashboard' }) returns { exists: true, kind: 'dir' } for an existing directory
- AC: resolvePathExists({ issueId, relativePath: 'does/not/exist.md' }) returns { exists: false, kind: null }
- AC: Path-traversal '../../etc/passwd' returns { exists: false, kind: null } — NOT a PanRpcError, so timing cannot leak whether the target exists
- AC: Symlink inside workspace that points to /etc/hostname returns { exists: false, kind: null } (realpath escape caught by the second isInsidePath check)
- AC: Positional suffix ':12' or ':12:5' is stripped from relativePath before stat — 'src/App.tsx:12' resolves the same as 'src/App.tsx'
- AC: relativePath longer than 4096 bytes throws PanRpcError code=INVALID_ARGUMENT without touching the filesystem
- AC: Service never calls readdir/readlink — confirmed by code review and by the test suite mocking node:fs/promises to assert only stat and realpath are reached
- AC: Issue ID that maps to no project throws PanRpcError code=WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND (mirrors read-workspace-file behaviour)

title: pan-1430: Module-level circuit breaker after retried 401 with single actionable log
description:
In src/lib/github-app.ts, add module-level state (`appDegradedUntil: number`, `appDegradedLogged: boolean`) and helpers `markAppDegraded(reason)` / `isAppDegraded()`. Disabling App-backed calls for 5 minutes. To recover: `node scripts/create-github-app.mjs` (PANOPTICON_DEV_WEBHOOKS=1).'. While `isAppDegraded()` returns true (5-min TTL), `githubApi` throws immediately without a network call. The error message points at the same diagnostic command. When the TTL expires, log ONCE that App calls are re-enabled and clear `appDegradedLogged`. Unit-test that the breaker opens after a retried 401, stays open for the TTL, blocks `githubApi` calls in the meantime, and re-opens after expiry.

title: pan-1430: Retry githubApi once after re-issuing installation token on HTTP 401

- AC: If the retry succeeds (200/204), the caller receives the parsed response — no exception
- AC: If the retry also returns 401, the original error-throwing path runs (caller sees the 401 surface area unchanged from today, modulo the breaker bead)

- AC: Unit test in `src/lib/__tests__/github-app-401-retry.test.ts` covers the 401→regenerate→200 success path and the 401→regenerate→401 failure path

title: pan-1416: Integration tests for lockfile lifecycle, port-lock guard, canonical-path guard, and pan doctor multi-dashboard detection

title: pan-1416: pan doctor reports multiple dashboard instances and flags non-canonical primary-port owners
description:

On Linux: read /proc/*/cmdline, filter for entries containing 'dist/dashboard/server.js', resolve each pid's cwd via /proc/<pid>/cwd. On darwin/win32: parse `ps -e -o pid,command` and skip cwd resolution. Cross-reference with ~/.panopticon/dashboard.lock if present to confirm canonical identity. Return: ok if exactly one canonical instance; warn if >1 instance running; error if a non-canonical (cwd matches workspace pattern) instance is bound to the configured primary port. Include the conflicting pid + cwd in the message and recommend `pan down && pan up` to recover.

- AC: pan doctor with two dashboards (one canonical, one workspace, different ports) reports WARN listing both with their pids/cwds

title: pan-1416: Add startup port-lock guard that refuses to bind the primary port when a live canonical dashboard holds the lock
description:
Before binding the HTTP server in src/dashboard/server/server.ts (the HttpServerLive layer around L71-L92, or in main.ts before runServer is awaited), read the lockfile via readDashboardLock(). If the lock exists, lock.pid is alive (process.kill(pid, 0) succeeds), lock.heartbeatAt is within the last 90s, lock.port === intendedBindPort, AND lock.pid !== process.pid, fire the guard. When firing: log a loud multi-line warning identifying the conflicting pid/cwd, then either (a) if process.cwd() matches the workspace pattern, override config.port to 0 (kernel-assigned ephemeral) and continue, then log the actual chosen port after listening, or (b) if not in a workspace cwd, process.exit(75) (EX_TEMPFAIL) so pan up surfaces the collision. Skip the guard entirely when PANOPTICON_DISABLE_DEACON=1 is set.
- AC: Starting a second dashboard against an alive lockfile, from a non-workspace cwd, exits with code 75 and prints a loud warning naming the conflicting pid and cwd
- AC: Starting a second dashboard against an alive lockfile, from a workspace cwd (e.g. workspaces/feature-pan-1416), falls back to an ephemeral port, logs the chosen port, and continues to serve
- AC: Starting a dashboard with a stale lockfile (heartbeatAt > 90s old OR lock.pid not alive) proceeds normally and overwrites the stale lock
- AC: Starting a dashboard with PANOPTICON_DISABLE_DEACON=1 bypasses the guard entirely (used by workspace devcontainer peers)
- AC: Canonical pan up restart cycle works without delay: pan down → pan up completes within the normal time budget (graceful shutdown unlinks lockfile in time for the new bind)

title: pan-1416: Add startup canonical-path guard that refuses primary-port bind when cwd is a workspace path and API_PORT is unset
description:

The canonical dashboard (cwd = project root) and devcontainer peers (PANOPTICON_DISABLE_DEACON=1) are unaffected.

title: pan-1419: Frontend classifier returns active | stopped | orphan_test for every agent, with unit tests
description:
Create src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/agent-classifier.ts that exports `classifyDashboardAgent(agent): 'active' | 'stopped' | 'orphan_test'`. Rules: (1) if `agent.hasLiveTmuxSession === true` → 'active' (overrides any stale status); (2) if `agent.status === 'running' || agent.status === 'starting'` → 'active' (tmux-undefined fallback); (3) if `agent.issueId` matches the orphan-prefix regex `/^PAN-(AC|PI(-PROMPT)?|TEST|REVIEW|SHIP|SUB(REVIEW|SIGNAL)?)-?\d*$/` AND lastActivity/startedAt older than 7d → 'orphan_test'; (4) otherwise → 'stopped'. Export the orphan-prefix regex and the age threshold as named constants so they can be reused by pan doctor. Co-locate Vitest unit tests in src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/__tests__/agent-classifier.test.ts covering every mixed-state combination from the issue body (running+tmux, stopped+tmux, stopped+no-tmux+recent, stopped+no-tmux+old+orphan-prefix, etc.).
- AC: `classifyDashboardAgent` returns 'active' whenever hasLiveTmuxSession===true, regardless of status
- AC: `classifyDashboardAgent` returns 'orphan_test' only when BOTH the prefix matches AND the age exceeds 7d
- AC: `classifyDashboardAgent` returns 'stopped' for pipeline-role agents with status='stopped', tmux dead, and recent activity (the genuinely-failed-recently case)
- AC: Unit tests cover all five named cases from the issue body (PAN-1370 running+tmux; PAN-AC22 orphan; PAN-TEST-1 orphan; recently-stopped pipeline agent; ambiguous tmux-unknown running)
- AC: ORPHAN_PREFIX_PATTERN and ORPHAN_AGE_THRESHOLD_MS are named exports reused by the pan doctor check (no duplicate regex)
close_reason: Added classifyDashboardAgent with reusable orphan prefix and age constants plus unit coverage for live tmux, stale status, recent stopped, and old orphan-prefix cases.

title: pan-1417: Make POST /api/review/:id/request non-destructive on already-passed reviews; add ?force and ?nudge flags
description:
Modify the `reviewStatus === 'passed'` branch in `src/dashboard/server/routes/workspaces.ts` (around line 3677, inside the `postWorkspaceRequestReviewRoute` handler) to add a code-drift safety gate. Parse `force` and `nudge` flags from both query string and JSON body (mirror the /trigger route's pattern at workspaces.ts:3395-3398). Read the workspace HEAD via `git rev-parse HEAD` — use `flyExecCmd` for `workspaceInfo.isRemote`, plain `execAsync` for local — and compare against `existingStatus.reviewedAtCommit`. Branch logic: (a) `force=true` → preserve existing `shouldTreatAsRerun` destructive path, log `[request-review] FORCE: full reset requested by operator for <id>`; (b) `nudge=true` AND reviewStatus=passed AND testStatus=passed → re-emit `test.passed` via the route's existing `EventStoreService` (yield* pattern, matching workspaces.ts:3987-3991), do NOT touch any status fields, log `[request-review] NUDGE: re-emitting test.passed for <id> without state reset`, return `{ success: true, nudged: true, message }`; (c) `nudge=true` AND tests have not passed → HTTP 400 with `{ success: false, error: 'Cannot nudge — tests have not passed', hint: 'Use ?force=true for a full re-review or wait for tests to complete' }`; (d) no flags AND `reviewedAtCommit` is defined AND matches current HEAD (no drift) → HTTP 200 + `{ success: false, noCodeDrift: true, error: 'No code drift since review passed', hint: 'Use ?nudge=true to re-emit lifecycle events without resetting state, or ?force=true to force a full re-review' }`, log `[request-review] REFUSED: no code drift since review passed for <id> at <short-sha>`; (e) no flags AND drift detected OR `reviewedAtCommit` undefined OR HEAD lookup failed → fall through to the existing `shouldTreatAsRerun` destructive path unchanged. Wrap the HEAD lookup in try/catch — failure falls through to (e). Add vitest coverage in `src/dashboard/server/routes/__tests__/request-review-nudge.test.ts` exercising every branch above with mocked review-status, mocked git-info helper, and mocked EventStoreService.
- AC: When reviewStatus === 'passed' AND reviewedAtCommit === currentHeadSha AND neither force nor nudge is set, the endpoint returns HTTP 200 + { success: false, noCodeDrift: true, error: 'No code drift since review passed', hint: <mentions both ?force=true and ?nudge=true> } and does NOT mutate review-status (verified by reading status before and after).
- AC: When `?nudge=true` is sent AND reviewStatus === 'passed' AND testStatus === 'passed', the endpoint emits exactly one `test.passed` event via EventStoreService (payload includes the normalized issueId), returns HTTP 200 + { success: true, nudged: true, message }, and does NOT write to reviewStatus, testStatus, verificationStatus, autoRequeueCount, mergeStatus, readyForMerge, or any other status field.
- AC: When `?nudge=true` is sent AND testStatus !== 'passed', the endpoint returns HTTP 400 + { success: false, error: 'Cannot nudge — tests have not passed', hint } and does NOT emit a `test.passed` event or mutate any status field.
- AC: When `?force=true` is sent AND reviewStatus === 'passed', the endpoint preserves the current destructive `shouldTreatAsRerun` behavior: reviewStatus → pending, testStatus → pending, mergeStatus → pending, readyForMerge → false, autoRequeueCount → 0, verificationCycleCount → 0, verificationStatus → pending, notes cleared; dispatches review role; logs `[request-review] FORCE: full reset requested by operator for <id>`. Existing log line `[request-review] ${issueId}: forcing full review/test rerun from passed state` is preserved verbatim.
- AC: When reviewStatus === 'passed' AND reviewedAtCommit is defined AND currentHeadSha !== reviewedAtCommit (drift detected) AND no flags are set, the endpoint falls through to the existing destructive rerun path (same as `?force=true` outcome). This preserves correct behavior for the merge-agent rebase-conflict curl hint and for any operator who legitimately rebased before re-requesting.
- AC: When reviewStatus === 'passed' AND reviewedAtCommit is undefined (legacy row) AND no flags are set, the endpoint falls through to the existing destructive rerun path. When the HEAD lookup throws (e.g. workspace path missing, git unavailable, remote VM unreachable), the endpoint also falls through to the destructive path with a warning log — never a 5xx.
- AC: Both `force` and `nudge` are accepted from either the URL query string (?force=true / ?nudge=true) OR the JSON request body ({ force: true } / { nudge: true }). When both are sent, `force` takes precedence (full reset wins over nudge). When neither is sent and the no-drift gate refuses, the response hint mentions BOTH flags so operators can pick the right one.
- AC: Remote workspaces (workspaceInfo.isRemote === true) read HEAD via `flyExecCmd(vmName, 'cd <path> && git rev-parse HEAD')` with a 30s timeout, mirroring the existing pattern at workspaces.ts:3495-3503. Local workspaces use plain `execAsync('git rev-parse HEAD', { cwd: workspacePath })`. Both are wrapped in try/catch and fall through on failure (AC6).
- AC: Vitest unit-test file at `src/dashboard/server/routes/__tests__/request-review-nudge.test.ts` exercises every branch (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7) against the postWorkspaceRequestReviewRoute handler with mocked getReviewStatusSync, mocked setReviewStatus, mocked EventStoreService, mocked getWorkspaceInfoForIssue, and mocked execAsync. Tests use `vi.useFakeTimers()` if any retry/timeout paths are exercised. `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test` all pass on the workspace after the change.
- AC: Regression: `pan review request <id>` CLI continues to work for its primary use case (reviewStatus === 'blocked' or 'failed' — agent re-requesting after fixing feedback). That path is untouched because the new gate only fires on reviewStatus === 'passed'. No CLI changes are required and no existing CLI tests need updating.
close_reason: Implemented non-destructive passed-review request handling with force/nudge flags, drift detection, and tests

title: pan-1415: Implement checkStuckAgentRemediation patrol with 3-stage escalation
description:
Create `src/lib/cloister/stuck-remediation.ts` exporting `async function checkStuckAgentRemediation(opts?: { now?: number }): Promise<string[]>`. The function iterates running work agents (`listRunningAgentsSync()` filtered by `state.role === 'work'` and `state.status === 'running'`), and for each one applies the gate cascade described below. Returns the same `string[]` action list shape as other deacon patrols.

Gate cascade (all must pass before stage logic runs):
  1. Config: skip if `stuck_remediation.enabled === false`.
  2. Session: skip if `!sessionExistsSync(agentId)`.
  3. Status: skip if `state.paused || state.troubled || state.completedAt`.
  4. Tracker: skip if `reviewStatus.stuck`, `reviewStatus.deaconIgnored`, `reviewStatus.mergeStatus === 'merged'`, or `reviewStatus.readyForMerge`.
  5. Dead-end overlap: skip if `reviewStatus.reviewStatus` is `'blocked'` or `'failed'`, or `reviewStatus.verificationStatus === 'failed'`, or `reviewStatus.testStatus === 'failed'` (let `checkDeadEndAgents` handle those).
  6. Idle: skip if `!isAgentIdleForNudge(agentId)` (active/waiting-on-human/uninitialized-fresh agents are not idle).
  7. Bead overlap: skip if `bd ready -l <issueLabel>` returns any rows in the agent's workspace (let `nudgeIdleWorkAgentsWithOpenBeads` handle those).

State handling:
  - Read `runtime.lastActivity` from `getAgentRuntimeStateSync(agentId)`. If missing, skip.
  - Read stored `stuckState = readStuckRemediationState(agentId)`.
  - If `stuckState` exists AND `runtime.lastActivity > stuckState.firstStuckAt` → `clearStuckRemediationState(agentId)` and continue (treat as fresh stall).
  - Compute `idleMinutes = (now - runtime.lastActivity) / 60_000`.

Stage transitions (highest applicable stage wins):
  - `idleMinutes >= stage3_minutes` AND `(stuckState?.lastStage ?? 0) < 3` → call `markAgentTroubled(agentId)`. Write `{ lastStage: 3, lastStageAt: now, firstStuckAt: stuckState?.firstStuckAt ?? runtime.lastActivity }`. Log `[deacon] stuck-remediation stage=3 issue=<id> idleMin=<n> action=marked-troubled`. Push to actions.
  - Else if `idleMinutes >= stage2_minutes` AND `(stuckState?.lastStage ?? 0) < 2` → call `resumeAgent(agentId, recoveryMessage)`. If `result.success` → write `{ lastStage: 2, lastStageAt: now, firstStuckAt }` and log/push action. If `!result.success` → DO NOT advance stored stage; log failure and let the next patrol retry.
  - Else if `idleMinutes >= stage1_minutes` AND `(stuckState?.lastStage ?? 0) < 1` → call `messageAgent(agentId, pokeMessage)`. Write `{ lastStage: 1, lastStageAt: now, firstStuckAt: stuckState?.firstStuckAt ?? new Date(runtime.lastActivity).toISOString() }`. Log/push action.
  - Otherwise no-op (waiting for the next threshold).

Messages (deterministic strings, no per-call variability):
  - Stage 1 poke: `"You appear stuck — no tool calls for ${idleMinutes} min. If your implementation is complete, run \`pan done ${issueId}\`. Otherwise reply with a one-line summary of what you're waiting on, then continue."`
  - Stage 2 resume: `"Resuming after auto-detected stall (${idleMinutes} min idle). Review your last work and decide whether to continue or signal done with \`pan done ${issueId}\`."`
  - Stage 3 has no message — it's silent gate-marking.

All exceptions wrapped per-agent in try/catch — one failing agent must not stop the loop for the others. Use `console.error` + `logDeaconEventSync` for unexpected throws.

title: pan-1408: Add src/lib/graphify/refresh.ts with refreshGraphify(projectPath, issueId) helper
description:

RefreshResult is a discriminated union: { skipped: 'no-graphify-cli' | 'no-graphify-out' | 'no-changes' | 'gitignored' } | { ok: true; commit: string; pushed: boolean } | { ok: false; error: string }. Implementation steps in order: (1) Use `which graphify` via execAsync to detect CLI; return skipped:'no-graphify-cli' if missing. (4) `git add graphify-out/` in projectPath. (5) `git diff --cached --quiet` — if exit 0, return skipped:'no-changes' (or 'gitignored'). (6) `git commit -m "chore(graphify): refresh after ${issueId}"`. (7) `git push origin main`; on non-fast-forward, run `git fetch origin main && git pull --rebase origin main && git push origin main` once. (8) Return ok:true with commit SHA. Wrap each shell-out in try/catch; map failures to RefreshResult.ok=false with descriptive error strings. NO execSync anywhere — repo rule (see hazards). NO `git add -A` — only stage graphify-out/.
- AC: Module exports refreshGraphify(projectPath, issueId): Promise<RefreshResult> with the discriminated-union shape described above.

title: pan-1405: deliverAgentMessage: try supervisor socket → channels → tmux
description:

(2) else if channelsEnabled and channels socket exists → existing channels POST path → log path='channel'. (3) else → sendKeys(tmux) → log path='tmux'. The explicit deliveryMethod argument is honored: 'tmux' still forces tmux, 'channels' still forces channels (errors if unavailable). A new explicit deliveryMethod value 'supervisor' is added that errors if the socket is missing. Default 'auto' uses the tiered fallback. Per-tier failure reasons are appended to the existing channel-delivery log under the new key 'pty-supervisor' (and continue to fall through). Module-private helper resolves the supervisor socket path with the same panopticonHomeForChannels() function (rename it to panopticonHomeForSockets() inside this bead, with the old name kept as an alias if any external caller imports it).

- AC: When neither socket exists (or both fail), the function falls through to tmux sendKeys and writes path='tmux' with the per-tier failure reasons.
- AC: deliveryMethod='supervisor' throws MessageDeliveryFailed when the supervisor socket POST fails (no silent fallback). 'channels' keeps its existing strict behavior. 'tmux' bypasses both sockets.
- AC: Bridge log and per-agent delivery log filename are unchanged so existing dashboards / log readers don't break — the new path='supervisor' line lands in the same file.
- AC: Existing call sites in agents.ts (resumeAgent, messageAgent, auto-continue) are NOT modified — they continue to call deliverAgentMessage; only its internals change.

title: pan-1405: Create src/lib/channels/pty-supervisor.ts (PTY master + unix socket)
description:
Create src/lib/channels/pty-supervisor.ts as a Node 22 script that spawns claude in a PTY (via @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch), proxies stdin↔PTY input and PTY output↔stdout, forwards SIGWINCH/resize events, and listens on ~/.panopticon/sockets/pty-<agentId>.sock for HTTP-on-unix POSTs that inject text into Claude's PTY input. Echo each socket-delivered message back to stdout (so the user sees it in the tmux pane). On EXIT/SIGTERM/SIGINT, unlink the socket and exit. Require PANOPTICON_AGENT_ID env var; reject requests without a matching pty-token header. Add a new tsdown entry to emit dist/pty-supervisor.js (node-pty marked external). Add @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch to root package.json. Header comment documents the architecture, the H1 PTY-owns-claude lifecycle, env-var requirements (TERM/COLORTERM/LANG passthrough), and the per-message echo behavior.
- AC: Spawning the supervisor with PANOPTICON_AGENT_ID set and `claude --version` as the child completes, prints 'claude --version' output to stdout, and exits when the child exits.
- AC: After spawn, ~/.panopticon/sockets/pty-<agentId>.sock exists at mode 0600 (verified via fs.stat).
- AC: POST { content: 'hello' } with a valid pty-token header writes 'hello\n' (with a trailing newline) to Claude's PTY input AND echoes it to supervisor stdout. POST without a token returns 403.
- AC: Process.stdout 'resize' events call pty.resize(cols, rows) on the spawned PTY.
- AC: On SIGTERM and SIGINT the supervisor unlinks its socket file and exits 0; the spawned child receives SIGTERM and is reaped before exit.
- AC: Per-agent log at ~/.panopticon/logs/pty-supervisor-<agentId>.log records each socket POST as one JSON line with { ts, agentId, kind: 'socket_write', contentLength, caller? }.
- AC: @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch is added to the root package.json dependencies, and tsdown emits dist/pty-supervisor.js with node-pty marked external (verified by inspecting the bundle).
- AC: Header comment in pty-supervisor.ts documents: Node-only requirement (no Bun), H1 PTY-owns-claude crash semantics, env-var passthrough, socket-path convention, per-message echo behavior, and the out-of-scope nature of permission relay.

title: pan-748: Add computeContextUsage() helper in conversation-service.ts
description:
In src/dashboard/server/services/conversation-service.ts, add an exported async function computeContextUsage(sessionFile: string, model: string | null): Promise<ContextUsage | null>. It calls findLastCompactBoundary(sessionFile) to get the byte offset, fs.stat()s the file to get total size, computes activeBytes = max(0, size - boundaryOffset), estimates tokens = Math.ceil(activeBytes / 4), resolves the model via resolveModelIdSync() and looks up contextWindow in MODEL_CAPABILITIES. Returns { activeBytes, estimatedTokens, contextWindow, percentUsed } when the model is known; returns null when model is null/empty or not in MODEL_CAPABILITIES after resolution. Clamps percentUsed to [0, 100]. Add a short code comment near the function noting the bytes/4 heuristic and the limitation. The ContextUsage type itself is defined in the contracts bead — for this bead, define a local interface and align it once contracts land (or coordinate ordering).
- AC: Helper returns null when model is null, empty string, or not in MODEL_CAPABILITIES after resolveModelIdSync.
- AC: Helper returns { activeBytes, estimatedTokens, contextWindow, percentUsed } when given a valid sessionFile and a known model.
- AC: activeBytes equals fileSize - findLastCompactBoundary(sessionFile) when a compact boundary exists; equals fileSize when no boundary exists.
- AC: estimatedTokens equals Math.ceil(activeBytes / 4); percentUsed = (estimatedTokens / contextWindow) * 100, clamped to [0, 100].
- AC: Vitest unit tests cover: known Claude model, known GPT model, deprecated model that resolves to current, unknown model returns null, null model returns null, file with no compact boundary, file with multiple compact boundaries (uses last), empty file (activeBytes = 0, percentUsed = 0).
- AC: Reuses existing compactOffsetCache via findLastCompactBoundary — does not re-scan the entire JSONL on each call.
close_reason: Added computeContextUsage helper with compact-boundary cache reuse and unit tests covering model resolution, token estimation, boundaries, empty files, and cache reuse.

SQLite writes serialized through a batch queue. Build a correlator.ts helper that queries existing conversations.session_file and cost_events.session_id for Panopticon-managed detection.

Selection via config.conversations.embeddingProvider. Stored as BLOB in session_embeddings with dim + model. Search integration: search --semantic "text" embeds the query with the same provider, loads all embeddings into memory, computes topK by cosine, optionally intersects with structured filters. --similar <id> loads that session's embedding and does the same comparison.

title: pan-1379: Implement issue
description:
## Background

PAN-1249 migrated `src/lib/` to **additive** Effect — every `async fn(): Promise<T>` got an `fnEffect()` sibling, keeping the Promise originals to avoid cascade breakage.

**PAN-1312 (Phase 2) is done** — every `src/cli/` and `src/dashboard/server/` caller now consumes the `*Effect` variants; gate-verified, `typecheck` green, on `main`. Zero `*Async()` call sites remain in production code.

## This issue — Phase 3: finish the migration

Deliver the full Effect-native end state for `src/lib/`. Two phases, in this order, with a verification gate between them:

### Phase 3a — Delete the legacy Promise variants

- **22 `*Async` exports** remain in `src/lib/`, across 8 files: `vbrief/vbrief-index.ts`, `vbrief/io.ts`, `vbrief/dag.ts`, `vbrief/continue-state.ts`, `pan-dir/specs.ts`, `pan-dir/continue.ts`, `memory/checkpoint-client.ts`, `cloister/config.ts`.
- **3 test files** still import `*Async` from `src/lib/`: `tests/lib/cloister/pan-464-container-health.test.ts`, `tests/unit/dashboard/server/routes/projects.test.ts`, `tests/unit/lib/lifecycle/teardown-workspace.test.ts` — migrate these to the `*Effect` siblings *first*, then the `*Async` exports can be deleted.
- Delete each `*Async` export and the dead `Effect.runPromise` bridges that only existed to span the Promise↔Effect boundary.
- Per-file: migrate any remaining test importers → delete `*Async` exports → `npm run typecheck`. A deletion that breaks typecheck means a caller was missed.

**Verification gate:** zero `*Async`-from-`src/lib/` imports anywhere in the repo; `npm run typecheck` + `npm run lint` + `npm test` all green.

### Phase 3b — Canonicalize naming

Once Phase 3a is verified clean (gate above passes), do the cosmetic rename:

- Rename every surviving `fooEffect` → `foo` across `src/lib/`, `src/cli/`, `src/dashboard/server/`, and the test suite. Effect is the canonical form; the `Effect` suffix was temporary scaffolding from PAN-1249's additive phase.
- Where a function has *both* an `*Effect` variant *and* a genuinely-needed sync variant of the same logical operation, the sync one becomes `*Sync` (e.g. `readPlanSync`). The Effect-returning one takes the plain name (`readPlan`).
- This is a codebase-wide mechanical rename — a single coherent commit using a scripted find-replace, then test fixups in the same commit.

**End state:** `src/lib/` exposes `foo()` (returns `Effect`) as the canonical name, `fooSync()` only where sync is genuinely needed. **No `*Async`, no `*Effect` suffix anywhere.**

## Risk control

A prior attempt to do canonicalization *bundled with the caller migration* spiraled ($82 of agent time, ~145 files of test fallout, no convergence — abandoned). The conditions now are different:

- Caller migration is **already done on `main`** — the canonicalization is a pure rename, not bundled with semantic changes.
- Phase 3a + 3b are explicitly **sequenced** — finish deletions first, *verify clean*, *then* canonicalize. Do NOT interleave.
- Use a scripted rename for 3b (one find-replace pass + test fix-ups), not 100 separate Edits.

## Reference

- `backup/pan-1312-deletion-attempt` (on origin) has 4 of the 8 Phase-3a files already cleanly deleted: `agents`, `tmux`, `config-yaml`, `vbrief-dag` async bridges. Those commits can be cherry-picked as a starting reference.

## Done = the migration is fully complete

When 3a + 3b land, `src/lib/` is Effect-native end-to-end, with clean canonical names — the migration arc (PAN-1249 → PAN-1312 → PAN-1379) closed.
- AC: **22 *Async exports** remain in src/lib/, across 8 files: vbrief/vbrief-index.ts, vbrief/io.ts, vbrief/dag.ts, vbrief/continue-state.ts, pan-dir/specs.ts, pan-dir/continue.ts, memory/checkpoint-client.ts, cloister/config.ts.
- AC: **3 test files** still import *Async from src/lib/: tests/lib/cloister/pan-464-container-health.test.ts, tests/unit/dashboard/server/routes/projects.test.ts, tests/unit/lib/lifecycle/teardown-workspace.test.ts — migrate these to the *Effect siblings *first*, then the *Async exports can be deleted.
- AC: Delete each *Async export and the dead Effect.runPromise bridges that only existed to span the Promise↔Effect boundary.
- AC: Per-file: migrate any remaining test importers → delete *Async exports → npm run typecheck. A deletion that breaks typecheck means a caller was missed.
- AC: Rename every surviving fooEffect → foo across src/lib/, src/cli/, src/dashboard/server/, and the test suite. Effect is the canonical form; the Effect suffix was temporary scaffolding from PAN-1249's additive phase.
- AC: Where a function has *both* an *Effect variant *and* a genuinely-needed sync variant of the same logical operation, the sync one becomes *Sync (e.g. readPlanSync). The Effect-returning one takes the plain name (readPlan).
- AC: This is a codebase-wide mechanical rename — a single coherent commit using a scripted find-replace, then test fixups in the same commit.
- AC: Caller migration is **already done on main** — the canonicalization is a pure rename, not bundled with semantic changes.
close_reason: Implemented PAN-1379 Effect migration cleanup; typecheck, lint, npm test, and exported suffix audit passed.

Do not throw on missing/corrupted state.json; `getAgentStateAsync` already returns null in that case. No call sites are migrated in this bead — that is bead 2's job. This bead defines the helper's exact shape so bead 2's wiring and bead 3's tests have a stable contract to write against. Foundation flag is set because the return-shape and naming choices here propagate to two dependent beads; if the shape were wrong, both would have to be redone.

title: pan-1235: Wire missing drawer issue-filtered subscription in useDrawerData

title: pan-1231: AgentCard 'Open issue' actually scrolls IssueDrawer to #active-agent (not just sets URL hash)
description:
Reproduce the audit failure in a real browser via Playwright (isolated instance): start the dashboard, navigate to /?tab=agents, click 'Open issue' on a fleet card with an active agent, and confirm whether the drawer is actually scrolled with the Active Agent section in view at the top of the scrollable region. The wiring code is in place (FleetAgentsView.openAgentIssue line 342-347; IssueDrawer.scrollToActive useEffect line 54-67; DrawerActiveAgent id='active-agent' line 57 and 95) — the most likely root cause is that scrollToActive runs in a useEffect that fires when drawer.issueId changes, but at that moment the DrawerActiveAgent element may not yet be in the DOM (async data load via useDrawerData). Fix: ensure the scroll happens AFTER the active-agent element actually exists — either via a layout effect that watches the element via MutationObserver / ref, or by retrying scroll on a short delay until the element is found (capped retries). Replace the existing FleetAgentsView 'opens the drawer from a fleet card issue action at the active-agent anchor' test with a behavioural test that spies Element.prototype.scrollIntoView and asserts it was called on the live #active-agent element after the click.
- AC: Manual Playwright UAT (isolated browser, no shared session): clicking 'Open issue' on a fleet AgentCard opens the drawer AND the Active Agent section is visible in the drawer's scroll viewport without manual scrolling. Recorded as a passing UAT step.
- AC: A new unit test mounts FleetAgentsView + IssueDrawer + DrawerActiveAgent, spies Element.prototype.scrollIntoView, clicks 'Open issue' on a card, and asserts scrollIntoView was invoked on the element with id='active-agent'. The existing URL-hash-only test is replaced (not just supplemented) — a hash-only assertion is the original closed-without-delivery pattern and must not remain as the sole proof of delivery.
- AC: The fix handles the async DrawerActiveAgent mount: if the element is not in the DOM when the effect first runs, the scroll is retried (e.g., via ref/observer/short polling with a small retry cap) until it succeeds or a clean timeout — never silently no-ops.
- AC: Opening the drawer via other entry points (e.g., kanban card click without #active-agent hash) does NOT auto-scroll to the active-agent anchor — scroll behaviour is gated on the hash being present.
- AC: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, and npm test pass
close_reason: Fixed IssueDrawer scroll to #active-agent with capped retry loop, replaced hash-only test with behavioural scrollIntoView test, and added Playwright UAT.

title: pan-1215: Work-agent startup untracks .pan/continue.json on branches where it leaked (Gap B.1 cleanup)
description:
Add a one-shot cleanup step that runs early in the work-agent spawn flow (best site: in src/lib/agents.ts spawnRun for role==='work', or in src/lib/cloister/work-agent-prompt.ts startup, whichever runs before the first checkpoint and after workspace existence is confirmed). The cleanup checks `git ls-files --error-unmatch .pan/continue.json .pan/spec.vbrief.json` to detect tracked copies; if either is tracked AND `git status --porcelain -- .pan/` shows the workspace clean for those paths, it runs `git rm --cached .pan/continue.json .pan/spec.vbrief.json` (separately for each, ignoring missing-file errors) and commits with subject `chore: untrack workspace .pan/ artifacts (PAN-1215)`. If the workspace is dirty for those paths, log a clear warning and skip — the next clean spawn will pick it up. Cleanup runs at most once per spawn and short-circuits when nothing is tracked.

title: pan-1215: `pan checkpoint` does not capture workspace-only .pan/ artifacts (Gap B.1 root)
description:

title: pan-1194: Add `POST /api/swarm/:issueId/slot/:slotId/recover` recovery endpoint with retry/drop/handoff actions
description:
Add a new Effect route at `POST /api/swarm/:issueId/slot/:slotId/recover` in src/dashboard/server/routes/swarm.ts. Body schema: `{ action: 'retry' | 'drop' | 'handoff' }`. Auth: require the internal token (same pattern as `/api/swarm`). Validate `issueId` via canonicalIssueId, `slotId` as positive integer. Resolve the latest matching slot record (reverse-scan, must be `failed-merge`). Reject 409 if no failed-merge slot found. `retry`: mutate the slot record's status back to a sentinel `'recovering'` (or set status to a value that causes the next dispatch to re-spawn — simplest: re-add the item to a dispatchable set by clearing the matched slot's status and clearing top-level autoAdvanceFailureCount/autoAdvanceRetryAfter/lastAutoAdvanceError; let the next pollSwarmAutoAdvance dispatch run). `drop`: apply `done` task operation to the vBRIEF for `slot.itemId` via `applyTaskOperationToPlanFileAsync` and leave the slot record at `failed-merge` (it's a terminal but advance-allowed state); clear top-level failure counters so auto-advance resumes. `handoff`: clear top-level autoAdvance flag on the SwarmState and emit a handback activity entry. All three: emit `source: 'ship', level: 'info', message: 'Operator recovered slot <N> via <action>'`. Internally use the existing `saveSwarmState` writer. Return 200 with `{ ok: true, action, slotId, issueId }`. Authoritative behavior matrix lives in a JSDoc above the route.
- AC: Route registered at exact path `POST /api/swarm/:issueId/slot/:slotId/recover` with internal-token auth. Returns 403 without the token, 400 for invalid issueId/slotId, 409 if no failed-merge slot exists, 400 for invalid action.
- AC: `action: 'retry'` clears the matched failed-merge slot (reverts to pending/recovering state) AND clears top-level autoAdvanceFailureCount, autoAdvanceRetryAfter, lastAutoAdvanceError. Next pollSwarmAutoAdvance tick is free to dispatch. Unit test verifies the next pollSwarmAutoAdvance call dispatches a fresh slot for the same itemId.
- AC: `action: 'drop'` calls applyTaskOperationToPlanFileAsync({ type: 'done', itemId: <slot.itemId>, reason: 'Operator dropped slot via failed-merge recovery', writerId: 'swarm-recover-drop-<pid>' }) AND clears top-level failure counters. The slot record stays at `failed-merge` but advance is no longer blocked. Subsequent poll dispatches the next DAG-ready item.
- AC: `action: 'handoff'` flips state.autoAdvance to false and emits `source: 'ship', level: 'warn', message: 'Swarm autoAdvance disabled for <ISSUE> after operator handoff of slot <N>. Take it from here.'`. The auto-advance poll loop drops the issue from activeSwarmIssueIds on its next tick (existing cleanup branch).
- AC: Every successful action emits a `source: 'ship', level: 'info'` activity entry recording the operator decision and naming slot, item, action.
- AC: Persistence ordering: ALL three actions write SwarmState via the existing saveSwarmState path. drop additionally writes the vBRIEF via applyTaskOperationToPlanFileAsync; if the vBRIEF write fails, saveSwarmState is NOT called and the route returns 500 with the underlying error (no half-applied state).
- AC: Idempotency: replaying the same recover request on a slot that has already been recovered (no failed-merge entry exists) returns 409 with a clear message rather than 500 or silently re-applying.
- AC: Unit tests for all three actions use vi.useFakeTimers() where the poll loop is exercised post-recovery.

title: pan-1194: Implement `refreshSwarmSlotMergeability` helper with PR-state-driven `failed-merge` detection
description:
Add `async function refreshSwarmSlotMergeability(state: SwarmState, projectPath?: string): Promise<{ state: SwarmState; changed: boolean }>` to src/dashboard/server/routes/swarm.ts, mirroring the contract of the existing `refreshSwarmSlotStatuses`. For each slot whose `status ∈ {'running','completed'}` AND `phase === 'implementation'`, resolve the slot branch (`feature/<issueLower>-slot-<N>`) and query `gh pr list --repo <owner/repo> --head <slotBranch> --state all --json number,mergeable,mergeableState,state,closed,url,mergedAt --limit 5` via `execAsync` with a 5 s `AbortSignal.timeout`. Decision matrix: PR `mergeableState === 'CONFLICTING'` OR (`mergeable === false` && `mergeableState` nullish) → increment `consecutiveConflictCount`; when count reaches 2, transition slot to `failed-merge` with `failureReason: 'PR #<n> not mergeable: <reason>'` and `prUrl: pr.url`. PR list empty AND slot already `completed` → transition (branch was deleted post-merge-attempt). PR `state === 'CLOSED' && !pr.mergedAt` → transition. Any successful mergeable observation resets `consecutiveConflictCount` to 0. Non-GitHub projects (`!resolveGitHubIssue(issueId).isGitHub`) → return `{ state, changed: false }` immediately. gh timeout / shell error → skip that slot for that tick, do NOT transition (transient). MUST use only the latest matching slot record per slot number (reverse-scan + prefer running > completed, same shape as `onSlotMergeComplete`).
- AC: Function signature exactly: `async function refreshSwarmSlotMergeability(state: SwarmState, projectPath?: string): Promise<{ state: SwarmState; changed: boolean }>` exported via `__testInternals` for tests.
- AC: Synthesis slots (`phase === 'synthesis'`) are never inspected (no PR exists). Unit test asserts the helper returns `changed: false` when the only slot is a completed synthesis slot.
- AC: Non-GitHub project (resolveGitHubIssue returns isGitHub=false) is a no-op. Unit test stubs the helper to non-GitHub and asserts no gh process is spawned and changed=false.
- AC: PR CONFLICTING observed once: slot stays at its current status with `consecutiveConflictCount` incremented to 1. Observed twice consecutively: slot transitions to `failed-merge` with failureReason naming the PR number and prUrl populated. Unit test covers both ticks.
- AC: PR list empty AND slot was `completed`: slot transitions to `failed-merge` with failureReason 'No open PR found for <branch>'. PR list empty AND slot was `running`: no transition (PR may not have been opened yet).
- AC: PR closed without merge (`state === 'CLOSED' && !mergedAt`): slot transitions to `failed-merge` with failureReason 'PR #<n> closed without merge'.
- AC: PR mergeable (`mergeable === true` OR `mergeableState ∈ {'CLEAN','UNSTABLE','BEHIND','HAS_HOOKS'}` per existing KNOWN_NON_BLOCKING_STATES): consecutiveConflictCount is reset to 0 if previously > 0. No status transition.
- AC: gh shell-out timeout (AbortSignal fires) OR non-zero exit: slot is skipped for the tick, no transition, no exception bubbles out of the helper. Unit test uses execAsync mock that throws AbortError.
- AC: Cumulative slot history: when state.slots has multiple records sharing a slot number, only the latest running/completed implementation record is inspected and mutated. Historical merged/failed records are untouched. Unit test seeds two records for slot 1 (one merged, one running) and asserts only the running one is mutated.
- AC: No blocking I/O: helper uses execAsync (or execFileAsync), readFile from 'fs/promises', and never imports execSync/readFileSync/readdirSync. Verified by grep in the unit test file or in CI lint.
close_reason: Implemented refreshSwarmSlotMergeability with PR-state failed-merge detection and tests

title: pan-1169: Fail init container loudly on UNRESOLVED_IMPORT warnings during dashboard build
description:
Modify the `init.command` shell pipeline in `infra/.devcontainer-template/docker-compose.devcontainer.yml.template` so that the `npm run build:dashboard:server` step's combined stdout+stderr is captured and scanned for the literal token `UNRESOLVED_IMPORT`. If any line matches, the init container exits non-zero so the failure surfaces as a build error inside init rather than as a runtime `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` inside the server container at startup.

Keep the change local to the existing inline shell command — do NOT introduce a separate script file. A reasonable shape:

```
npm run build:dashboard:server 2>&1 | tee /tmp/dashboard-build.log
if grep -q 'UNRESOLVED_IMPORT' /tmp/dashboard-build.log; then
  echo 'ERROR: dashboard build emitted UNRESOLVED_IMPORT warnings — top-level node_modules is incomplete (see PAN-1169).' >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

The `PIPESTATUS`/`pipefail` handling matters: a `| tee` pipeline can mask the underlying build's non-zero exit, so either set `pipefail` first or check `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` after the tee. Use whichever idiom is portable to the busybox `sh` that the alpine-based init container uses (the existing command runs under `sh -c`, not bash).

Add a comment in the template above the new block explaining that this guard exists to catch the class of failure described in PAN-1169 (top-level node_modules missing → externalized imports unresolved → server crashes at runtime), so a future engineer doesn't remove the grep as 'noise'.
- AC: The init service's `command:` in `infra/.devcontainer-template/docker-compose.devcontainer.yml.template` captures the dashboard server build's stdout+stderr, scans it for the literal token `UNRESOLVED_IMPORT`, and exits the init container with non-zero status if any match is found.
- AC: The exit-status handling is correct under busybox `sh -c`: a non-zero exit from `npm run build:dashboard:server` itself (not just the grep) must also fail init. This means either `set -o pipefail` is used (and works under the container's sh) or `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is explicitly checked.
- AC: A comment above the new guard in the template explains why it exists, references PAN-1169, and warns against removing it as 'noise'.
- AC: On a freshly-rebuilt PAN-1169 workspace with the Bead 1 fix in place, the init container exits 0 (no UNRESOLVED_IMPORT warnings, build completes cleanly) — i.e. the guard does not produce a false positive when the system is working.
- AC: Manual injection test: run the init container once with the Bead 1 fix reverted (`--filter` restored) and a fresh empty top-level node_modules volume, and document the exact observed behavior. If that exact regression no longer emits UNRESOLVED_IMPORT in the current Bun/build environment, also run a direct missing-top-level-dependency injection that removes representative packages required by externalized dashboard imports, and require that the guard exits non-zero with a diagnostic referencing PAN-1169 and UNRESOLVED_IMPORT.
- AC: No new files are added (no separate shell script). The change is entirely inside `infra/.devcontainer-template/docker-compose.devcontainer.yml.template`'s `init.command` block.
notes:
Review clarification for PAN-1169: the exact restored --filter + empty top-level node_modules scenario no longer reproduced UNRESOLVED_IMPORT in this environment because the current dependency graph/build no longer emitted that warning. For AC5, the accepted manual injection method is synthetic top-level dependency removal: remove representative top-level packages required by externalized dashboard imports (yaml, @iarna, effect) from the named node_modules volume before the guarded build, then rerun init. That produced the intended non-zero init exit with the PAN-1169/UNRESOLVED_IMPORT diagnostic and validates the same missing-hoist failure class the guard is meant to catch.
AC12 restored-filter verification documentation (review follow-up): exact scenario was performed with a temporary compose copy where the Bead 1 fix was reverted to the original filtered install command, using a fresh compose project name pan1169filtertest so the top-level container-node-modules volume started empty. Command run: docker compose -f .devcontainer/docker-compose.pan1169-filter-test.yml -p pan1169filtertest up --build --abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from init init. Observed result in this current Bun/build environment: init printed Init complete and exited 0; no UNRESOLVED_IMPORT warning was emitted. Because the exact restored-filter regression no longer reproduces, AC12 accepts the documented equivalent failure-class test: remove representative top-level packages required by externalized dashboard imports (yaml, @iarna, effect) from the named node_modules volume before rerunning the guarded build. That alternate injection produced init exit 1 with the diagnostic referencing PAN-1169 and UNRESOLVED_IMPORT, proving the guard catches the missing-hoist class.
close_reason: Added guarded dashboard build log capture in init. Clean guarded init exited 0. Busybox sh status handling preserves build non-zero exits. A restored --filter install no longer reproduced UNRESOLVED_IMPORT in this environment, so the failure-class injection removed top-level yaml/@iarna/effect before build; init exited 1 with the PAN-1169 UNRESOLVED_IMPORT diagnostic.

title: pan-1148: Define and implement drawer subscription contract (Effect-managed, server-filtered by issueId)

- AC: All drawer subsection components (active agent, beads, specialists, side rail) consume useDrawerData ONLY — no direct fetches or per-section subscriptions
- AC: Server-side filter implemented in src/dashboard/server/ws-rpc.ts; client never receives events for other issues over this stream (vitest with mock server)
- AC: Re-opening the drawer for the same issue id within 1 second reuses the existing subscription (no spurious tear-down + re-subscribe)

title: pan-1148: Add Issue Detail drawer shell + global store slice (single-instance, URL-addressable)
description:
Create src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/drawer/IssueDrawer.tsx as the slide-out shell (980px max-width, full-height pinned right, scrim with backdrop-blur(2px), shadow per PRD §4.7.8). Add `drawer` slice to the existing Zustand store (src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/store.ts) with shape `{ issueId: string | null, tab: string }` and actions `openIssue(id, tab?)`, `closeIssue()`. Wire URL sync: `?issue=<id>&tab=<tab>` is the authoritative state — opening reflects to URL, closing removes both params, opening a different issue REPLACES the prior one (sequential, never stacked). Esc, X button, click-on-scrim all close. Parent surface dims (4% accent overlay + 2px blur) behind. Inspect: ensure the single-instance invariant is enforced at the store level (opening B while A is open is a replace, not a stack); ensure subscription teardown happens on close (no leaks on rapid open→close→open burst).
- AC: IssueDrawer.tsx implements PRD §4.7.8 surface spec: 980px max-width, max-width: calc(100vw - 48px), full-height pinned right, backdrop-filter blur(2px), shadow -24px 0 64px rgb(0 0 0 / 40%)
- AC: Zustand store has new `drawer` slice with `{ issueId: string | null, tab: string }` and actions `openIssue(id, tab?)`, `closeIssue()`; opening a new issue while one is open REPLACES (not stacks)
