title: pan-1170: Implement issue
description:
## Problem

PAN-829 wired the dashboard's in-process TTS subscriber (\`startTtsPlayback\`) but left the **Qwen3-TTS HTTP daemon** (\`skills/pan-tts/scripts/tts_daemon.py\`) as a manual-start, undocumented dependency. Every TTS feature in Panopticon — activity TTS playback, voice sampling, voice preset previews, AutoPreso voice feedback — POSTs to that daemon at \`daemonHost:daemonPort/speak\`. If the daemon isn't running, every TTS path fails with \`daemon-unavailable\` / \`TTS daemon unavailable\` and the user has no path-of-least-resistance to fix it.

Tonight a user hit:
- \"daemon is not running\" in the TTS status indicator
- \`{\"spoken\":false,\"result\":\"daemon-unavailable\",\"error\":\"TTS daemon unavailable\"}\` when trying to sample a voice preset

In both cases the actual fix was \`cd ~/Projects/qwen-tts && nohup .venv/bin/python /path/to/skills/pan-tts/scripts/tts_daemon.py &\`. That is not discoverable, and the dependency on a separate \`~/Projects/qwen-tts\` venv outside the panopticon-cli repo is even worse.

## Scope (single issue, all phases)

### 1. Install
- Move daemon Python deps under panopticon-cli (or under \`packages/qwen-tts-linux-x64/\` like the Moonshine sidecar) instead of \`~/Projects/qwen-tts/\`.
- Add \`pan install\` step that creates the daemon venv and installs \`qwen-tts\`, \`torch\` (with CUDA bindings), \`soundfile\`, \`numpy\`. Heavy — should be skippable via \`--skip-tts-daemon\` (heavy because of CUDA torch ~5GB).
- Optional: detect GPU and skip / warn if no CUDA available (daemon won't run usefully on CPU at the model's size).
- On non-Linux platforms, skip with a clear message.

### 2. Start / stop CLI
- \`pan tts start\` — launches the daemon (foreground or detached via \`--detach\`), waits for \`/health\` to return ok before exiting.
- \`pan tts stop\` — graceful SIGTERM → SIGKILL with PID tracked under \`~/.panopticon/pids/qwen-tts.pid\`.
- \`pan tts status\` — reports daemon PID, port, model, queue depth, uptime, GPU memory used.
- \`pan tts restart\` — wraps stop + start.
- All commands honor \`tts.daemonHost\` and \`tts.daemonPort\` from config.

### 3. Lifecycle integration
- \`pan up\` optionally launches the daemon (gated by \`tts.daemon.autoStart\` in config — default off because of the cold-start cost and VRAM footprint).
- Optional systemd user unit installer (\`pan tts install-systemd\`) for users who want auto-start on boot. Template lives in repo, \`pan install\` doesn't enable it by default.
- Dashboard supervisor / watchdog (extend the \`src/supervisor/watchdog.ts\` pattern from PAN-1139) detects daemon crash and restarts (with backoff and a give-up threshold so a misconfigured GPU doesn't restart-loop forever).

### 4. UI surface
- Dashboard Settings → TTS tab: \"Daemon: running on cuda:0 (4.2GB VRAM) | model loaded\" with a \"Start daemon\" button when it's down.
- Health badge in the sidebar (existing CloisterStatusBar already shows TTS — point it at the new status payload).

### 5. Docs
- Update \`skills/pan-tts/SKILL.md\` with the new CLI surface and remove the manual \`cd skills/pan-tts/scripts && python tts_daemon.py\` instruction (it survives as the lowest-level escape hatch).
- Add to \`docs/PANOPTICON_DEV_SOP.md\` (the doc PAN-1139 created) so post-restart troubleshooting includes \`pan tts status\`.

## Out of scope
- Replacing Qwen3-TTS with a different model.
- Cross-machine daemon hosting (the existing pan-tts SSE subscriber already handles that).
- Browser-side fallback synthesis (Web Speech API) for voice samples — keep the daemon as the single audio path so previews match what users hear in production.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Fresh \`pan install\` on a Linux/CUDA machine produces a working daemon (\`pan tts start\` → \`/api/tts/health\` returns ok).
- [ ] \`pan tts start\`, stop, status, restart all work and round-trip a single test phrase via \`pan tts test\`.
- [ ] Dashboard Settings TTS tab shows live daemon status and offers a one-click \"Start daemon\" when it's down.
- [ ] Crash + restart: kill the daemon process, watchdog brings it back within 30s.
- [ ] \`pan install --skip-tts-daemon\` completes without touching CUDA torch.
- [ ] Non-Linux platforms see a clear skip message during install (no failure).

## Why now

Tonight's session blocked at two separate points on the missing daemon — first \"TTS broken\" diagnosis, then \"voice sampling broken\" diagnosis — each requiring manual investigation. With \`pan tts start\` and the supervisor, both paths self-heal.

## Related
- PAN-829 (TTS lifecycle, merged) — shipped the in-process subscriber but didn't own the synth daemon.
- PAN-1139 (dashboard restart watchdog) — supervisor pattern to reuse here.
- PAN-1162 (ship-role allowHost) — example of a small substrate fix that unblocks a recurring failure mode.
- AC: Fresh \pan install\ on a Linux/CUDA machine produces a working daemon (\pan tts start\ → \/api/tts/health\ returns ok).
- AC: \pan tts start\, stop, status, restart all work and round-trip a single test phrase via \pan tts test\.
- AC: Dashboard Settings TTS tab shows live daemon status and offers a one-click \"Start daemon\" when it's down.
- AC: Crash + restart: kill the daemon process, watchdog brings it back within 30s.
- AC: \pan install --skip-tts-daemon\ completes without touching CUDA torch.
- AC: Non-Linux platforms see a clear skip message during install (no failure).
close_reason: Implementation complete

title: pan-1164: Emit `conversation.diff_summary_updated` from getCachedMessages parse hook
description:
Hook the emit into `getCachedMessages` (src/dashboard/server/routes/conversations.ts). After the parse result is computed (incremental or full), compare its `fileEditsByAssistantId` against the previous cache snapshot's edits to find new or grown entries. For each new assistantId, look up the merged assistant message (skip if not present — guards against orphan UUIDs per H2), then fire-and-forget call the helper from bead `extract-diff-helper` and emit `getEventStore().emitOnly({ type: 'conversation.diff_summary_updated', ... })` with the resulting `TurnDiffSummary` fields. Pass `conversationName` into `getCachedMessages` (currently it only takes `sessionFile` + `isSpecialist`) — derive it from the route caller. Skip emit when `isSpecialist === true` (per H4) or when the conversation lookup fails. Maintain a per-`sessionFile` Map<assistantId, fileCount> in module scope to dedup across concurrent pollers (per H1) and clear it on cache eviction.
- AC: `getCachedMessages` accepts an optional `conversationName?: string` argument; when present and `isSpecialist === false`, the function performs the diff-detect-and-emit step after computing `result`
- AC: The `/api/conversations/:name/messages` route passes the conversation name into `getCachedMessages`; the `/api/conversations/:name/diffs` route and any other callers continue to work (compile + run)
- AC: Detect-and-emit logic is fire-and-forget (`void (async () => {...})()`) so the HTTP response is not delayed; the inner work uses `await` for git/exec calls and handles errors via try/catch + console.error (no unhandled rejections)
- AC: Per-`sessionFile` last-emit tracking dedupes events: the same assistantId with the same file count emits exactly once across multiple concurrent `/messages` polls (verified by an integration test that simulates two parallel calls)
- AC: Orphan tool_use UUIDs (those not present as keys in `result.messages.find(m => m.role === 'assistant')`) do NOT trigger an emit; once re-keying merges them into the real assistant message UUID, that real UUID DOES emit
- AC: Specialist sessions (`isSpecialist=true`) and sessions for which `getConversationByName` returns null do not emit (silent skip, no error)
- AC: Integration test in `src/dashboard/server/__tests__/`: append a tool_use entry for `Edit` to a fixture JSONL between two `getCachedMessages` calls; assert exactly one `conversation.diff_summary_updated` event is captured from `getEventStore()` with the correct `conversationName`, `assistantMessageId`, and `files[]`
- AC: `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` all pass

title: pan-1139: Persist restart outcomes to `~/.panopticon/restart-status.json` and display in `pan status`

title: pan-1139: Active watchdog in supervisor: poll `/api/health`, auto-restart with cap
description:
Extend `src/supervisor/server.ts` with a background watchdog. On startup, read `PANOPTICON_SUPERVISOR_WATCHDOG` env (default '1'); if disabled, skip. Otherwise: every 10s (`PANOPTICON_SUPERVISOR_POLL_MS`), `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:${dashboardApiPort}/api/health', { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(2000) })`. Track `consecutiveFailures` (reset on any 2xx) and a sliding-window `restartAttempts[]` (timestamps in last 5 min). After 3 consecutive failures (`PANOPTICON_SUPERVISOR_FAIL_THRESHOLD`), check if `restartAttempts.length >= 3` (`PANOPTICON_SUPERVISOR_MAX_RESTARTS`) within 5 min (`PANOPTICON_SUPERVISOR_WINDOW_MS`) — if so, log loudly with 'WATCHDOG GIVING UP — manual intervention required' and stop attempting (don't restart at all until consecutiveFailures resets via a manual recovery). Otherwise: check the restart lockfile from the lockfile bead; if held, skip this cycle. If free: append timestamp to `restartAttempts`, spawn `pan restart --dashboard` exactly as the existing `/restart-dashboard` endpoint does, and log the trigger. Add a new `GET /status` endpoint returning `{healthy, lastCheck, consecutiveFailures, restartAttempts, gaveUp, lastError}` so the dashboard and `pan status` can read watchdog state. The dashboardApiPort is read from `readPlatformConfig()` so the supervisor doesn't need extra env wiring.
- AC: Supervisor polls `/api/health` every 10s by default (overridable via PANOPTICON_SUPERVISOR_POLL_MS).
- AC: After 3 consecutive failures, the supervisor spawns `pan restart --dashboard` and logs the trigger to `~/.panopticon/logs/supervisor.log`.
- AC: If 3 restart attempts have occurred within a 5-min rolling window, the watchdog logs 'WATCHDOG GIVING UP' and stops attempting until consecutiveFailures resets (i.e., a manual recovery brings the dashboard back).
- AC: If the restart lockfile is held by another caller (e.g., `pan reload` is in flight), the watchdog skips that cycle without consuming an attempt.
- AC: `PANOPTICON_SUPERVISOR_WATCHDOG=0` disables the watchdog loop at startup (the supervisor still serves /health, /restart-dashboard, /status).
- AC: `GET /status` returns `{healthy, lastCheck, consecutiveFailures, restartAttempts: [iso8601...], gaveUp, lastError}`. Endpoint is available even when the watchdog is disabled.
- AC: Manual smoke: kill the dashboard with `pkill -f dashboard/server.js`; within ~40s, the supervisor restarts it and `curl /api/health` returns 200 again. Confirm via supervisor.log.

title: pan-1139: Add `pan reload` CLI command (build-verified restart)
description:
Create `src/cli/commands/reload.ts` exporting `reloadCommand(options)`. Flow: (1) call `acquireRestartLock('pan reload')` — if null, print 'restart in progress (held by PID X)' and exit 2; (2) unless `--skip-build`, capture the pre-build mtime of `dist/dashboard/server.js` (or 0 if missing), spawn `npm run build` with stdio inherit so the user sees compiler output, await exit; if exit code != 0, print 'Build failed — old dashboard left running' and exit 1 WITHOUT calling stopDashboard; (3) verify `dist/dashboard/server.js` exists AND its mtime > pre-build mtime — abort with clear error if not; (4) call `restartDashboard(config, spawnDashboardDetached, { healthTimeoutMs })` (defaults to 30000); on StageError, print the staged error verbatim; (5) release the lock in a finally block. title: pan-1139: Add restart lockfile primitive (acquire/release/stale-detection)
description:
Add a new module `src/lib/restart-lock.ts` exporting `acquireRestartLock(caller: string): { release(): void } | null` and `readRestartLockHolder(): { pid, ts, caller } | null`. Lockfile lives at `${PANOPTICON_HOME}/restart.lock` and contains JSON `{pid, ts, caller}`. Acquire writes the file atomically (open with O_EXCL); if the file exists, parse it — if PID is dead OR ts is older than 5 min, overwrite (stale); otherwise return `null`. Release deletes the file (idempotent; tolerates missing). No SIGCHLD trap needed — beads that use the lock are responsible for calling release(), and the next caller's stale-detection will recover from forgotten releases. This is the cross-cutting primitive the next three beads depend on.
- AC: `acquireRestartLock(caller)` returns a release handle on first call; returns null if a live lock is held by a different PID < 5 min old.
- AC: Stale-detection: if the lockfile's PID is dead (process.kill(pid, 0) throws) OR ts is > 5 min ago, acquireRestartLock overwrites and succeeds.
- AC: release() deletes the lockfile and is idempotent (calling twice does not throw).
- AC: Lockfile path is `${PANOPTICON_HOME}/restart.lock` (uses paths.ts PANOPTICON_HOME, not hard-coded), and parent dir is auto-created.
- AC: Vitest unit tests cover: fresh acquire, contention, stale-by-time, stale-by-dead-PID, idempotent release.
close_reason: Added restart lockfile primitive with stale detection, guarded idempotent release, and Vitest coverage.

title: pan-1141: Exponential backoff and threshold-based troubled flip
description:

Default `backoffSchedule = [5, 30, 120]` (seconds). Track `firstFailureInRunAt`: set on the first failure of a run, cleared on counter reset. When `consecutiveFailures >= maxConsecutiveFailures` AND `(now - firstFailureInRunAt) <= troubledWindowMs`, call `markAgentTroubled()`. If the window has elapsed without hitting the threshold, reset `firstFailureInRunAt` to the current failure timestamp. Default thresholds: `maxConsecutiveFailures = 3`, `troubledWindowMs = 600000` (10 min). Add a skip clause in `autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents()` that skips agents whose `lastFailureNextRetryAt > Date.now()` (inclusive equality means retry-now). Create `src/lib/cloister/auto-resume-config.ts` exporting `AutoResumeConfig` interface and `DEFAULT_AUTO_RESUME_CONFIG` for reuse by tests and config overrides.
- AC: After 1st failure, agent is skipped during the next 5 seconds and resumable after; after 2nd, 30s; after 3rd, 120s
- AC: 3 consecutive failures within 10 minutes (default config) flip `troubled = true` and stamp `troubledAt`
- AC: If failures span > 10 minutes (e.g. 1 failure now, 2 more 11 minutes later), no troubled-flip happens — `firstFailureInRunAt` slides to the failure that resets the window
- AC: `AutoResumeConfig` interface and defaults exported from `src/lib/cloister/auto-resume-config.ts`
- AC: Skipping during backoff logs `autoResumeStoppedWorkAgents: <id> skipped — backoff active (next retry at <iso>)`

title: pan-1143: Implement issue
description:
## Symptom

`pan plan done <id>` (and the dashboard "Done" button) report **success** even when the canonical spec was never written and beads were never materialized. The user sees a green check, agent gets started, work agent has nothing to do (or has 1 placeholder bead instead of the planned 22).

- Planning agent (auto mode) wrote `workspaces/feature-pan-1141/.pan/spec.vbrief.json` with 22 plan items
- No canonical spec created at `<projectRoot>/.pan/specs/`
- `pan plan done PAN-1141` returned: `✓ Planning complete for PAN-1141`
- After: still no canonical spec, beads still show only 1 generic `PAN-1141: Implement issue` placeholder
- Work agent spawned successfully and loaded "1 task"

## Root cause

`src/dashboard/server/routes/issues.ts:1044-1053`:

```ts
const { pushed: gitPushed, beadsWarning } = yield* Effect.promise(async () => {
  if (!projectPath) return { pushed: false, beadsWarning: null };

  const workspacePath = join(projectPath, 'workspaces', `feature-${issueLower}`);
  const workspacePlanPath = findPlan(workspacePath);   // ← returns null on first run

  let gitRoot = '';
  if (workspacePlanPath) gitRoot = workspacePath;

  if (!gitRoot) return { pushed: false, beadsWarning: null };  // ← bails silently
  // ... spec promotion + bead sync never runs
```

`findPlan(workspacePath)` resolves via `findSpecByIssue(projectRoot, issueId)` in `src/lib/vbrief/io.ts:44`, which scans **only** `<projectRoot>/.pan/specs/`. There is no workspace-draft fallback. So on the **first** finalize attempt — when the canonical spec by definition doesn't yet exist — `findPlan` returns null and the entire promotion-and-bead-sync block is skipped. The endpoint returns `{ success: true }` regardless.

Additionally: the catch on line 1117-1119 around `writeSpecForIssue` swallows any promotion error as "non-fatal" with only a `console.warn` — so even if the path executed, errors wouldn't surface to the caller.

## Why this is critical

The documented planning lifecycle is: workspace draft → `pan plan-finalize` → `pan plan done`. The first link is broken because **`pan plan finalize` also calls `findPlan(workspace)` and fails with "No workspace spec found"** for the same reason — it expects the canonical spec to already exist, which it can't on first run.

Net effect: the auto-plan path silently produces unusable artifacts. Bug-by-bug:
1. **First-run chicken-and-egg.** `findPlan` requires canonical spec; canonical spec requires successful finalize; finalize requires canonical spec.
2. **Silent success.** Both `pan plan finalize` ("✓ No workspace spec found" is `process.exit(1)`, fine) and `complete-planning` (returns 200 with `success: true`) fail to surface the missing-canonical case usefully to the operator.
3. **Work agent runs on stub beads.** `pan start` happily spawns an agent with 1 placeholder bead, leading to "agent has nothing to do" or "agent does ill-defined mega-task" failures downstream.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **First-run path works.** When `complete-planning` runs and no canonical spec exists, it reads the workspace draft at `<workspace>/.pan/spec.vbrief.json`, validates it, and uses it as the source for `writeSpecForIssue(...)`. The canonical spec gets written, beads get materialized, the issue advances. No more silent bail at line 1053.
- [ ] **Same for `pan plan finalize`.** If invoked when canonical spec doesn't exist, it should accept the workspace draft as the source.
- [ ] **No more silent error swallow.** Remove or narrow the catch at line 1117-1119 — promotion failures must propagate to the HTTP response so the CLI fails loudly with the real error.
- [ ] **Work-agent start validates beads count > 1.** Or validates plan items match bead count. Refuses to spawn with the stub placeholder.
- [ ] **Planning role doc is accurate.** `roles/plan.md` step 6 references `pan plan-finalize` (hyphenated, doesn't exist as a separate command). Align doc with actual CLI: `pan plan finalize`.
- [ ] **Test coverage.** Integration test for the first-run path: create a workspace draft, call complete-planning, assert canonical spec written + N beads created.

## Out of scope

- Reworking the four-artifact model in `docs/VBRIEF.md` — the model is fine; the implementation diverges from it.
- Adding new planning modes.

## Why this matters operationally

I just spent ~20 minutes of context tracing why PAN-1141 had 1 bead instead of 22. A first-time user would hit this on their first non-trivial plan, get an unusable workspace, and have no idea why. This is the kind of bug that destroys trust in the planning pipeline.

## Related

- PAN-1124 (single-spec-on-main model) — the architecture that introduced this. The model is sound; the first-run case wasn't wired up.
- PAN-1140 (workspace init container fix) — concurrent in-flight work, no direct overlap.

## Workaround until fixed

Manually re-run the planning agent for the affected issue. If it fails the second time the same way, that's a deterministic bug — file a comment with the agent's transcript.
- AC: **First-run path works.** When complete-planning runs and no canonical spec exists, it reads the workspace draft at <workspace>/.pan/spec.vbrief.json, validates it, and uses it as the source for writeSpecForIssue(...). The canonical spec gets written, beads get materialized, the issue advances. No more silent bail at line 1053.
- AC: **Same for pan plan finalize.** If invoked when canonical spec doesn't exist, it should accept the workspace draft as the source.
- AC: **No more silent error swallow.** Remove or narrow the catch at line 1117-1119 — promotion failures must propagate to the HTTP response so the CLI fails loudly with the real error.
- AC: **Work-agent start validates beads count > 1.** Or validates plan items match bead count. Refuses to spawn with the stub placeholder.
- AC: **Planning role doc is accurate.** roles/plan.md step 6 references pan plan-finalize (hyphenated, doesn't exist as a separate command). Align doc with actual CLI: pan plan finalize.
- AC: **Test coverage.** Integration test for the first-run path: create a workspace draft, call complete-planning, assert canonical spec written + N beads created.
close_reason: Implemented first-run vBRIEF draft promotion, loud completion failures, bead-count start validation, planning command docs, and regression coverage.

Add a 3-5 line comment above the catch block explaining why the heuristic is gone (refs beads v1.0.3 dolt auto-recovery + v1.0.4 perms repair). The work.inspect gate runs here because every subsequent bead (tests, integration test) builds on this exact control flow — a wrong rewrite cascades.
- AC: On `bd ping` failure, the code invokes `bd doctor --fix` exactly once before retrying the probe
- AC: The stale-artifact heuristic (staleArtifacts array, presentStale check, dolt-residue diagnostic) is deleted from src/lib/vbrief/beads.ts
- AC: The redirect-vs-main-beads branch logic in the catch block is collapsed into a single retry/error-return path

title: pan-1107: Implement issue
description:
## Symptom

\`agent-pan-457-ship\` ran for 23m and accumulated \$4.95 in gpt-5.5 spend resolving 19 sync-main merge conflicts on PAN-457 (\`feature/pan-457\`).

That's an order of magnitude higher than the expected ship-role cost. Ship is meant to be mechanical conflict resolution + verification on a cheap workhorse model; previous ship runs typically cost a few cents.

Status line at completion:
\`\`\`
gpt-5.5 (gpt-5.5)  ctx 63%  189/200.0k  out 260  cost \$4.9465  +2/-1
\`\`\`

## Contributing factors (suspected)

- 19 conflicts is on the high end. A few of them involved \`.beads/config.yaml\` (with conflict markers inside YAML) and \`.pan/spec.vbrief.json\`, which the ship agent had to repeatedly re-scan.
- One tool call referenced a stale path (\`src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/MissionControl/styles/mission-control.module.css\`) that no longer exists. That suggests the agent was using cached state from training or earlier turns rather than reading the actual tree.
- Verification ran the full \`npm test\` (329 files) which is appropriate but pulls heavy context.
- Ship apparently ran through several rounds of \"stage → verify → fix\" loops based on output budget (out=260).

## Why it matters

Sync-main is invoked automatically on every \`pan start\` for an existing workspace. If sync-main routinely produces 19-conflict merges that cost \$5 in ship time, the per-restart cost adds up fast.

## Acceptance

- Capture per-attempt cost in the ship role audit log so spikes are visible from the dashboard
- Investigate whether the agent's repeated re-scans of conflict files can be short-circuited (e.g., feed it the conflict-marker locations directly instead of re-reading every file)
- Decide whether ship should bail out and ask for human help past a certain cost/conflict-count threshold rather than burn through a workhorse budget

- AC: Verification ran the full \npm test\ (329 files) which is appropriate but pulls heavy context.
- AC: Ship apparently ran through several rounds of \"stage → verify → fix\" loops based on output budget (out=260).
- AC: Capture per-attempt cost in the ship role audit log so spikes are visible from the dashboard

title: pan-1106: Implement issue
description:
## Symptom

In the Command Deck issue tree, PAN-457 row expands to:

\`\`\`
PAN-457  Archived Conversations page — …
  Review (gpt-5.5)               error
    Correctness (gpt-5.5)        stopped

    Requirements (gpt-5.5)       stopped

\`\`\`

The \`agent-pan-457-ship\` and \`agent-pan-457\` (work) sessions are running for the same issue at the same time, but they don't appear under the PAN-457 node in the tree. They show up in the flat Conversations list in the sidebar instead.

## Expected

Per \`docs/ROLES.md\`, every issue has up to five roles: plan, work, review, test, ship. The issue-tree should render whichever roles exist for that issue (with their model and live status), not just review and its sub-roles.

## Why it matters

- Whether the issue has a work agent at all (\"why hasn't anything happened on PAN-457?\")
- What model each role is running on
- Whether ship/test passed
- Where to click to attach to the right session

## Suspected cause

The tree-row renderer probably hardcodes review as the only role that gets a sub-row, instead of iterating over the roles defined for the issue. Likely in \`src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/CommandDeck/\`.

## Acceptance

- PAN-457 row in the issue tree shows: work, ship, review (with its sub-roles), test, plan — for whichever are present
- Each role row shows its model, status, and (where applicable) cost
- Clicking a role row opens the right tmux session / conversation

- AC: Each role row shows its model, status, and (where applicable) cost

title: pan-1105: Implement issue
description:
## Repro

PAN-457 review run \`agent-pan-457-review-5c799040\` (2026-05-12 ~17:10Z): all four convoy reviewers (security, correctness, performance, requirements) exited before producing a non-empty report. A retry was attempted for each — also exited without writing the required output file.

Synthesis at \`.pan/review/agent-pan-457-review-5c799040/synthesis.md\`:

> ### [security] Reviewer failed to write report — security.md
> The security reviewer session exited before producing a non-empty report. A retry was attempted and also exited without producing the required output file.

(Same line for correctness/performance/requirements.)

## Why it matters

When all four convoy reviewers fail this way, the parent review role marks PAN-XXX as \`review: blocked\` and the work agent cannot auto-respawn. The user has to \`pan reopen\` to unstick. Two PRs hit this back-to-back today (PAN-457, possibly PAN-1069 — the conversations sidebar lists \`agent-pan-1069-review-*\` sessions from earlier).

## Likely cause

Convoy reviewer specialists spawn via Claude Code agents but exit without producing output. Candidates:
- Specialist agent prompt blows past context budget before writing the report
- Specialist agent crashes on first tool call (broken MCP, missing skill, etc.)
- The required-output-file path is wrong or unwriteable
- Specialist is gated on something stale from the workspace state (e.g. \`.beads/\` corruption — but PAN-457 had this resolved by the time review ran)

## Acceptance

- Identify which of the above causes the silent exit
- Surface the underlying error in the synthesis instead of \"exited before producing a non-empty report\"
- Optionally: gate the retry on a different failure mode than \"file missing\" so a second silent exit doesn't look like a fresh failure
- AC: Specialist agent prompt blows past context budget before writing the report
- AC: Specialist agent crashes on first tool call (broken MCP, missing skill, etc.)
- AC: The required-output-file path is wrong or unwriteable
- AC: Specialist is gated on something stale from the workspace state (e.g. \.beads/\ corruption — but PAN-457 had this resolved by the time review ran)
- AC: Identify which of the above causes the silent exit
- AC: Surface the underlying error in the synthesis instead of \"exited before producing a non-empty report\"
- AC: Optionally: gate the retry on a different failure mode than \"file missing\" so a second silent exit doesn't look like a fresh failure
close_reason: Added monitorSynthesisAgent background function that detects silent synthesis exits before the 30-minute deacon threshold and surfaces actual error in reviewNotes. Fixes root cause: review-agent.ts had no detection when synthesis agent died without writing output.

title: pan-1104: Implement issue
description:

- AC: \pan reopen pan-457\ updates the GitHub issue \#457 in eltmon/panopticon-cli, not MIN-848 in Linear

title: pan-1048: Reactive Cloister: onIssueStateChange + stateToRole hooked into existing emitters
description:

Hook into existing internal event sources rather than building a new poller: (a) issue-lifecycle service (src/dashboard/server/services/issue-lifecycle.ts) already emits `issue.*` events when state transitions occur — Cloister subscribes via the dashboard event bus / domain-services. (b) When a work agent emits `agent.completed` (or signals via `pan done`), Cloister transitions the issue state to 'in_review' and onIssueStateChange spawns the review role. (c) Review approval emits a `review.approved` event → Cloister transitions to 'testing' → spawns test. (d) Test pass emits `test.passed` → transition to 'shipping' → spawn ship. Concurrency guard: skip spawn if an active run already exists for the (issue, role) tuple. stateToRole maps: in_planning → 'plan', in_progress → 'work', in_review → 'review', testing → 'test', shipping → 'ship'. requiresInspection=true because this is the cross-cutting protocol — C2 deletes the old dispatch machinery on the assumption this works.
- AC: src/lib/cloister/service.ts exports `onIssueStateChange(issueId, newState)` and `stateToRole(state): Role | null`
- AC: Cloister subscribes to existing issue.* domain events (issue-lifecycle.ts) and existing agent-completion events (agent.completed, work.completed, review.approved, test.passed)
- AC: stateToRole maps in_planning→plan, in_progress→work, in_review→review, testing→test, shipping→ship; closed/canceled→null
- AC: Concurrency guard: if an active run exists for (issueId, role), the second spawn is skipped (and logged)
- AC: End-to-end test: simulating a work-agent completion event drives the issue to in_review and spawns a review run; review approval drives to testing; test pass drives to shipping; etc.

title: PAN-1031: Harden bead-close hook parsing for multiline commands
description: The inspect-on-bead-close hook can see multiline Bash tool inputs. When any later line contains bd close, the current line-oriented sed extraction leaves unrelated earlier command lines in the candidate argument list, causing false bead IDs such as 'install' to be inspected. Parse the Bash command as a single stream and extract only tokens after the actual bd close invocation so hook installation or heredoc commands cannot dispatch bogus inspections.
acceptance_criteria: A multiline Bash command that includes setup/install work before a bd close line dispatches inspection for the real bead ID only; commands without a valid bd close invocation dispatch nothing; focused hook tests cover the multiline regression while existing local-CLI and pan fallback behavior stays intact.
close_reason: Multiline hook parsing hardened and verified

title: PAN-1031: Pin inspect specialist to sentinel-safe runtime
description: Inspect specialists routed to MiniMax through claudish repeatedly exited without any assistant message or INSPECTION PASSED/BLOCKED sentinel, leaving the bead workflow stuck. Inspect is a control-plane gate whose sentinel output is parsed by Cloister, so dispatch must use a runtime that can reliably run the Claude Code agent definition and emit literal sentinels. Force inspect-agent dispatch away from non-direct provider wrappers and document/test the routing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When work-type routing resolves specialist-inspect-agent to a non-direct provider model, spawnEphemeralSpecialist falls back to the Anthropic direct inspect runtime before launching; registry resolution trace makes the fallback visible; tests cover inspect fallback without changing other specialist routing.
close_reason: Direct inspect runtime fallback implemented and verified

title: PAN-1031: Keep bead-close inspect hook workspace-local
description: The per-agent bead-close hook still invokes the global pan binary from ~/.panopticon/bin/inspect-on-bead-close. In a feature workspace this can dispatch stale main-built code and fail before inspection, as happened when main lacked the dist/cli/prompts inspect prompt asset. Fix the hook source and installer so bead-close inspections prefer the current workspace's built CLI when available and the hook script is installed by setup even though it is no longer registered globally.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/inspect-on-bead-close prefers node ./dist/cli/index.js when run from a workspace with that built CLI and falls back to pan otherwise; setup installs inspect-on-bead-close into ~/.panopticon/bin for per-agent frontmatter hooks; automated coverage or a shellcheck-style test verifies the local CLI selection behavior without invoking a destructive request.
close_reason: Bead-close hook now prefers workspace-local built CLI, setup installs the per-agent hook script, and tests cover local/fallback dispatch.

title: PAN-1031: Stabilize inspect specialist prompt context
description: pan inspect spawned the inspect specialist but the prompt context was unusable: bead details were missing because bd show --json returns an array with acceptance_criteria, and the specialist looped over a huge repeated prompt without delivering INSPECTION PASSED or INSPECTION BLOCKED. Fix the inspect dispatch context so per-bead inspections receive concrete bead requirements and can terminate with a sentinel result.
acceptance_criteria: bd show --json array output is parsed into title/description/acceptance_criteria/labels in the inspect prompt; inspect specialist dispatch has automated coverage for the bead-description parsing shape; the fix does not manually approve or bypass inspection.
close_reason: Inspect dispatch now includes bead metadata, avoids duplicate model/permission flags, launches inspectors from the workspace, and has focused tests plus typecheck/lint/build verification.

title: pan-829: POST /api/tts/speak — voice-resolving proxy to Qwen3-TTS daemon
description:
Create src/dashboard/server/routes/tts.ts and a shared resolver src/lib/tts-speak.ts. The resolver function resolveAndSpeak({ text, source?, eventType?, issueId? }): Promise<'spoken'|'muted'|'daemon-unavailable'|'no-voice'> implements: (1) mute check — if source in config.tts.mutedSources, return 'muted'; (2) issue mute check — if issueId in config.tts.mutedIssues, return 'muted'; (3) template override — if utteranceTemplates[eventType] exists, substitute {issueId} and replace text; (4) voice resolution — look up voiceMap[eventType] first, fall back to config.tts.voice (for priority<2 events) or config.tts.statusVoice (for priority=2 routine events), if neither set return 'no-voice'; (5) load voice from tts-voices.json; (6) build speak payload: preset→{voice:presetName,instruct:instruct??'',mode:'custom'}, design→{voice:description,instruct:instruct,mode:'design'}, clone→{voice:'clone',mode:'clone',embedding:embedding}; (7) POST to http://{daemonHost}:{daemonPort}/speak; (8) on ECONNREFUSED/timeout return 'daemon-unavailable'. The HTTP route POST /api/tts/speak calls resolveAndSpeak with body fields; returns 200 with {spoken,result} or 503 if daemon unavailable. Register the route in server.ts.
- AC: POST /api/tts/speak with a preset voice sends correct {voice,instruct,mode:'custom'} to port 8787
- AC: POST /api/tts/speak with a clone voice sends {mode:'clone',embedding:[...]} to port 8787
- AC: Muted source returns 200 {result:'muted'} — no call to port 8787

title: pan-985: Dismiss the dev-channels confirmation dialog at agent startup with one Enter keystroke
description:
In the work-agent launch path in src/lib/agents.ts, after the tmux session is created and BEFORE the first deliverAgentMessage / sendKeysAsync of an actual prompt, add a dismissDevChannelsDialog(agentId) step that runs only when channelsEnabled is true for the agent. Implementation: poll capturePaneAsync for the literal string 'WARNING: Loading development channels' (case-sensitive) every 200ms with a 20-second timeout (cold-start claude with TLDR + Playwright MCP servers commonly takes 8-15s to render the first frame; a tighter budget will frequently false-negative and silently fall through to tmux). On match, call sendRawKeystrokeAsync(agentId, 'C-m', 'channels:dismiss-dev-dialog') ONCE and wait 500ms. If the string is not found within the timeout, log 'channels:dismiss:dialog-not-detected' and proceed (the dialog is suppressed in some auth states). Must NOT use sendKeysAsync (that would type text and submit). The dismissal step must run before any prompt is delivered, otherwise the channel listener does not register and all early channel pushes silently fail.
- AC: dismissDevChannelsDialog runs only when the agent state has channelsEnabled: true; flag-off launches skip it entirely
- AC: When the dialog text is detected within 20s, exactly one sendRawKeystrokeAsync(C-m) is fired (verified by checking the send-keys log)
- AC: When the dialog text is NOT detected within 20s, the launch continues (does not block forever) and a 'channels:dismiss:dialog-not-detected' log line is written
- AC: Implementation uses sendRawKeystrokeAsync, NOT sendKeysAsync (no load-buffer/paste-buffer machinery for a single keystroke)
- AC: Dismissal completes before any deliverAgentMessage is called for that agent (test asserts ordering with a fake clock or call-order assertion)
close_reason: See commit history on feature/pan-985 for workspace-02v7 implementation.

title: pan-985: Add deliverAgentMessage primitive in src/lib/agents.ts with eligibility check and tmux fallback
description:
Export a new function deliverAgentMessage(agentId, message, caller?) from src/lib/agents.ts. The function: (a) reads the agent state file at ${PANOPTICON_HOME}/agents/<id>/state.json and looks up channelsEnabled (written at launch by the launch bead); (b) if channelsEnabled and the socket file exists, POSTs the message as JSON {content, meta: {caller}} to the Unix socket using a 2-second connect+write timeout; (c) on 200 response: returns success and logs to the existing send-keys log file with caller='channel:<original-caller>'; (d) on any failure (ENOENT, ECONNREFUSED, EPIPE, non-2xx, timeout): falls back to sendKeysAsync(agentId, message, caller) and logs the fallback reason. Pure-tmux behavior (channelsEnabled=false in agent state, or no state file) is identical to today: call sendKeysAsync directly with no socket attempt. Function must use async fs/promises (no sync IO) per dashboard server constraints.
- AC: deliverAgentMessage exported from src/lib/agents.ts with signature (agentId: string, message: string, caller?: string) => Promise<void>
- AC: When agent state.channelsEnabled is false or state file missing, deliverAgentMessage delegates to sendKeysAsync exactly once and never attempts a socket connection
- AC: When channelsEnabled is true and socket POST returns 200, sendKeysAsync is NOT called and the channel-path log line is written
- AC: When channelsEnabled is true and socket POST fails (any error mode), deliverAgentMessage falls back to sendKeysAsync and writes a fallback-reason log line; the user-visible behavior is identical to a tmux-only delivery
- AC: Implementation uses fs/promises and node:net (or fetch with unix-socket dispatcher) — no readFileSync/writeFileSync/execSync in this code path
- AC: Unit tests in src/lib/__tests__/deliver-agent-message.test.ts cover: (a) flag-off pure-tmux path, (b) flag-on socket-success path, (c) flag-on socket-ENOENT fallback, (d) flag-on socket-timeout fallback. Each test mocks both the socket and sendKeysAsync.

title: pan-985: Add Unix-socket inbound listener to panopticon-bridge that pushes channel notifications

In src/lib/launcher-generator.ts, add two optional fields to LauncherConfig: `channelsBridgeMcpConfig?: string` (absolute path to the per-agent .mcp.json) and `channelsBridgeServerName?: string` (default 'panopticon-bridge'). When BOTH are set, buildNonConversationCommand and buildCommand for specialist-dispatch must append --mcp-config <path> --dangerously-load-development-channels server:<name> to the claude invocation, before --session-id and --model flags. Do NOT add --strict-mcp-config: --mcp-config is additive by default and we MUST keep project-level MCP servers (TLDR, Playwright) loading alongside the bridge. When either is unset, the generated script must be byte-for-byte identical to today (no new tokens, no whitespace changes). Update src/lib/__tests__/launcher-generator.test.ts: (a) regression test asserting flag-off output is unchanged for representative work-agent and specialist configs, (b) new test asserting flag-on output contains the two new flags in the documented order, (c) test asserting --strict-mcp-config is NOT present in the flag-on output.
- AC: LauncherConfig has optional fields channelsBridgeMcpConfig?: string and channelsBridgeServerName?: string with documented defaults
- AC: generateLauncherScript output is byte-for-byte identical to the current behavior when channelsBridgeMcpConfig is undefined (regression test asserts string equality against a known fixture)
- AC: When channelsBridgeMcpConfig is set, generated command includes --mcp-config <quoted-path> --dangerously-load-development-channels server:panopticon-bridge in that order, before --session-id/--model, and does NOT include --strict-mcp-config
- AC: Existing launcher-generator unit tests pass without modification; new tests added for both flag-off-regression and flag-on cases, including an explicit assertion that --strict-mcp-config is absent
close_reason: See commits on feature/pan-985 for workspace-d79y.

title: pan-985: Scaffold panopticon-bridge as a Bun MCP server entrypoint in src/lib/channels/
description:
Create src/lib/channels/panopticon-bridge.ts as the Bun-runnable MCP server entrypoint. Add @modelcontextprotocol/sdk to root package.json. The file is a single self-contained Bun script: import Server and StdioServerTransport from the SDK, construct a Server with capabilities.experimental['claude/channel'] = {} (no tools entry), include an instructions string telling Claude how to handle incoming <channel source="panopticon-bridge"> events, and connect over StdioServerTransport. Stub the socket listener as a TODO comment for the next bead. The file's header comment must document the Bun-runtime requirement and reference the Claude Code Channels reference URL. The bridge must read PANOPTICON_AGENT_ID from env at startup (passed in via the MCP config env block); fail-fast with a clear error if missing.
- AC: src/lib/channels/panopticon-bridge.ts exists and runs cleanly under Bun (bun run src/lib/channels/panopticon-bridge.ts) without immediate exit when stdin is open
- AC: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk is added to root package.json dependencies and bun install completes successfully
- AC: Server constructor declares capabilities.experimental['claude/channel'] = {} and OMITS capabilities.tools and capabilities.experimental['claude/channel/permission'] (one-way, no reply tool, no permission relay)
- AC: Bridge process exits with non-zero code and a clear error message when PANOPTICON_AGENT_ID env var is unset
- AC: Header comment in panopticon-bridge.ts documents the Bun-runtime requirement, the Channels reference URL, and the fact that the socket-unlink-on-startup is intentional (not defensive)

title: pan-636: End-to-end smoke test: spawn Pi agent, drive one prompt, assert lifecycle signals
description:
Add a vitest under src/lib/runtimes/__tests__/pi-e2e.test.ts (gated behind `if (process.env.PAN_E2E === '1')` so it doesn't run in standard CI without Pi installed). It: (1) spawns a Pi work agent for a fixture issue against a fake provider (or `pi --provider mock` if Pi supports it; otherwise targets ollama with a tiny local model), (2) waits for ready.json, (3) sends a prompt via fifo, (4) waits for /pan-done marker after a custom command, (5) parses the session JSONL via pi-parser and asserts non-zero token totals + non-zero cost_v2, (6) kills the agent and verifies cleanup. Documents how to run the test locally in docs/HARNESSES.md.
- AC: Test gated behind PAN_E2E=1 env var; CI default skips it
- AC: Test spawns a Pi agent, observes ready.json within 30s, sends a prompt that triggers tool execution, observes a heartbeat file refresh, observes /pan-done marker
- AC: Test verifies pi-parser returns non-zero tokens and non-zero cost_v2 from the resulting session JSONL
- AC: Test verifies killAgent cleans up rpc.in/ready.json/heartbeat but preserves the session JSONL

title: pan-636: PiRuntime.killAgent: graceful RPC abort then SIGTERM then SIGKILL
description:
killAgent writes {cmd:'abort'} to the fifo, waits 2s for graceful shutdown (poll tmux pane PID exit), then SIGTERM the Pi process, waits 5s, then SIGKILL. Always unlinks the fifo and removes the per-agent dir's transient files (heartbeat, ready.json, completed marker). NEVER deletes session JSONL files (per CLAUDE.md sacred-jsonl rule).
- AC: killAgent on a healthy Pi process exits within 3s and the tmux session is gone
- AC: killAgent on a hung Pi process (ignoring abort) escalates to SIGTERM after 2s and SIGKILL after 7s total
- AC: killAgent unlinks rpc.in, ready.json, heartbeat, and completed marker but does NOT delete the session JSONL under <agentDir>/sessions/
close_reason: Replaced minimal killAgent with full ladder: writePiCommand({cmd:abort}) — graceful flush — then pollUntilSessionGone (2s @ 100ms cadence) — then tmux send-keys C-c + pkill -TERM -f agent-id=<id> — then poll (5s) — then tmux kill-session SIGKILL fallback. cleanupPiTransientFiles always runs and removes rpc.in (destroyPiFifo), ready.json, completed marker, ~/.panopticon/heartbeats/<id>.json — but NEVER touches <agentDir>/sessions/*.jsonl (sacred JSONL rule from CLAUDE.md). 2 new tests: sacred jsonl survives killAgent + exit < 3.5s when no tmux session to escalate against. 10 pi.test cases pass total. typecheck + lint clean. Force-closed (planning seed inverted depends_on).

title: pan-636: Resume a Pi agent session via stored session id
description:
After PiRuntime spawnAgent succeeds, the extension writes ~/.panopticon/agents/<agentId>/session.id. On resume (e.g., dashboard restart, post-crash recovery), PiRuntime.spawnAgent reads session.id and adds `--session <id>` to the Pi command line. If the file is missing, it spawns a fresh session and logs a warning.
- AC: After a successful initial spawn, ~/.panopticon/agents/<agentId>/session.id contains the Pi session id reported by the extension
- AC: Re-spawning the same agentId after a kill reuses the stored session id via `pi --session <id>`
- AC: When session.id is missing on resume, a fresh session is spawned and a warning is logged but the spawn does not fail
close_reason: session.id persisted by pi-extension; PiRuntime.spawnAgent reads + forwards as resumeSessionId. AC1/AC2/AC3 satisfied. 3 pi.test + 2 pi-extension tests pass.

title: pan-636: src/lib/runtimes/pi.ts implements AgentRuntime for Pi
description:
Create src/lib/runtimes/pi.ts exporting class PiRuntime implements AgentRuntime { name: 'pi' }. Methods: spawnAgent (creates fifo via pi-fifo-ipc, writes launcher.sh via pi-launcher-support, kicks off tmux session, waits up to 30s for ready.json before returning); sendMessage (writes {cmd:'prompt',text} to fifo via writePiCommand, errors with PiNotReady if no ready.json); killAgent (writes {cmd:'abort'} to fifo, waits 2s, then kill -TERM, then kill -KILL after 5s; unlinks fifo); getHeartbeat (reads ~/.panopticon/heartbeats/<agentId>.json, falls back to JSONL mtime + tmux pane activity); getTokenUsage / getSessionCost (delegate to parsePiSession on the agent's session JSONL under <agentDir>/sessions/); getSessionPath; isRunning; listSessions. Register PiRuntime in runtimes/index.ts.
- AC: PiRuntime is registered in getGlobalRegistry() alongside ClaudeCodeRuntime and getRuntime('pi') returns it
- AC: spawnAgent({harness:'pi',...}) creates the fifo, writes the launcher script, starts a tmux session, and resolves only after ready.json is detected (with a 30s timeout that throws a PiSpawnTimeout error)
- AC: sendMessage(agentId, text) writes a single {"cmd":"prompt","text":...} JSONL line to the fifo and resolves after the write completes; sendMessage before ready.json exists rejects with PiNotReady
- AC: getHeartbeat(agentId) returns a Heartbeat sourced from the heartbeat file when fresh (<60s old), falls back to JSONL mtime when stale, falls back to tmux activity when JSONL is missing
- AC: getSessionCost(agentId) returns a CostBreakdown derived from parsePiSession on the agent's active Pi session file
close_reason: Created src/lib/runtimes/pi.ts implementing AgentRuntime (name=pi). Spawn flow: mkdir agent+sessions, createPiFifo, optional prompt file, generateLauncherScript({harness:pi,...}) -> ~/.panopticon/agents/<id>/pi-launcher.sh (0755), createSessionAsync(tmux + env PANOPTICON_AGENT_ID), waitForReady (100ms poll, 30s -> PiSpawnTimeout typed error). sendMessage: throws PiNotReady when ready.json absent, otherwise writes {cmd:prompt,text} via writePiCommand. killAgent: best-effort {cmd:abort} -> killSessionAsync -> destroyPiFifo (full TERM/KILL ladder belongs to bead 8qco). Heartbeat priority: fresh active heartbeat (<60s, high) > jsonl mtime (medium) > tmux session created (low). getSessionCost: CostBreakdown from parsePiSession on latest .jsonl. PiRuntime registered in getGlobalRegistry alongside Claude Code. Widened AgentRuntime.killAgent and isRunning return types to allow async (claude keeps sync; pi async). 9 tests pass. typecheck + lint clean. Force-closed (planning seed inverted depends_on).

description:
Add src/lib/cost-parsers/pi-parser.ts. Read Pi v3 JSONL line by line. Build a Map<id, entry> and a parentId chain. Identify the latest leaf by max(timestamp) among entries with no children. Walk leaf→root via parentId, collecting message/usage/cost entries. Sum usage.input/output/cacheRead. Use entry.usage.cost.total directly as cost_v2 (Pi's inline cost). Map to existing SessionUsage interface from jsonl-parser.ts (do NOT redefine it). Handle compaction entries (subtract pre-compaction input that has been folded into a summary). Handle model_change entries (record model breakdown per segment). Emit a debug log with delta(piInlineCost - localRecomputedCost) for observability. Snapshot fixtures under src/lib/cost-parsers/__tests__/fixtures/pi/.
- AC: parsePiSession(filePath) returns a valid SessionUsage object for a linear (no-fork) Pi v3 JSONL file with correct totals
- AC: For a forked Pi session with two branches, parsePiSession returns totals for ONLY the active branch (latest leaf), not the union of all branches
- AC: For a session with one model_change entry, modelBreakdown contains both models with their respective tokens/cost
- AC: For a session with a compaction entry, input_tokens are NOT double-counted across the compaction boundary
- AC: Unknown event types are logged once per session and do not throw; parser returns whatever it could compute
- AC: cost_v2 equals the sum of entry.usage.cost.total along the active branch (Pi's inline cost is the canonical figure)
close_reason: Created src/lib/cost-parsers/pi-parser.ts: parsePiSession reads Pi v3 JSONL line-by-line, builds id->entry + parent->children index, finds latest leaf among childless entries, walks leaf->root via parentId, sums per-message usage and Pi inline cost.total along active branch into existing SessionUsage shape from jsonl-parser.ts (no redefinition). Pi reports per-call deltas (not cumulative) so summing the branch is correct without subtracting pre-compaction input. cost_v2 = sum of entry.usage.cost.total (Pi inline). Unknown event types deduped + logged via console.debug. Added 5 fixtures (linear, forked, model-change, compaction, unknown-event) and 6 tests covering AC1-5 + missing-file. typecheck + lint clean. Force-closed (planning seed inverted depends_on).

title: pan-636: Per-agent mkfifo named pipe creation and lifecycle
description:
Add helper functions in src/lib/runtimes/pi.ts (or src/lib/runtimes/pi-fifo.ts) to: create the agent dir if missing, mkfifo at ~/.panopticon/agents/<agentId>/rpc.in (chmod 0600), and unlink it on agent kill. Use mkfifoSync from the `fs` module — node has no async mkfifo. The fifo writer side is opened lazily on first write. Adapter must wait for ready.json before opening write-side. NEVER call this from server route handlers; it's only invoked from spawnAgent and killAgent paths which run on dedicated handlers.
- AC: createPiFifo(agentId) creates ~/.panopticon/agents/<agentId>/rpc.in with mode 0600 and is idempotent (unlinks existing fifo first)
- AC: destroyPiFifo(agentId) unlinks the fifo and is safe to call when the fifo does not exist
- AC: writePiCommand(agentId, json) opens the writer fd lazily, writes one JSONL line, and closes — covered by integration test that pre-creates a reader (cat fifo.in > out.log) and asserts the line appears
- AC: writePiCommand returns a typed error (PiNotReady) — and does NOT block — when ready.json is not present yet
close_reason: Created src/lib/runtimes/pi-fifo.ts. createPiFifo uses execAsync(mkfifo -m 600) (Node has no native mkfifo), idempotent — unlinks any existing inode at the path so a stale regular file from a crashed agent is replaced cleanly. destroyPiFifo unlinks, tolerates ENOENT. writePiCommand: checks ready.json existsSync first, throws PiNotReady without blocking when missing (AC4); opens O_WRONLY|O_NONBLOCK so reader-less fifo throws ENXIO -> typed PiNotReady letting adapter recycle the agent. Writes one JSONL line + newline. Integration test uses an O_RDWR Node reader (kept open across writer lifecycles, mirroring how Pi keeps stdin open for the whole session). 8 tests pass: mode 0600, idempotent recreate, stale regular-file replacement, destroy noop, both PiNotReady paths, JSONL round-trip through kernel pipe. typecheck + lint clean. Force-closed (planning seed inverted depends_on).

title: PAN-133: Fix deacon idle/lazy detection false positives
description:
The deacon's idle detection and lazy agent correction features were disabled in commit ed493fa due to false positives.

**Problem:**
- Planning agents and work agents that are actively working appear idle to the detection logic
- This caused false positive interventions on agents that were functioning correctly

**Root Cause (suspected):**
- Detection logic doesn't account for agents waiting on external processes (e.g., Claude API responses)
- May need to distinguish between 'waiting for response' vs 'truly idle'

**Current State:**
- Both features disabled in src/lib/cloister/deacon.ts
- No idle/lazy detection active

**Fix Required:**
- Implement proper activity detection that accounts for agent states
- Consider heartbeat patterns, pending tool calls, or Claude API activity
- Add tests to prevent regression

title: PAN-116: Implement per-message cost calculation in parseClaudeSession()
description:
Replace session-level costing with per-message costing in parseClaudeSession():

1. Initialize modelBreakdown map and totalCostV2 variable
2. In message loop:
   - Extract model ID (exact) and usage for each message
   - Normalize model name for pricing lookup
   - Calculate cost for this message using its model pricing
   - Update modelBreakdown[modelId] with cost/tokens/count
   - Accumulate totalCostV2
3. Generate model display string:
   - Extract normalized model names from breakdown
   - Join with ' → ' if multiple models (e.g., 'claude-sonnet-4.5 → claude-opus-4.5')
4. Keep old cost calculation for backward compatibility
5. Return SessionUsage with cost, cost_v2, and modelBreakdown

title: Conversation DB status stays 'active' after Claude process dies
description:
## Problem

A conversation's DB `status` remains `active` after its Claude process has died.
Observed 2026-06-06: 7 conversations whose Claude had crashed (channels-flag
error on Claude Code 2.1.158) all still reported `status: "active"` from
`GET /api/conversations`, while the actual Claude process was dead and the tmux
session was idling in the launcher keep-alive loop.

This is closely related to the resume-reattaches-to-a-dead-session bug
(discovered-from that investigation): both stem from there being no liveness
signal for "is Claude actually running" beyond "does the tmux session name
exist". Status is set `active` on spawn/resume and never reconciled when Claude
exits unexpectedly.

## Impact
- Dashboard shows dead conversations as live/green.
- No surface tells the user (or the deacon) that the session needs a respawn.

## Fix direction
- A reconciler (deacon patrol or on-read enrichment) should mark a conversation
  not-active when its Claude/pty-supervisor process is no longer running, even
  if the tmux session lingers.
- Ideally share the same liveness check used to fix the resume reattach bug.

## Acceptance
- A conversation whose Claude has exited is no longer reported `status: active`.

title: PAN-140: Investigate CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS for potential Panopticon integration
description:
## Overview
Claude Code v2.1.32+ includes an experimental agent teams feature that enables multi-agent collaboration natively. We should investigate what this offers and whether it can enhance or replace parts of our cloister implementation.

## Investigation Goals
1. **Feature parity analysis**: Compare agent teams capabilities vs our current cloister (work agents, test agents, merge agents, review agents)
2. **Integration opportunities**: Can we leverage this for specialist agents instead of managing tmux ourselves?
3. **Hook events**: Evaluate `TeammateIdle` and `TaskCompleted` events for deacon integration
4. **Sub-agent spawning**: Review the `Task(agent_type)` frontmatter syntax for restricting what agents can spawn

## Key Questions
- Does agent teams handle the orchestration we currently do manually?
- Can it replace our tmux-based agent management?
- What's the token overhead compared to our approach?
- How does memory scope interact with teammate agents?

## Resources
- Enable with: `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`
- Changelog: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
- Related: v2.1.32, v2.1.33 releases

## Deliverables
- [ ] Test agent teams feature hands-on
- [ ] Document capabilities and limitations
- [ ] Compare with current cloister architecture
- [ ] Recommendation: adopt, partially adopt, or continue with cloister
